eighthcourtyards.label: Eighth College / Theatre District Living & Learning Neighborhood — the COURTYARDS AND HARDSCAPE. HKS (design architect) + EYRC Architects with SWA Group (landscape); Kitchell GC; Walter P Moore structure. Construction Jan 2021 - Nov 2023, project complete 2024, the Market Hall (STATION8) still unopened as of Feb 2026. NOT Safdie Rabines and NOT OJB — that team designed North Torrey Pines LLN / Sixth College, and a search on those names documents the wrong buildings.
eighthcourtyards.epoch: 2024-2025 built-condition photography (EYRC/Lawrence Anderson phf01-phf49; SWA Group gallery 1-23) over a 2025-03 built-condition site plan (SDAF OH! San Diego), over the repo's ArcGIS facilities survey. THE 2014 LiDAR IS BLIND HERE: the college was a parking lot in 2014, campus-lidar.json massHeights has no entry for any Eighth mass, and campus-massing.js:16 records that LiDAR measures Sankofa at parking-lot height. Every argument of the form 'the LiDAR is smooth here so there is no step or wall' is therefore VOID over Eighth — it describes a demolished car park. That argument is what campus-eighth.js and campus-eighth-furniture.js used to withhold every stair, terrace, retaining wall and seat wall; this section re-decides it on eleven dated 2024-25 photographs. Google satellite over Eighth is MID-CONSTRUCTION and is never an existence or colour source. The 2021 Revelle town-hall deck is the DESIGN epoch and is superseded wherever it disagrees with the built photographs (its rooftop PV fields and its figure-of-eight meditation pavilion were not built).
eighthcourtyards.note: INVENTED class — photo-sourced detail (README 'the second declared invented class'), quarantined in campus-photo-detail.json. Nothing measured may read from it. Photographs decide what exists and how it looks; the ArcGIS survey keeps deciding every ground EXTENT. Items labelled [estimated] are the third declared tier: each names the sourced pattern it extends and is replaced the day a real source appears. Textures are code-generated by campus-materials.js; sourced colours feed the materials.
eighthcourtyards.boundsNote: x -220..30, z 490..730. The shipped `eighth` section's bounds (x -220..-40, z 500..640) exclude the whole southern third of the college — Market Hall Plaza (walk #3045 runs to z 724.6 and x +26.0), The Backyard (#323 z 651.5, #114 z 654.5), Theatre Walk, the Theatre Drop-Off, the South Parking Entrance, the Loading Dock, the Survivance Front Porch, the mid-site parking-elevator pavilion and the mobility hub. This section's bounds are the corrected envelope. CORRECTED 2026-08-19: these bounds are the college ENVELOPE and they stay as they are — Market Hall Plaza (arcgis.ground#3045, to z 724.6 and x +26.0) really is inside the college and the shipped eighth.bounds really do truncate it. What was wrong was using the envelope to crop the PAVING: arcgis.ground[3632] is the campus-wide walk layer, so the envelope alone let 1,929 m2 of Keeling, Galbraith and Revelle approach take Eighth photographed paver blend. The paving now carries its own measured.paving.collegeClip, whose two edges are survey vertices. Note that #3045 itself contributes no span to the paving table at all — it is a separate walk polygon — so it never justified the eastern reach of the paving crop in the first place.

sources.what: SWA Group (landscape architect) project page + 19-image gallery on swacdn.s3.amazonaws.com, UCSD_UC-San-Diego_Theater-District_Living-Learning-<N>.webp for N in 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,12,13,14,16,17,18,20,21,22,23. The landscape authority.

San Diego Architectural Foundation OH! San Diego tour map — a north-up, labelled, BUILT-condition site plan. Source of every named outdoor space and, georegistered on the surveyed basketball court, of the Meditation Pavilion and Tea House positions.

UCSD Revelle College town-hall deck. Slide 6 is the DESIGN site plan (BLDG 1-5, storey counts, MEDITATION PAVILION, TEA HOUSE, two PARKING ELEVATORs). DESIGN EPOCH — superseded by the built photographs wherever they disagree.
The facade-geometry text: windows popped out and rotated SIX DEGREES on the lower towers for +30% airflow, fins on the taller sections; LEED v4 Platinum achieved.
Structural engineer: four-level SUBTERRANEAN parking connected to only three towers, ~1,200 spaces, 10.9-acre site, post-tensioned slabs, exposed concrete finishes.
The university's own per-building program and the phrase 'Eighth College Plaza: grills, Zen Garden, Meditation Pavilion'.
19 new classrooms, a 150-seat lecture hall, market hall, conference centre, one-mile walking trail, enhanced valet/drop-off.

2022 California Building Code — 1013.2 guard height 42 in / 1.067 m and the 4 in sphere rule; 11B-505.4 handrail 34-38 in; 1011.5 riser <= 7 in and tread >= 11 in; 11B-405 ramp 1:12 max. Used ONLY as a BOUND on figures the photographs cannot separate, never as a measurement.

The UCSD facilities ArcGIS survey shipped in this repo. ground[3632] is the paved extent; ground[]#NNNN are the named beds, lawns and the court; massing[] are the building footprints. Ring coordinates are DECIMETRES — every figure here is /10 into local metres.
The WS-E1/WS-E2 measurement dossier — 74 ground features, each registered to an arcgis.ground[] ring and already in local metres.

georegistration.what: A transform from the 2025 BUILT-condition SDAF site plan into repo world metres, established on the surveyed basketball court.
georegistration.plan: sdaf-plan rendered at 400 dpi to 3400 x 4400 px
georegistration.derivation: Court baselines at px x 902 and 1140 (238 px = the surveyed 22.7 m -> 10.48 px/m); sidelines at px y 927 and 1085 (158 px = the surveyed 15.4 m -> 10.26 px/m). The centre line falls at px x 1021, the exact midpoint — an independent check. The two scales agree to 2%, so there is no rotation between plan and world.
georegistration.verification: Overlaid on the drawn footprints of Sankofa, Podemos, Azad and Pulse — all land within a few metres.
georegistration.products: The Meditation Pavilion box and the Tea House box below are its two products.

paving.what: The measured paved extent of the whole college. arcgis.ground[3632] is a single k:"walk" multipolygon: ONE outer ring and 213 holes that punch out every planting bed, lawn, garden island and the basketball court. Building the paving as outer-minus-holes guarantees paving and beds cannot overlap and that no plate outline is invented.

subtractedMassing.why: ground[3632]'s holes do NOT punch out the buildings — 1,645 m2 of the walk layer runs under the TDLLN masses. Every campus-arcgis massing ring whose bbox meets these bounds is therefore cut out of the spans as well, with a 0.15 m keep-off, so no paver decal passes under a wall.

paving.method: Exact scanline: at each row centre z the outer ring edge crossings are paired into spans and clipped to the envelope AND to collegeClip.x1; rows north of collegeClip.z0 are dropped whole; then every hole, every massing ring (with clearance) and every carried survey ring is subtracted — sampled at BOTH ROW EDGES as well as the centre and unioned, so a strip is cut wherever any part of it overlaps rather than only where its centre line does. Spans shorter than minSpan are dropped as survey slivers. Rounded to 3 decimal places, which is the form shipped below; the test re-derives the whole table from campus-arcgis.json and campus-eighth.json and compares it entry for entry.

collegeClip.why: arcgis.ground[3632] is the CAMPUS-WIDE walk layer, not an Eighth feature: it runs x -223..235, z -186..702. Cropping it to this section bounds still left 1,929 m2 of it — 19.7% of the field — outside Eighth College, and painted it with Eighth photographed P1/P2 blend. That is photo-sourced APPEARANCE applied to ground the photographs never covered, which is the same overreach as reading a height off the wrong epoch. Both edges below are survey vertices, so nothing here is typed.
collegeClip.z0Source: z >= 499.6 is the NORTH face of arcgis.massing[252] (TDLLN - Podemos), the northernmost of the ten TDLLN masses. North of it the walk layer serves Charles David Keeling Apartments 2 (massing[329], z 421.5..497.6) and Galbraith Hall (massing[0], z 428.6..491.7), neither of which any frame in this section source set covers. 1,305 m2 removed.
collegeClip.x1Source: x <= -24.3 is the EAST face of arcgis.massing[253] (TDLLN - Podemos tower), the easternmost of the ten TDLLN masses. Every span east of it lies in z 480..540 — the Galbraith / Revelle approach — and none of it is Market Hall Plaza: the Plaza is arcgis.ground#3045 (x -73.2..26.0, z 605.3..724.6), a SEPARATE walk polygon that contributes no span to this table at all. 624 m2 removed. The bounds keep their eastern reach because Market Hall Plaza really is inside the college and the shipped eighth.bounds really do truncate it; it is the PAVING that must not run there.
collegeClip.removedNote: Declared, not silently dropped — see absent.

subtractedRings.why: arcgis.ground[3632] own 213 holes punch out MOST beds, but not the ten campus-eighth.json bed rings and six named survey rings this section carries and draws on. Round one cut the spans by the holes and the massing only, so about 12 m2 of paving was drawn INSIDE surveyed planting beds, coplanar with the mulch and the gravel on the same `carpet` rung — two decals fighting for the same pixel. Every ring this section renders anything on is now subtracted as well, at the same three-probe row quantisation.
subtractedRings.excluded: pavilionSlabWest (arcgis.ground#2374) is NOT subtracted: it is the PAVED apron of the north parking-elevator pavilion, hardscape rather than planting, and the pavilion stands on it.

paving.surveyAreaNote: The full arcgis.ground[3632] scanline inside `bounds`, BEFORE the college clip and the carried-ring subtraction: 9,784.995 m2 in 1,342 spans. Kept as the record of what the survey layer gives here, so the two subtractions below are auditable subtractions and not a quietly smaller number.

keepOut.what: Every campus-arcgis massing ring inside these bounds, carried verbatim so the module can cut buildings out of the SURVEYED BED fills as well as out of the paving. The green survey layer does not agree with the massing layer: arcgis.ground#2703, a courtyard ring, runs 20 m under the drawn Sankofa Base. The survey is the authority on a bed's extent and the massing is the authority on where a building stands, so where they overlap the building wins and the bed is cut.

rings.name: Joan and Irwin Jacobs Center for La Jolla Playhouse

notDrawn.what: Every numeric figure this section RECORDS but does not draw, and why. The rule this list exists to enforce: a measurement either drives geometry or is named here with the reason it cannot. A number sitting in the data driving nothing, unremarked, is the defect. The test enumerates every numeric leaf in the section and fails on any key name the module never reads that is also missing from this list.

keys.paving.families.*.thickness: The paver / slab thickness. The paving is a ground DECAL on the overlay ladder, not a solid, so a thickness has nothing to drive. P1 0.057 m is itself [estimated] (the paver edge is never visible in any frame; 2.25 in is the standard for the class); P4 0.15 m likewise. Recorded so a future section that builds a kerb reveal or a step nosing against the paving has the figure.
keys.paving.families.P1.lengths: The four observed plank lengths, 0.20 / 0.30 / 0.40 / 0.60 m, read as 2x / 3x / 4x / 6x the measured 0.089 m width in EYRC phf03. The library unit-grid class draws one repeating cell size and cannot lay random lengths, so unit[1] carries the MODAL 0.30 m and this array records what was actually seen. Drawing it would need a per-unit geometry pass, which is a different and much more expensive object than a decal.
keys.paving.families.P4.unit: The 1.5 m score panel. Measured, and deliberately not drawn — see absent, the library joint would be 11x the measured sawcut. It still drives P4.tile as the noise scale.
keys.court.tileModule: 0.305 m, the modular sport-tile module. campus-eighth-court.js owns the court SURFACE (see court.surfaceNote); this section changes only its colours, so nothing here can draw a tile grid. [estimated] anyway — the grid is visible in SWA -16 but never against a scale bar.
keys.levelChange.retaining.chamfer: 0.02 m arris chamfer on the cast-in-place retaining wall. The wall is drawn as a scaled box and a 20 mm chamfer is below the geometry this module builds; adding it would cost a bespoke extrusion per run for a detail smaller than the wall own segmentation error. Recorded from SWA -5.
keys.levelChange.stairs.*.nosing: 0.00 m. The photographed flight has a square nosing with no projection, which is why the figure is zero; it is recorded so that a later flight with a real nosing is not silently given this one geometry.
keys.lawns.mown: 0.06 m mown turf height. The Sun Lawn is a ground decal on the carpet rung, so there is no blade geometry to give a height to. Recorded from SWA -4.
keys.lawns.panels.*.areaM2: 351.6 m2. Not drawn — but not dead either: the test re-derives it by shoelace from the surveyed ring and fails if the two disagree, which is what makes the ring verbatim claim checkable at the panel level rather than only at the ring level.
keys.lawns.syntheticWithheld.*: The Social 10 x 6 m synthetic turf panel, its 0.03 m pile and 0.30 m edge band. Sourced and deliberately NOT built: no measured paved run in The Social accepts a 10 x 6 m footprint without overrunning a surveyed bed, and shrinking a sourced dimension to make it fit would be inventing a measurement. See absent.
keys.levelChange.seatWalls.courseHeight: NOW DRAWN. 0.203 m course and 0.406 m unit drive the CMU texture repeat on the seat wall so the coursing renders at true scale; listed here only to record that round one left both figures unread.
keys.court.apron.width: 2.45 m, the surveyed apron run east of the court. The zone rectangle is grown by court.apron.reach (5.48 m, the widest surveyed adjacent run) instead, so this figure is the corroborating measurement rather than the driver.

paving.rungNote: campus-eighth.js repaints the surveyed ground features on the `pad` rung. This field paints the same ground in its photographed paving families on the rung ABOVE it, so the two never z-fight and the older repaint remains the fallback if this module fails to load. Lifts and depth state come from campus-overlay.js; this module defines no lift of its own.

P1.label: narrow linear plank paver, warm blend — Scholars Cloister, academic-wing forecourt, Ridge Walk terrace
P1.unitNote: Unit WIDTH 0.089 m +/- 0.010 — nearest catalogue unit is the 4 in nominal / 98 mm actual narrow modular paver. Derivation: in EYRC phf03 (1799x1200) the man walking a bicycle spans 147.5 px (head y 855 -> feet y 1002); at 1.75 m that is 84.3 px/m at his foot depth, and the paving course pitch measured at the same depth is 7.5 px -> 0.089 m. Random lengths in the same field read as 2x, 3x, 4x and 6x the width, i.e. 0.20 / 0.30 / 0.40 / 0.60 m; 0.30 m is the modal length carried here.
P1.thicknessNote: [estimated] — the paver edge is never visible; 0.057 m (2.25 in) is the standard thickness for this class. Nothing is drawn from it; it is recorded so a future drawing can correct it.
P1.tileNote: tile = unit x 6 = 0.534 x 1.8 m, because one pavingConcreteUnit texture tile is a 6 x 6 grid of units. Anisotropic, so the measured 0.089 x 0.3 m unit renders at its measured aspect.

P2.label: 2:1 rectangular paver, warm buff blend — the courtyards, The Social, the tower loggias, the Bamboo Garden surround. The dominant courtyard surface.
P2.unitNote: 0.315 x 0.157 m (12 x 6 in nominal, 305 x 152 mm). Derivation: in SWA -17 two walkers 1.70 m tall span 405 px (head y 430 -> feet y 835) -> 238 px/m at their foot depth; joints at that depth fall at 150 px pitch on the long axis and 75 px on the short -> 0.315 x 0.157 m. Cross-check: a 0.26 m sneaker in the same frame spans 140 px -> 538 px/m upper bound, consistent. Half-lap offset 0.157 m.
P2.tileNote: tile = unit x 6 = 1.89 x 0.942 m, because one pavingConcreteUnit texture tile is a 6 x 6 grid of units. Anisotropic, so the measured 0.315 x 0.157 m unit renders at its measured aspect.

P3.label: small 2:1 mosaic, cool grey blend — the Ramble courtyard fields
P3.unitNote: About 0.20 x 0.10 m (2:1), read off the near-overhead SWA -12 where the unit aspect is unambiguous and the field runs continuous with the P2 field whose module is measured at 0.315 x 0.157 m. THE 'MOSAIC' IS THE COLOUR BLEND, NOT THE UNIT SHAPE — three to four greys laid checkerboard-random. That is the correction of record against campus-eighth.js's 'angular concrete plate mosaic', which assumed large irregular plates and shipped a 30-degree scoring as its weak form for want of per-plate geometry: there are no plates.
P3.tileNote: tile = unit x 6 = 1.2 x 0.6 m, because one pavingConcreteUnit texture tile is a 6 x 6 grid of units. Anisotropic, so the measured 0.2 x 0.1 m unit renders at its measured aspect.

P4.label: cast-in-place concrete in large scored panels — Market Hall Plaza, Theatre Walk, the basketball-court apron
P4.unitNote: Score-joint grid about 1.5 m, read against a 1.75 m walker in EYRC phf19 whose height spans 118 px at the panel depth. Joint width about 0.006 m sawcut. Warm buff integral colour, sandblast / light broom finish.
P4.tileNote: [estimated] extends P4.unit, the MEASURED 1.5 m score panel. smoothConcrete has NO unit grid, so no x6 factor applies and this is a noise scale: setting it to the measured panel makes the cast-concrete surface variation read at panel scale, but it is a choice of scale and not a measurement OF the noise, so it takes the estimated tier. The score grid itself is NOT drawn: see absent. campus-materials.js FIELDS.pavingConcreteUnit would draw its joint at a fixed 4.5% of the cell, i.e. 0.0675 m at a 1.5 m panel against the measured 0.006 m sawcut, and an 11x joint is a worse statement than no joint.

DG.label: stabilised decomposed granite — the Ramble's meandering paths
DG.unitNote: Main path 3.0-3.3 m wide (510 px across at 157 px/m from a 1.78 m walker in SWA -8), secondary loops 1.8-2.4 m; DG depth to the check-step riser 0.15-0.18 m. Not a unit product — `unit` here is only the texture tile.
DG.tileNote: [estimated] extends nothing measured — decomposedGranite is a NOISE class with no unit grid, so its tile is a grit scale and not a product dimension. 2.5 m is the scale at which the library grit reads as walked-flat DG at eye height; no frame in the set resolves a DG grain against a scale bar. Recorded as estimated rather than stamped measured.

paving.zoneNote: [estimated] — WHICH blend covers WHICH field is photo-inferred. The zones below are read off the frames listed against each; the survey does not record paving material, and no paving schedule is published. The first zone a span's centre falls in wins; anything unclaimed takes the default P2. Zone boundaries are deliberately rectangles: the real field boundaries are angular chevrons (SWA -12 shows five re-entrants at an included angle of 110-130 degrees, deviating 25-35 degrees from the building grid), and inventing chevron outlines would be exactly the invented plate geometry this section exists to retire.

zones.source: eyrc phf03; swa -7 — the academic-wing forecourt and the Ridge Walk terrace

[measured] DERIVED, not typed: measured.court.rect (arcgis.ground#3898, the surveyed court) grown by court.apron.reach = 5.48 m, the widest paved run adjacent to the court in the shipped span table. SWA -16 shows the cast-concrete apron on all four sides.
eyrc phf19 — Market Hall Plaza and Theatre Walk (arcgis.ground#3045, #4073)
swa -8, -9, -6, -22 — the Ramble corridor between the surveyed swale beds
swa -12, -2 — the four principal fields between Pulse, Sankofa Mid, Azad and the Ramble

paving.tileRule: A texture tile is NOT one paving unit. campus-materials.js FIELDS.pavingConcreteUnit lays COLS = 6 by ROWS = 6 units inside one tile (campus-materials.js:175), so a family whose material is pavingConcreteUnit must carry tile = unit x 6 on BOTH axes, and the strip mesh must lay uv = (x / tile[0], z / tile[1]) so a 2:1 unit renders 2:1 and not square. Round one set tile to the unit itself and rendered every paver at one sixth of its measured size — the 0.315 m P2 unit drew at 52 mm. campus-photo-galbraith.js:1015 (paverPitch * 6) and campus-photo-keeling.js:1028 (7.2 = 1.2 * 6) are the shipped precedent. Classes with no unit grid (decomposedGranite, smoothConcrete) take no factor: their tile is a NOISE scale, tiered [estimated], not a product dimension.

edging.label: flush dark steel bed edging
edging.source: swa -17, -13, -12 — a dark flat edge strip set flush with the paver top at every bed boundary
edging.note: Run along every segment of every ring named in `rings`, verbatim from the survey, so the edging is SURVEYED geometry and not a traced line; its length is therefore a measured figure the module reports. Each ring says WHY it takes an edge, because an edge is a claim about a boundary. A segment whose midpoint falls inside a drawn massing ring is dropped: a bed edge running under a building is a survey/massing conflict, not an edge. `measured.rings.teaHouseIsland` and `measured.rings.pavilionSlabWest` are carried for CLIPPING only and are NOT in this list — the Tea House island is eighthgathering's ground and the pavilion slab is paved, so neither is a bed boundary this section may assert.

gardenBands.label: the same edging used decoratively as parallel bands through the Bamboo Garden's raked gravel
gardenBands.source: swa -3, -21 — about eight bands counted across the garden island, dividing the gravel into 3-4 m panels
gardenBands.pitchNote: DERIVED, not measured: the module spreads the COUNTED 8 bands evenly across the surveyed island, so the pitch is a consequence of the count and the island, never an independent claim. Island z extent 29.80 m (arcgis.ground[3632] hole ring 193) / (8 + 1) = 3.311 m. Round one declared 3.5 m alongside the count and the module honoured only the count, so the two disagreed by 6% with nothing to catch it. The photographed 3-4 m panel width is what corroborates the count.

rings.why: arcgis.ground#2369, the Sun Lawn. This section lays turf inside it, so its whole boundary is a turf/paving edge — the exact condition SWA -17, -13 and -12 photograph a flush steel strip at.

arcgis.ground#1160. THE SURFACE IS WITHHELD AND THE BOUNDARY IS NOT — see absent[21]. What #1160 cannot resolve is the internal edge between its mown west/centre lobe and its decomposed-granite east arm, so no DECAL may cover it; its OUTER 54-vertex ring is a surveyed boundary between a planted ring and the paved field either way, and both readings of the inside are bed surfaces that the same photographed detail edges. The edge asserts nothing about which surface is behind it. Segments that run under a drawn mass are cut by the massing keep-out like every other ring's.
arcgis.ground[3632] hole ring 193, the Bamboo Garden island. This section lays its raked gravel inside it, so its boundary is a gravel/paving edge.
arcgis.ground#1761, the clipped hedge strip on the court's north side. This section plants it, so its boundary is a planting/paving edge.
arcgis.ground#2144, the clipped hedge strip on the court's east side, as courtHedgeNorth.

the ten campus-eighth.json bed rings this section carries. eighthramble plants them; this section neither plants nor paves inside them, and it subtracts every one of them from its own paving — so their boundary is a bed/paving edge in the shipped document whichever section fills them.

levelChange.epochNote: THIS BLOCK EXISTS TO RETIRE A DEAD-EPOCH WITHHOLDING. campus-eighth.js omits every stair, terrace, retaining and seat wall on the ground that 'the 2014 LiDAR under the courtyard is smooth to 1.5% over 150 m with no step anywhere, so there is no built grade for a flight to descend or a wall to retain'. The 2014 LiDAR is describing a demolished parking lot: it cannot see a college built in 2021-2023. Eleven 2024-25 photographs resolve stair flights, tan retaining walls, buff CMU seat walls, stepped LED-lit seat terraces, an accessible ramp and a bridge. Existence is settled. POSITION is the remaining problem, and it is settled only where the survey or the georegistered 2025 plan reaches: what is anchored is built, what is not is in `absent` with the reason.

handrail.label: brushed stainless round tube on stainless posts, full horizontal returns top and bottom
handrail.source: eyrc phf03 — a rail post at orig (985,920) rises 70 px to the rail at 0.90 m -> 78 px/m at that station, consistent with the 93 px/m read further up the flight from the 1.75 m man. Height bounded by CBC 11B-505.4 (0.864-0.965 m).
handrail.specOwnerNote: THE RAIL SPEC IS NOT THIS SECTION'S. 0.90 m to the gripping surface, 0.042 m (1 1/4 in Sch.40) tube, 0.038 m intermediate baluster, a 1.55 m post pitch and a 0.305 m (12 in) extension are the canonical Eighth values arbitrated 2026-08-19 and owned by eighthsiteworks.systems.handrail. This section's 0.90 m height WON that arbitration — it was re-measured off phf03 at 0.896 m against a fitted ground plane, against the 0.87 m code minimum the other section had assumed. What this section owns is the FLIGHT: S1, 15 risers counted in phf03 with its step-light positions. The rail is placed on the flight because a rail without its stair hovers. POST PITCH CORRECTED 2026-08-19: this section carried 1.35 m with no derivation of any kind and the arbitration's `unresolved` named it — 'eighthcourtyards says 1.35 m with no derivation ... I left 1.55 standing as the only value with any derivation'. 1.55 m is now carried from the spec owner with that derivation, and the figure is enumerated above so a value outside the owner's list cannot sit here unremarked again.

figures.tube: [measured] 0.042 m. 1 1/4 in Sch.40, OD 42.2 mm — a named product step, not a round number. eighthsiteworks re-measured the phf03 return at 4.6 px against 106 px/m = 0.043 m; ADA 505.7.1 bounds a circular gripping surface at 32-51 mm. Owned by eighthsiteworks.systems.handrail.tube.diameter.
figures.height: [measured] 0.90 m to the gripping surface. phf03: a rail post at orig (985,920) rises 70 px to the rail at 78 px/m at that station, consistent with the 93 px/m read further up the flight from the 1.75 m man; eighthsiteworks' independent re-measurement against a fitted ground plane gives 0.896 m. Bounded by CBC 11B-505.4 (0.864-0.965 m). THIS SECTION'S VALUE WON the 2026-08-19 arbitration against a 0.87 m code-minimum assumption.
figures.post: [measured] 0.038 m. The intermediate baluster diameter, owned by eighthsiteworks.systems.handrail.post.diameter and carried verbatim.
figures.postSpacing: [estimated] 1.55 m, CARRIED FROM THE SPEC OWNER eighthsiteworks.systems.handrail.post.pitch, which derives it: 'phf03 reads 4 (possibly 5) posts over a ~7 m oblique run, 1.4-1.7 m; 1.55 is the middle'. It extends that read. This section's own 1.35 m had no derivation at all and is retired.
figures.returnLength: [measured] 0.305 m. The 12 in horizontal extension CBC 11B-505.10.2 requires beyond the bottom riser, and 0.305 m is its exact metric equivalent. Owned by eighthsiteworks.systems.handrail.

guard.label: hot-dip galvanised guard: vertical round pickets between a round top rail and a lower rail, on posts
guard.source: swa -5 — a walker 1.70 m tall spans 185 px (head y 385 -> feet y 570) -> 109 px/m; the rail top is 115 px above the deck at her station -> 1.06 m, and CBC 1013.2's 42 in = 1.067 m agrees. 30 pickets counted over 300 px -> 0.092 m pitch, dia 0.016 m -> clear opening 0.076 m, inside the 4 in sphere rule.
guard.specOwnerNote: THE GUARD SPEC IS NOT THIS SECTION'S. 1.067 m, 0.019 m picket at 0.1016 m centres, 0.048 m top rail and 0.033 m lower rail are the canonical Eighth values arbitrated 2026-08-19 and owned by eighthsiteworks.systems.guardrail, which is the only section that models the raised kerb a guard is fixed to rather than fixing it to the walking surface. This section applies them to the level changes it owns and nowhere else. Its own earlier reads (0.092 m pitch counted at ~2 px a picket on a 0.6x copy, and a 0.016 m picket) are retired. TWO FIGURES DERIVED HERE 2026-08-19, because the spec owner carries no post spec at all and this section was typing round numbers into the gap: `post` was 0.05 m and `postSpacing` was 2.4 m, neither derived from anything, and together they placed 22 guard posts. Both are now consequences of the members that WERE measured — see `figures`. `lowerRailHeight` was 0.10 m for the same reason and is now the same 4 in module as the picket pitch.

figures.height: [measured] 1.067 m (42 in). SWA -5: a 1.70 m walker spans 185 px (head y 385 -> feet y 570) = 109 px/m, and the rail top is 115 px above the deck at her station = 1.06 m; CBC 1015.3's 42 in = 1.067 m is the exact figure that read brackets, and four independent photographic reads across the sibling sections (1.06, 1.066, 1.067, 1.07) bracket it too. Owned by eighthsiteworks.systems.guardrail.
figures.picketPitch: [measured] 0.1016 m — 4 in exactly, the arbitrated Eighth value owned by eighthsiteworks.systems.guardrail. This section's own earlier 0.092 m was counted at about 2 px a picket on a 0.6x copy and is retired.
figures.picketDia: [measured] 0.019 m — 3/4 in round bar, the arbitrated value. This section's earlier 0.016 m is retired.
figures.topRail: [measured] 0.048 m — 1 1/2 in Sch.40, OD 1.900 in = 0.04826 m. A named product step. Owned by eighthsiteworks.systems.guardrail.
figures.lowerRail: [measured] 0.033 m — 1 in Sch.40, OD 1.315 in = 0.03340 m. A named product step. Owned by eighthsiteworks.systems.guardrail.
figures.lowerRailHeight: [derived] 0.1016 m to the lower rail's axis. NOT a free figure: the clear opening beneath the bottom rail is governed by the same 4 in (0.1016 m) sphere rule that fixes the picket pitch, and at an axis height of one 4 in module the clear opening under a 0.033 m rail is 0.1016 - 0.0165 = 0.085 m, inside the rule with margin. It is therefore the picket module itself, not an independent claim. The 0.10 m carried until 2026-08-19 was that same number rounded, and rounded to a value the module grid does not contain.
figures.post: [estimated] 0.0603 m. EXTENDS THE GUARD'S OWN MEASURED PIPE SCHEDULE: the three members that ARE measured are exactly 3/4 in round bar (0.019), 1 in Sch.40 (OD 1.315 in = 0.033) and 1 1/2 in Sch.40 (OD 1.900 in = 0.048), so the assembly is a standard Sch.40 pipe-and-picket guard. A post cannot be a lighter section than the top rail it carries, so it takes the next size in that same schedule — 2 in Sch.40, OD 2.375 in = 0.06033 m. No frame in the set resolves the post's own diameter; SWA -5 is the only frame that reads the guard at all and at 109 px/m a post images about 6 px. The 0.05 m carried until 2026-08-19 is not a size in any pipe schedule and was typed, not read.
figures.postSpacing: [estimated] 2.4384 m. EXTENDS THE MEASURED PICKET MODULE: pickets are at 0.1016 m (4 in) centres, a shop-fabricated picket panel spans a whole number of those bays, and 24 bays is 2.4384 m = 8 ft, the standard fabricated panel length. No frame resolves the post stations — SWA -5 shows the guard obliquely and the picket run it does resolve is not bounded by two visible posts — so the panel length is estimated and the MODULE it must land on is measured. The 2.4 m carried until 2026-08-19 was 8 ft rounded to two figures, which is 23.6 picket bays: every post after the first landed mid-bay, which is the one thing a fabricated panel cannot do.

retaining.label: W1 — tan integral-colour cast-in-place, smooth form finish, chamfered top arris, flush cope
retaining.source: swa -5, -6, -16, -14, -18, -2; eyrc phf19. Height 0.9-1.6 m where retaining, 0.45 m where doubling as a seat; the wall behind the basketball court measures 1.2-1.5 m (people standing in front of it in SWA -16 give 70 px/m and the wall top is 108 px above their feet). Cope thickness 0.30-0.40 m.

runs.source: swa -16 — the tan wall behind the basketball court, with a picket guard on top and a clipped hedge row in front of it. ANCHORED: its line is the north edge of the surveyed hedge strip arcgis.ground#1761 (x -188.0..-161.2, z 514.3..515.3), which is 26.8 m long and 1.0 m deep and lies exactly along the court's north side. Height 1.35 m is the midpoint of the measured 1.2-1.5 m.

retaining.withheldNote: About 260 m of W1 run is visible across SWA -2, -5, -6, -16 and phf19. Only the 26.8 m the survey anchors is built; the rest is in `absent`.

seatWalls.label: W2 — buff ground-face (burnished) architectural CMU in running bond under a smooth cast-stone cap
seatWalls.source: swa -18 — five courses span 180 px where a 1.78 m standing man spans 290 px -> 163 px/m -> 0.221 m per course including a 10 mm joint, i.e. a nominal 203 mm (8 in) unit; the face reads 2:1 -> a 406 mm (16 in) unit. Seat walls 0.45 m high x 0.40 m thick with a 0.06 m cap projecting 0.02 m. Also eyrc phf03 (the block the man sits on) and swa -14, -17, -16.

runs.source: [estimated] extends the measured W2 coursing across the court's north hedge strip: SWA -16 shows a buff block wall about 22 m long behind the court, but the frame cannot separate it from the tan W1 behind. Anchored to the south edge of arcgis.ground#1761.

planterWalls.label: W3 — smooth bone-white precast raised planters with a flat cap, holding clipped columnar shrubs
planterWalls.source: swa -18 and -14 — read against the 1.78 m standing man at 163 px/m: the planter top is 147 px above the paving -> 0.90 m. Six visible at The Social. A different, paler and smoother family than W1 and W2.
planterWalls.positionNote: [estimated] position — the count is sourced, the individual positions are not. Scattered deterministically on measured paved spans inside The Social's surveyed paved extent.

terraces.label: the raised academic-entry terrace the S1 flight serves
terraces.source: [estimated] position — EYRC phf03 photographs a full straight flight of 15 risers with stainless handrails, a folded dark-grey metal cheek and a buff CMU seat wall at the 9185 address on the Ridge Walk face of the Podemos academic wing (arcgis.massing[252], x -82.6..-25.2, z 499.6..555.3). The flight EXISTS and its rise is counted; where along a 55 m elevation the address plate sits is not resolved by any frame or plan. The 5.0 x 7.0 m landing is placed by the same stated rule the rest of this section uses: the position CLOSEST to the drawn academic wing (arcgis.massing[252]) at which the whole landing stands on MEASURED paved spans, is clear of every massing ring, and leaves the 4.95 m flight a clear run — searched on a 0.5 m grid over the whole north-east quarter. That is [-68.0, 500.0], 2.8 m off the wing's ring, on 100% measured paving. It lands on the wing's WEST elevation rather than the Ridge Walk face because the survey carries no paved ground against the east face inside the wing's extent; that is a statement about the survey, not a claim about the address. The flight descends from the landing, so nothing floats — replace the moment a drawing gives the address position. Extends the sourced pattern of the same photograph.

stairs.label: Scholars Cloister / academic-wing main stair
stairs.source: eyrc phf03 — 15 risers COUNTED, nosings at orig y 745, 763, 782, 802, 823, 845, 868, 893, 920, 948, 978, 1010, 1045, 1082 with two more above. Flight width about 5.5 m from the 1.75 m man on the flight at 93 px/m. Recessed riser step-lights 0.24 x 0.11 m (22 x 10 px at 93 px/m), TWO per lit riser 1.0 m apart (95 px), on ALTERNATE risers. Riser and tread cannot be separated from the projected step spacing without the camera geometry: they are BOUNDED by CBC 1011.5 (riser <= 0.178 m, tread >= 0.279 m) and the observed proportion gives 0.17 / 0.33 m, total rise 2.55 m. [estimated] on riser/tread only — it extends nothing but the code bound.

stairs.label: the decomposed-granite path check-step — a single riser laid across the path as a grade break
stairs.source: [estimated] position — SWA -6/-8 show a single full-width riser across the DG path. Its position along the Ramble is not resolved; it is laid across the widest measured DG span nearest the Ramble zone's centre, so it spans a real surveyed path and cannot float. Riser 0.15-0.18 m measured against the DG depth; 0.165 m is the midpoint.

seatTerraces.label: the stepped LED-lit seat terrace on the Bamboo Garden's north side
seatTerraces.source: eyrc phf48 and swa -21, -20 — two to three tiers of tan concrete seat steps, each carrying a CONTINUOUS recessed LED strip under the nosing; this is what makes the garden read as glowing lines at dusk. Riser 0.45 m confirmed by people sitting on it in phf48; tread 0.75 m and run about 18 m; in SWA -21 seated figures give 141 px/m and the tier face measures 63 px. The LED channel is built as a recessed dark reveal only: NO luminous state is drawn, because this project has no night source (campus-photo-keeling.js takes the same position on its lamps).
seatTerraces.positionNote: ANCHORED to the surveyed Bamboo Garden island (arcgis.ground[3632] hole ring 193, x -189.7..-158.8, z 573.0..602.8) AND REJECTED OUT OF THE MEDITATION PAVILION. RE-SOLVED 2026-08-19: the earlier station [-175.0, 585.0] put this 18.0 x 1.5 m run at x -184.0..-166.0, z 584.25..585.75 — 12.9 m of it inside eighthgathering's `meditation.deck` (x -181.3..-168.4, z 584.85..591.05, 0.45 m solid on the same ground) and under its roof rect. The rule that produced it optimised for the island alone and never excluded the pavilion, so it landed on top of it. THE RULE NOW: reject any station unless the whole 18.0 x 1.5 m footprint lies inside the surveyed island AND clears `bambooGarden.pavilionClip.rect` by at least `pavilionClip.clearance`; among the accepted stations on a 0.05 m grid take the one whose south face is CLOSEST to the pavilion's north edge, tie-broken toward the pavilion's own centre line. That is [-180.35, 583.20] — footprint x -189.35..-171.35, z 582.45..583.95, 0.05 m clear of the pavilion's north edge, wholly inside the island's west lobe (which runs x -189.5..-171.3 through this z band, giving 0.2 m to spare on an 18.0 m run), and 5.64 m from the station the photograph was read at. The run is still on the garden's north side, which is what phf48 and SWA -21, -20 show. Every tier is provably inside the island and provably outside the pavilion, and the test asserts both.

seatTerraces.label: the stepped seat terrace at The Social, against the public-art wall
seatTerraces.source: [estimated] position — SWA -18 and -14 photograph three tiers of wide tan concrete seat steps used as informal amphitheatre seating, with eight students sitting on them; riser about 0.42 m, tread about 0.90 m, run about 9 m, read at 163 px/m. THIS is the real stepped seating on this site. The repo's `eighth.areas.amphitheatre` (3 tiers between the court's east edge and bed #2144) is corroborated by NO 2024-25 photograph and is superseded.
seatTerraces.positionNote: The station along The Social is not resolved by any frame. It is placed by a stated deterministic rule rather than a guess: the position nearest The Social's OWN DERIVED CENTROID at which the whole 9.0 x 2.7 m footprint — three 0.90 m treads over a 9.0 m run — lies on MEASURED paved spans, searched on a 0.5 m grid over `places.social.rect`. That is [-76.1, 563.8], 13.75 m from the centroid (-62.35, 563.70); only four stations in the whole rectangle accept, all of them in the same 0.5 x 1.0 m cluster, so the answer is not sensitive to the tie-break. RE-SOLVED 2026-08-19, TWICE OVER. (1) The footprint shrank: the earlier 9.0 x 3.1 m assembly included a public-art wall at its north edge, and that wall is WITHDRAWN — eighthgathering.bbq.mural builds the same commission, anchored on a surveyed ring and with its artwork sourced, so this section may not build a second carrier for it. See `absent`. (2) The earlier station [-75.5, 563.0] did not satisfy its own stated predicate: run against the shipped span table it is NOT a position at which the whole assembly lands on measured paving, and the centroid it claimed to be nearest, (-74, 559), was not the centroid of the derived rectangle either — both were left over from the round-one `places` table that the arbitration replaced. The rule and the answer now agree, and the test re-runs the search rather than reading the answer.

court.label: the basketball court — a MODULAR SPORT TILE court, not paint on asphalt
court.surfaceNote: The tile grid is visible across both the navy field and the gold keys in full sun (SWA -16). THE MARKINGS AND THE SURFACE ARE NOT REBUILT HERE: campus-eighth-court.js already draws the court line for line off the survey, with a parametric trident. What this section changes is COLOUR — see `supersedes` — and what it adds is the hardware campus-eighth-court.js declares absent.

apron.source: [measured] from the survey itself, not from the photograph. In the shipped span table the paved run immediately EAST of the surveyed court polygons is 2.44-2.48 m on all 25 rows that cross the court z band (median 2.45), which is the apron proper and independently corroborates SWA -16 read of a 2-3 m cast-concrete apron. The WEST run is 5.48 m on both its rows; `reach` is that widest surveyed adjacent run, and the courtApron paving zone is the surveyed court bounding rectangle grown by it, so the whole cast-concrete apron takes the P4 family. Round one typed the zone rectangle as x -190..-158, z 512..537 with no derivation at all.
apron.note: The zone rectangle is DERIVED by the module from measured.court.rect and `reach`; the stored rect must equal that derivation and the test re-derives it.

hedge.label: the clipped hedge row along the court's north side and its east side
hedge.source: swa -16 — a clipped hedge row on the court edge. Anchored to the surveyed strips arcgis.ground#1761 (north, 26.8 x 1.0 m) and #2144 (east, 2.2 x 20.7 m); campus-eighth.js already paints both, this builds the volume.

court.tileModuleNote: [estimated] 0.305 m (12 in) is the standard modular sport-tile product module; the tile grid is visible in SWA -16 but no frame resolves it against a scale bar. RECORDED, NOT DRAWN — campus-eighth-court.js owns the court surface (see surfaceNote), so nothing here reads this figure. Listed in measured.notDrawn.

parkingElevator.label: the north parking-elevator pavilion in The Wellness Corridor
parkingElevator.source: [estimated] position — SWA -16 shows a tan-brick surface block with one large louvre panel and one flush door at the end of the basketball court; both site plans label two PARKING ELEVATOR structures, one here and one mid-site. Plan about 7 x 5 m and 4.0 m high, read against the 1.70 m figures in front of it at 70 px/m. ANCHOR: arcgis.ground#2374 (252 m2, x -202.7..-191.2, z 514.6..537.4) is the pale slab immediately WEST of the court that campus-eighth.js flags as unregistered, uncoloured and 'what a viewer actually sees'. A surface structure with an apron is the reading that explains that slab; the pavilion is centred on it. Replace if a frame resolves the pavilion's true station.
parkingElevator.note: The mid-site pavilion is NOT built — see `absent`.

bambooGarden.label: the Bamboo Garden / Mental Wellness Zone floor

gravel.tileNote: [estimated] extends DG.tile — the same decomposedGranite noise class at a finer scale, because SWA -3 and -21 show the Bamboo Garden raked to a visibly finer grade than the Ramble walks. No unit grid, so no x6 factor.

planterCubes.source: swa -3 overhead — twelve dark charcoal square planter cubes counted, 1.60 x 1.60 x 0.90 m with a thin cap, holding clipped shrub balls, small multi-stem trees or clumping bamboo. Read against people sitting on the cube rims in SWA -13.

bambooGarden.extentNote: THIS SUPERSEDES the shipped eighth section's '~11 x 8 m surveyed opening', which used the GAP between arcgis.ground#328 and #329 rather than the garden island itself. The island is arcgis.ground[3632] hole ring 193, 792.3 m2, x -189.7..-158.8, z 573.0..602.8, and the 2025 plan's white field at x -192..-161, z 576..605 independently confirms it to about 3 m.

pavilionClip.note: NOT THIS SECTION'S GEOMETRY. This is eighthgathering.meditation.bark.rect, carried verbatim so everything this section builds in the Bamboo Garden can be held out of it. The gravel rides the `carpet` rung and gathering's bark decal rides `pad`, so gravel over the whole island would paint the Meditation Pavilion's own ground surface out from under it; and the rect is a 0.45 m solid deck under a roof in the owning section, so a solid of this section's built inside it is inside the pavilion. The rect is gathering's measured spine opening, clipped to the courtyard-328/329 rings; this section neither measures it nor draws anything inside it. CORRECTED 2026-08-19: that last sentence used to be false. The LED seat terrace was built 12.9 m inside this rect and two of the eight garden bands ran straight across it, and nothing gated it because the test asserted that the clip EXISTED rather than that anything was absent from it. The seat terrace is re-solved, the bands are cut, the gravel clip now cuts spans in x instead of dropping whole rows, and the gate walks every placement and every merged vertex this module builds.
pavilionClip.clearanceNote: [derived] 0.02 m, the same one-drawing-tolerance offset eighthgathering holds its own bark decal inside this rect at (`meditation.bark.inset`). It is not decoration: this rect is a SOLID 0.45 m deck with a roof over it in the owning section, so anything this section builds must clear it rather than touch it, and geometry sharing a face with a sibling's solid is geometry inside it as soon as either side moves. It is the rejection margin for the seat terrace, the garden bands, the raked gravel and the planter cubes alike.

lawns.label: the one resolved turf panel
lawns.materialNote: The library class is chosen for its MICROSTRUCTURE, not its name: decomposedGranite is the library's fine granular normal/roughness pair and at a 0.8 m tile it reads as mown turf grain. The library's own `foliage` class is an alpha-cut CARD map and would punch holes through a ground fill — campus-photo-keeling.js records the same trap.

panels.source: arcgis.ground#2369, 7 vertices, x -135.7..-104.3 (31.4 m) x z 559.2..580.7 (21.5 m); arcgis.ground[3632] hole ring 176 punches the identical polygon out of the paving. Photographed green and mown in SWA -4 and phf22.

lawns.falsifies: This section does NOT retire shipped eighth.absent[7]. That entry names 'the big turf panel NORTH OF THE TERRACE'; the terrace is arcgis.ground#2375 (shipped eighth.areas.bbq.anchor), so absent[7] refers to the lawn inside arcgis.ground#1160, whose outline is still unresolved and whose panel is withdrawn from this section. What this panel DOES supersede is campus-eighth-furniture.js TURF_PANELS `turf-2369`: the same lawn, traced from one Apple frame at 148.0 m2, an under-trace of the surveyed 351.6 m2 ring by 58%, and offset ~8-10 m west of the turf in ESRI orthoimagery registered sub-metre to the surveyed court. Both must not ship: two turf decals on different rungs at different colours.
lawns.colourConflict: campus-eighth.js paints both panels EIGHTH_COLORS.dryLawn #ab9d83 with the note 'tan in FULL SUN, never green', sampled from Apple Maps 3D frame ref3. SWA -4 and EYRC phf22, both 2024-25, show mown irrigated green turf with hard concrete edges. Two dated sources disagree; the newer, higher-resolution one wins under the epoch rule, and the Apple read is consistent with a newly-seeded lawn photographed before establishment. The tan paint stays on the `pad` rung underneath; this section's turf paints over it on `carpet`.

syntheticWithheld.source: NOT BUILT — SWA -18 and -14 show a bright uniformly green synthetic panel about 10 x 6 m with a hard concrete edge and a paver band, holding the Adirondack cluster at The Social. No measured paved run anywhere in The Social accepts a 10 x 6 m footprint without overrunning a surveyed planting bed (searched on a 0.5 m grid over the whole place), and the panel's dimensions are approximate. Shrinking a sourced dimension to make it fit would be inventing a measurement; see `absent`.

lawns.tileNote: [estimated] extends DG.tile — decomposedGranite is borrowed for its fine granular microstructure (see materialNote) and has no unit grid, so this is a grain scale, not a product dimension.

social.label: The Social, the courtyard between Podemos and Sankofa Base
social.derivation: [measured] DERIVED FROM TWO MASSING RINGS, not typed. z0 = 555.3 is the SOUTH face of arcgis.massing[252] (TDLLN - Podemos, z 499.6..555.3); z1 = 572.1 is the NORTH face of arcgis.massing[461] (TDLLN - Sankofa Base, z 572.1..630.2); x0 = -82.6 and x1 = -42.1 are the overlap of those two masses x extents (Podemos x -82.6..-25.2, Sankofa Base x -129.3..-42.1). The Social is by definition the courtyard between those two buildings, so every edge of this rectangle is a survey vertex. The seat terrace this section solves at (-76.1, 563.8) falls inside it, which is the independent check. Until 2026-08-19 the check named a public-art wall at (-75.5, 561.65) that has since been withdrawn to eighthgathering.
social.note: This is the ONLY `places` rectangle left. Round one carried seven (academic, social, wellness, bamboo, ramble, loggia, market), all typed round numbers with no source, and they were the sampling domain for about 250 scattered objects. Every one of those objects went to a sibling section in the 2026-08-19 arbitration; the six orphaned rectangles are deleted rather than left as unsourced geometry, and the one that survives now has a derivation.

supersedes.target: campus-eighth.js EIGHTH_COLORS.courtSurface = "#141727" ("ref9 + ref2, agreeing to 2 RGB counts — the navy inside the lines")
supersedes.replacement: colors.courtNavy #404a5b — the sunlit albedo, measured by ratio to the court's own white linework
supersedes.why: Both Apple frames agree with each other because both are DEEP SHADOW; agreement between two shadowed samples is not a calibration. SWA -16 is a clean sunlit eye-level photograph of the whole court, and the navy is the median of the navy/linework reflectance ratio over 174 tiles containing both, repeated at five region/threshold configurations, anchored to the shipped courtLine neutralised at its own luma601. Even after campus-eighth-court.js's old 1.7x tonedToLift the shipped value rendered at luma 40.7 against a measured 72.9 — the court shipped about 1.8x too dark. This section no longer draws the court (eighthsiteworks owns the hardware and campus-eighth-court.js the markings); the correction is recorded here because this is where it was measured.

supersedes.target: campus-eighth.js EIGHTH_COLORS.courtKey = "#2f372f" ("the lanes are OLIVE/khaki, not UCSD gold")
supersedes.replacement: colors.courtGold #cf9443 (the lanes) — measured by ratio to the court's own white linework over 8 configurations
supersedes.why: SWA -16 is a clean sunlit eye-level photograph of the whole court and the keys are UCSD gold. The olive read is a median of a SHADOWED Apple 3D frame (ref9 + ref2, both recorded in campus-eighth.js as deep blue-cast shadow); a sunlit dated photograph beats a shadowed photogrammetric mesh sample of the same surface.

supersedes.replacement: colors.courtTrident #e1c44b (the centre mark) — a different, yellower gold from the lanes, derived by transfer in the same frame
supersedes.why: The centre trident is the same UCSD gold as the keys in SWA -16. The #576564 median is 24,470 rectified pixels of the same shadowed frame; the geometry it was measured on (campus-eighth-court.js's parametric trident) is unaffected and stays.

supersedes.target: campus-eighth-furniture.js TURF_PANELS[0], key "turf-2369" — a 15-vertex 148.0 m2 turf panel traced from one Apple frame inside arcgis.ground#2369
supersedes.replacement: lawns.panels[0] "sun-lawn" — the FULL surveyed arcgis.ground#2369 ring, 351.6 m2, on the `carpet` rung
supersedes.why: Same lawn, and only one of them may ship or the Sun Lawn is drawn twice on two rungs at two colours (#9d947c against lawnTurf). The shipped panel is a single-frame trace at 148.0 m2, a 58% under-trace of the surveyed ring, and in ESRI orthoimagery registered sub-metre to the surveyed basketball court it sits 8-10 m WEST of the turf while the surveyed ring lands on it; the shipped module's own note concedes the outline is 'declared as one frame's' and that its second frame ref8 was 5.7 m out. SHIPPED eighth.absent[7] IS NOT TOUCHED: 'the big turf panel north of the terrace' is the lawn inside arcgis.ground#1160 (the terrace is #2375), whose outline is still unresolved and which this section no longer paints.

supersedes.target: campus-photo-detail.json eighth.areas.amphitheatre (3 tiers between the court's east edge and bed #2144)
supersedes.why: No 2024-25 photograph corroborates stepped seating in that band; it was inferred from a zigzag tiered edge on the 2021 DESIGN plan. The real stepped seat terrace is at The Social (SWA -18, -14), with eight students sitting on it.

supersedes.target: campus-eighth.js omission "Stair flights, terraces, retaining and seat walls ... the 2014 LiDAR under the courtyard is smooth ... so there is no built grade for a flight to descend or a wall to retain"
supersedes.replacement: levelChange (built where anchored; declared in `absent` where not)
supersedes.why: The 2014 LiDAR predates the college by seven years and measures a parking lot. Its smoothness is evidence of nothing here. Eleven 2024-25 photographs resolve the flights and walls.

supersedes.target: campus-eighth.js omission "The angular concrete plate mosaic ... a 30-degree rotated scoring ships instead"
supersedes.why: There are no plates. SWA -12 (near-overhead) resolves the units as a narrow-modular 2:1 paver in a three-to-four-grey random BLEND; the 'mosaic' is the colour blend and the chevron FIELD boundaries, not irregular plate outlines. And the extent was never missing: arcgis.ground[3632] is a surveyed walk multipolygon that yields 9,785 m2 of paving inside these bounds with guaranteed non-overlap against every bed.

Market Hall Plaza, The Backyard, Theatre Walk, the Theatre Drop-Off, both southern portals, the Loading Dock, the Survivance Front Porch, the mid-site parking-elevator pavilion and the mobility hub all fall outside the shipped bounds, so the southern third of the college could not ship under the ultra standard at all.

absent: The artificial turf panel at The Social. SWA -18 and -14 photograph a bright uniformly green synthetic panel about 10 x 6 m with a hard concrete edge, holding the Adirondack cluster. No measured paved run anywhere in The Social accepts a 10 x 6 m footprint without overrunning a surveyed planting bed, searched on a 0.5 m grid over the whole place. The photographed dimension is approximate and the station is unresolved; shrinking the dimension to force a fit would be inventing a measurement.

The accessible ramp. Cast concrete, 1.80 m clear width, about a 14 m run between landings with a 0.10 m upstand kerb and a guard both sides, photographed in SWA -4 and -2. Its rise is inferred from the CBC 1:12 maximum, not measured, and NO source resolves where it starts or ends. A ramp placed at a guessed station on a terrain that predates the college would be a floating deck with an invented grade at both ends.

The bridge over the Ramble — RETIRED, BUILT BY A SIBLING. eighthramble.systems.bridges builds BOTH crossings on their surveyed walk rings, and its west-bridge correction is real: the survey's own ring there is a right TRIANGLE, 5.60 m on its legs, not the 5 x 2.4 m rectangle the shipped model 'shortened to fit'. The deck width 2.4 m this section measured (two men abreast in phf22) survives inside that. Nothing here is unresolved any more; the entry stays only so the measurement keeps its provenance and so the reader is sent to the section that owns it.

Stairs S2, S3 and S4 — PARTLY RETIRED. S2, the Pulse entry steps at the basketball court, is BUILT: eighthgathering.courtStair ships it with a derivation, 7 treads, clipped by the surveyed planting bed it runs into. Still absent are The Social steps (6-7 risers, about 6 m wide) and the two broad Ramble flights (6-7 risers each, about 3.5 m): both are photographed and neither is anchored to a surveyed ground feature or to a terrace anyone has built, so a flight placed by eye would be an invented grade change. The handrail spec they will take is eighthsiteworks.systems.handrail; the flights themselves land first.

Every retaining-wall run except the 26.8 m behind the basketball court. About 260 m of W1 is visible across SWA -2, -5, -6, -16 and phf19, but the survey does not carry walls and the level changes they hold are not in the 2014 terrain; only the run the surveyed hedge strip arcgis.ground#1761 anchors is built.

The Front Porches at Pulse, Podemos, Azad and Sankofa — RETIRED AS A GAP, RE-POINTED AT THEIR OWNERS. All four are named on the 2025 plan as raised entry terraces, and each is now its own building team's geometry rather than this section's: sankofa.frontPorch, azad.porch and pulse.groundStorey.porch ship, and Podemos' is being built in this same pass. This section never had a source that dimensioned any of them and it does not build one; what it withdraws is the claim that the porches are UNBUILT. They are simply not hardscape.

The mural artwork — RETIRED FROM THIS SECTION, BUILT BY A SIBLING. SWA -14/-18 resolve a panel of pale eucalyptus branches on a blue-lilac ground; the same eucalyptus-leaf motif is the interior lobby mural in phf32/phf35, so it is one commission. eighthgathering.bbq.mural builds it — 3.4 x 1.9 m on its service-enclosure face, anchored on the surveyed arcgis.ground#2375, with the branch and leaf figures code-generated from its seed and never a photographic texture — and gathering's note already retires the shipped eighth absent entry. This section's own read (a panel about 7.5 x 3.2 m on a board-formed wall at the top of The Social's seat terrace) is a DIFFERENT STATION for the same commission and it is the weaker of the two: gathering's is anchored on a survey ring and this one was an [estimated] position. One commission, one owner. This section no longer claims to supersede the shipped entry either.
The mid-site parking-elevator pavilion between Sankofa Base and Market Hall Plaza. Labelled on both site plans, photographed by nothing in the set.
The Loading Dock, the Theatre Drop-Off turnaround, the mobility hub and both parking-structure portals. Named on the 2025 plan, inside the corrected bounds, and photographed by nothing in the set.

The Market Hall / STATION8 pavilion itself and the Survivance and Podemos-academic masses. They are massing, not hardscape, and arcgis.massing[462], [464] and [252] are missing from campus-eighth.json entirely. This section cuts them out of the paving so nothing runs under them, and builds none of them.

Paving manufacturer, exact nominal unit sizes and the colour-blend recipe. Unit widths and aspect ratios are measured to about 10% (0.089 m for P1, 0.315 x 0.157 m for P2), but no catalogue product is named and no paving schedule is published. WHICH blend covers WHICH field is photo-inferred and ships as a rectangle approximation of angular chevron boundaries.

The chevron field boundaries themselves. SWA -12 shows five distinct re-entrants in one frame at an included angle of 110-130 degrees, deviating 25-35 degrees from the building grid. Their outlines are not traceable at that resolution and the survey does not carry them; drawing them would be exactly the invented plate geometry this pass exists to retire.

Luminaire manufacturer and model for both pole families, for the bollard and for the recessed riser step-light. Head and pole geometry are measured off 6x crops; product identity is not established and no cut-sheet, spec or campus lighting standard was found. No pole POSITION is sourced either — the grid rule is declared, not photographed.

Every night state. Two LED systems are photographed (the continuous strips under the Bamboo Garden seat nosings and the vertical slots between the pavilion's screen segments) and both are built as recessed dark channels only. This project has no night source; campus-photo-keeling.js takes the same position on its lamps.

The Meditation Pavilion's screen-segment count and radii — SETTLED BY A SIBLING. eighthgathering.meditation builds three free-standing curved vertical batten drums, 46 screen panels at a 0.95 m module with a 0.075 m slot on the three measured drum arcs, and three oculi counted in SWA -3. That retires this section's 'five to six individual cylindrical segments per frame, none of them resolvable'. The pavilion is not this section's geometry at all any more; the observation is kept so the count's provenance is not lost.

The Meditation Pavilion roof's plan dimension — SETTLED BY A SIBLING. This section read 14.9 x 8.6 m off the georegistered 2025 plan and SWA -3's overhead read close to square, and it shipped the plan figure with the conflict open. eighthgathering resolved it to 13.5 x 7.3 m by solving the horizon from two known heights, which cancels the unknown focal length and camera distance (12.6 m), and cross-checking against a 37.2 m surveyed ruler in SWA -3 (14.3 m). It is also the only figure that fits inside courtyard-328/329's measured 14.9 x 7.9 m opening without standing on either surveyed ring. Not this section's geometry.

The basketball backboard size conflict — SETTLED, AND NOT THIS SECTION'S OBJECT ANY MORE. This section measured 1.35 +/- 0.07 x 0.98 +/- 0.05 m against the 3.048 m rim and called it recreational, not the 1.83 x 1.07 m regulation board; eighthsiteworks asserted the regulation board without measuring its width. Arbitration measured it against the coplanar 24 x 18 in shooter's square and by affine rectification of the board plane on both hoops: it is a 54 x 42 in (1.372 x 1.067 m) institutional glass board — this section's WIDTH class was right and its height was wrong. The standards are built by eighthsiteworks.systems.courtHardware and this section builds no court hardware. Kept so the measurement keeps its provenance.

Plant species as identifications. Every species in this section's `species` list is a photograph-based reading: genus is confident and species probable for most, but no planting schedule is published, so cultivars, quantities and spacings are unknown and the drifts are visually estimated. Nothing is labelled with a species in the built geometry.

New trees. The footprint already carries 45 LiDAR canopies and the 2024-25 photographs show a later generation; adding unregistered trees would double-plant. campus-eighth.js's judgement that 'the correct tree work here is subtractive' still stands and is not this section's to make.

arcgis.ground#1127 (1,985 m2, the south-western slope) and the remaining unregistered rings inside the envelope. #2374 is now given a reading — it is the apron of the north parking-elevator pavilion — but #1161 (334 m2, east of the court) and the rest still have no colour source and are not painted.

The CEQA / EIR record — RUNG EXERCISED 2026-08-19, AND IT FAILS. ceqanet.lci.ca.gov/2016111019 is the UC San Diego La Jolla 2018 LRDP Update, a campus-wide Notice of Preparation filed 2016-11-04, not a project EIR for this college; its own page states that the record was posted before CEQAnet could host attachments and that the 28 project documents must be obtained from the lead agency by telephone. The Theatre District Living and Learning Neighborhood entry inside it (2016111019/7, Addendum No. 5, August 2020) hosts exactly two attachments: a 187 KB Notice of Determination and a 145 KB Department of Fish and Wildlife fee receipt. Neither is a plan set. There are therefore NO risers, no terrace levels, no ramp rise and no grading or landscape drawings on this rung, and the ladder is genuinely exhausted before the [estimated] tier is used for the academic stair, the ramp and the terrace levels. The one planning document that IS in hand, the 2020 Regents item f9attach6, is a design-approval narrative with renderings and no dimensioned plan. What would still settle these: a UC San Diego Physical and Environmental Planning records request for the Addendum No. 5 project description, or the Kitchell / HKS record drawings.

THE WELLNESS CORRIDOR LAWN, arcgis.ground#1160. The ring is 1,521.9 m2 and carries TWO surfaces, so it cannot take one decal. ESRI z20 orthoimagery, registered sub-metre against the surveyed basketball court, shows a mown irrigated lawn over the west and centre (chroma-normalised gn 0.4061, the greenest surface in the college) and decomposed-granite mulch with boulders, sparse bunchgrass and a serpentine concrete walk over the east arm and everything south of z 530 (gn 0.3684, indistinguishable from Ramble beds #332 and #2703). The SDAF 2025 plan agrees: dark-linework fraction 59.1% over the east arm, matching Ramble bed #2703 at 53.6%, against 18.1-27.8% over the middle and west and 15.0% over the Sun Lawn. THE DIVIDING EDGE IS NOT RESOLVED: no arcgis ring and no ground[3632] paving hole divides #1160, and every imagery classifier tried here confuses mown turf with bunchgrass (control medians gn 0.3757 lawn vs 0.3722 bunchgrass) or is broken by the tower shadow — one fitted edge, x = -0.6335z + 203.28, looked clean at rms 1.93 m and proved ~20 m wrong against the raw pixels. The lawn's east limit is somewhere between x -107 and -103; that is not good enough to ship. Shipped eighth.absent[7] therefore STANDS, and #1160 keeps campus-eighth.js's dry-lawn #ab9d83. Better absent than wrong. THE OUTER RING STILL TAKES ITS BED EDGE, and that is not a contradiction: what is unresolved is the internal boundary BETWEEN the two surfaces, so no decal may cover the ring; its outer 54-vertex boundary is a surveyed edge between a planted ring and the paved field under either reading of the inside, and the flush steel strip SWA -17/-13/-12 photograph at every bed boundary asserts nothing about which surface is behind it. `edging.rings` says so per ring rather than leaving it to a list in code — that list was previously hard-coded in the module with no justification anywhere, which is how ~226 m of the reported 1,152 m of edging came to be asserted on a ring whose surface this section withholds.

Site lighting — the three pole families this section proposed are superseded by eighthsiteworks' canonical schedule. Positions here were an invented 19 m/13 m grid, and this section's 5.5 m read of the Market Hall Plaza square-pole light is contradicted by phf26, where that family stands ABOVE the 5.75 m pedestrian post-top. eighthsiteworks.systems.l1Pole / l2Pole / bollardLight is the only fitted metrology in the set — two independently solved horizons 1.7% apart — and it is the only one that anchors positions to surveyed polygons by a declared rule.

The Meditation Pavilion and the Tea House — WITHDRAWN FROM THIS SECTION. Both were built here and by eighthgathering, whose versions win on evidence: the pavilion's plate is solved by cancelling the focal length between two known heights and cross-checked against a surveyed ruler, and this section's box overran courtyard-328/329's measured opening by 0.6 m in x and 3.2 m in z, i.e. it stood on two surveyed rings. The Tea House cube is EYRC phf44's, the only frame that shows the whole object unclipped; this section's 5.3 x 5.0 m plan is out by 55%. This section's own audit had already found its pavilion shipping a 30 mm-tall roof that missed its fascia by 1.48 m and hovered 50 mm over its screens.

Loose furniture, bike racks, bins, emergency towers, standpipes and cabinets — WITHDRAWN FROM THIS SECTION. Every one of them was placed here by a deterministic rejection scatter over `places` rectangles: the footprint had to land on a measured paved span, which keeps them out of beds and buildings but does not put any of them where a photograph shows one. eighthgathering anchors its furniture to the surveyed BBQ terrace ring and counts it frame by frame, and eighthsiteworks anchors its bike ranks, waste pairs and blue-light tower to named surveyed polygons by a declared placement rule. A scatter loses to an anchor. The standpipes and cabinets this section scattered have no anchored replacement and are therefore simply absent.

The two linear gas fire features. Both are real and both were built here, anchored at (-118.0, 561.0) and (-146.5, 594.5) — but eighthgathering builds the same object from the same frames, as a masonry wall with a real firebox opening and a lava-media bed rather than a glass pane on a box, and it already supersedes the shipped fire-feature and fire-seat-wall items. One fire feature, one section. This section withdraws its own; the anchored centres it measured are recorded here so the positions are not lost.

Colour roles for the objects that left this section. 21 roles went with their objects (pavilionRoof -> eighthgathering.colors.pavilionRoof; pavilionFascia -> eighthgathering.colors.pavilionFascia; pavilionSoffit -> eighthgathering.colors.pavilionSoffit; seatPod -> eighthgathering.colors.seatPod; woodScreen -> eighthgathering.colors.woodScreen; teaWood -> eighthgathering.colors.teaWood; adirondack -> eighthgathering.colors.adirondack; cafeChair -> eighthgathering.colors.cafeChair; tableTop -> eighthgathering.colors.tableTop; tableLeg -> eighthgathering.colors.tableLeg; fireGlass -> eighthgathering.colors.fireGlass; binCharcoal -> eighthsiteworks.colors (waste); emergencyBlue -> eighthsiteworks.colors (blueLight); rimOrange -> eighthsiteworks.colors.safetyOrange; backboardAcrylic -> eighthsiteworks.colors (courtHardware); cobble -> eighthramble.colors; mulch -> eighthramble.colors; boulderPale -> eighthramble.colors; slabStone -> eighthgathering.colors.standingStone; grassBlue -> eighthramble.colors; grassStraw -> eighthramble.colors) rather than staying here as a second hex for a surface a sibling already colours — two values for one surface inside one merged document is the defect the colour arbitration existed to close. THREE ARE DELIBERATELY KEPT although this section no longer draws them: courtNavy #404a5b, courtGold #cf9443 (the lanes) and courtTrident #e1c44b (the centre mark). All three are this section's own corrections of shipped campus-eighth.js hexes, they are named in `supersedes`, and eighthsiteworks carries the identical values — they are a record, not a second opinion. THREE MORE ROLES LEFT 2026-08-19 with the objects below: `safetyOrange` #d4622a went with the calisthenics rig (it survives as eighthsiteworks.colors.safetyOrange, which adopted THIS section's value and THIS section's derivation in the arbitration), and `fdcRed` #b02318 went with the grill station's protective bollards (it survives as eighthramble.colors.fdcRed, which likewise adopted this section's value). Neither hex is lost from the merged document; both are simply no longer this section's to carry, because a colour role for an object a section does not build is a colour for nothing.

1,929 m2 of arcgis.ground[3632] INSIDE this section bounds that is NOT Eighth College paving, and is no longer painted. ground[3632] is the campus-wide walk multipolygon (x -223..235, z -186..702); cropping it to the corrected bounds still left 1,305 m2 north of z 499.6 — the Charles David Keeling Apartments 2 and Galbraith Hall approach — and 624 m2 east of x -24.3, the Galbraith / Revelle side, all of it in z 480..540. Round one painted every square metre of it in Eighth PHOTOGRAPHED P1/P2 blend, which is photo-sourced appearance applied to ground that no frame in this section source set covers. It is now cut by measured.paving.collegeClip, whose two edges are the north face of arcgis.massing[252] and the east face of arcgis.massing[253], the northernmost and easternmost TDLLN masses. The survey outline of that ground is real and is still the survey; what is absent is any claim about what it LOOKS like. Note the trap this caught: the round-one boundsNote justified the eastern reach with Market Hall Plaza running to x +26.0, but the Plaza is arcgis.ground#3045, a separate walk polygon that contributes not one span to this table.

The 1.5 m sawcut score grid in the P4 cast-in-place concrete. The 1.5 m panel is MEASURED (EYRC phf19, against a 1.75 m walker spanning 118 px at panel depth) and the sawcut is about 0.006 m wide. It is not drawn. campus-materials.js has exactly one unit-grid class, FIELDS.pavingConcreteUnit, and its joint is a fixed 4.5% of the cell — 0.0675 m at a 1.5 m panel, eleven times the measured sawcut — so drawing the grid with the library would state a joint an order of magnitude wrong across the whole of Market Hall Plaza, Theatre Walk and the court apron. P4 therefore ships on smoothConcrete with no grid at all, and the measured panel size survives as the noise scale. Better absent than 11x wrong. What would settle it: a joint-width parameter on the library class, which is campus-materials.js work and not this section to do.

The paver blend AMPLITUDE. The three-to-four-grey random blend is real (SWA -12 resolves it) and it IS built — campus-materials.js FIELDS.pavingConcreteUnit gives every unit its own tone through N.cell(ci, ri), which multiplies the sourced hex, so the field is not one flat colour. What is NOT measured is how far apart those greys are: the library variation is a generic 0.86..1.02 of the base, about plus or minus 9%, and no frame in the set gives a clean enough unshaded patch to measure the spread between the lightest and darkest unit in one field. The MEDIAN of each family is measured (p1Paver, p3Paver, p4Concrete) and the amplitude around it is the library. Recorded rather than tuned by eye.

The LAYING DIRECTION of every paver family. The strip mesh lays uv = (x / tile[0], z / tile[1]), which aligns the measured unit long axis with world x everywhere. The measured units are strongly directional — P1 is 0.089 x 0.30 m and P2 is 0.315 x 0.157 m — so this is a real claim and no frame in the set fixes it: SWA -12 and -17 are the only near-overhead frames and neither carries surveyed control to resolve a bond direction against the building grid, and the field boundaries themselves are the unresolved chevrons already declared above. A single world-aligned direction is the honest minimum: it is stated here rather than presented as measured, and one rotation constant per family would fix it the day a georegistered overhead resolves the bond.

The Street View rung, and what it would and would not settle. It has NOT been exercised, and this entry says so rather than letting the [estimated] figures stand as though the ladder were exhausted. What it could settle: the academic stair risers and tread, the terrace levels, the ramp rise and the guard kerb — all things a camera at eye level on the flight resolves and a drone frame at 30 m does not. What makes it a weak lead here rather than a strong one: the objects still estimated stand in INTERIOR pedestrian courtyards between Podemos, Pulse and Sankofa, off any vehicle route, so they need Google pedestrian photo-path coverage rather than car coverage; and the section epoch rule already bars Google imagery over Eighth as MID-CONSTRUCTION, so any Street View pass has to be date-stamped after November 2023 before a single figure may be read off it. The two figures that most need it are stairs.S1.riser 0.17 and .tread 0.33, which are today bounded by CBC 1011.5 and proportioned from phf03, not measured.

The p1Paver / p2Paver duplicate hex, DECLARED NOT ACCIDENTAL. colors.p1Paver and colors.p2Paver are the same #cdbdaf and that is the honest answer, not an oversight: p1Paver is a [measured] median of a 400 x 70 px unshaded patch in EYRC phf03, and p2Paver is [estimated] carrying it verbatim because no frame gives the P2 field a clean unshaded median large enough to trust. The two families are the same warm three-tone narrow-modular blend photographed at different unit sizes, so extending the measured hex is the ultra standard third tier used exactly as written — it names the sourced pattern it extends and it is replaced the day a clean P2 patch is sampled. What DOES separate the two families on screen is the tile: 0.534 x 1.8 m against 1.89 x 0.942 m, both derived from their measured units.

THE SAFETY-ORANGE CALISTHENICS RIG — WITHDRAWN FROM THIS SECTION, OWNED BY campus-photo-pulsefitness.js. The rig beside the basketball court at the Pulse base is real: SWA -16 shows an orange steel rig with a top bar about 2.4 m above the pad, about 5.0 x 2.0 m overall in 0.09 m OD tube, read against the 1.75 m players at 70 px/m. It was built HERE at [-169.5, 534.5] and independently by eighthsiteworks at a different size 4.9 m away, and round two never arbitrated the collision — two orange rigs 4.9 m apart is worse than either. `pulseFitness` now owns it outright, at one size and one station. This section builds no part of it and carries no figure for it; its `safetyOrange` colour role went with it (see the colour-role entry above).

THE BBQ / GRILL STATION — WITHDRAWN FROM THIS SECTION, OWNED BY eighthgathering.bbq.grill. EYRC phf22 and SWA -4 do show a buff-CMU counter with TWO built-in grills, a thin flat canopy and red protective bollards, and this section built it at [-110.0, 557.5] on the measured paving just outside the Sun Lawn's north-east corner — an [estimated] POSITION. eighthgathering builds the same object ANCHORED on the surveyed arcgis.ground#2375 with the counter run measured at 4.6 m off crop_grill.png, plus the bays, splashback, end piers, extinguisher and service enclosure this version never had. The two stood about 30 m apart. Under this section's own rule — an anchored object beats a scattered one — gathering wins, and the claim this section made against the shipped `eighth.areas.bbq` anchor is withdrawn with it. Its `fdcRed` bollard colour went with it.

THE PUBLIC-ART CARRYING WALL AT THE SOCIAL — WITHDRAWN FROM THIS SECTION. This section built an 8.5 x 4.0 x 0.4 m board-formed concrete wall at [-75.5, 561.65] as the carrier for the eucalyptus commission, with the artwork itself left undrawn for want of a sampled palette. The commission is eighthgathering's (see the mural entry above), and a carrier for an artwork built 40 m away in another section is an invented wall. It is deleted rather than kept as scenery, and the seat terrace it stood behind is re-solved on its own 9.0 x 2.7 m footprint. If a frame is ever found that shows a board-formed wall at the head of The Social's seat terrace INDEPENDENTLY of the mural, this is the entry to replace.

STAIR S6, THE TEA HOUSE PLINTH STEPS — WITHDRAWN FROM THIS SECTION, OWNED BY eighthgathering.teaHouse.plinth. This section recorded two risers, riser 0.175 m, tread 0.45 m, width 3.2 m from EYRC phf44/phf45 and SWA -23, anchored to the georegistered Tea House plinth — and then the Tea House itself went to eighthgathering in the 2026-08-19 arbitration and took the plinth with it, leaving these four figures in the file with nothing to build and nothing to be anchored to. Gathering builds the object with its own derivation (2 risers counted in SWA -23, riser 0.165 m extending the college's measured 0.155 m court-stair riser, tread 0.45 m extending the measured 0.42 m terrace-stair tread), so no geometry is lost. A second, disagreeing record of a sibling's object is not a measurement this section may keep.
