species: Juncus patens (California grey rush) — stiff blue-grey upright clump 0.6-0.9 m x 0.6 m; the dominant swale and bed-edge plant through the Ramble, the Bamboo Garden mulch and the Tea House surround. Species probable, genus confident.
Muhlenbergia rigens (deer grass) — straw fountain tussock 0.9-1.2 m with 1.5 m flower spikes; Ramble slopes, Sun Lawn edge.
Verbena lilacina 'De La Mina' — airy 0.9 x 1.2 m shrub with lilac ball flowers; the purple flowering mass in SWA -5, -6, -2. Species probable.
Agave 'Blue Glow' / Agave attenuata — rosette 0.45-0.9 m; the gravel and cobble zones at the Tea House and the Bamboo Garden.
Westringia fruticosa or Pittosporum tenuifolium 'Golf Ball' — clipped sphere 0.6-0.9 m; the shrub balls in the charcoal planter cubes and at The Social.
Podocarpus macrophyllus or columnar Pittosporum — clipped upright column 2.5-3.0 m x 0.8 m; The Social planters and the basketball-court hedge.
Bambusa multiplex 'Alphonse Karr' — clumping bamboo with golden culms 4-6 m; the Bamboo Garden planters in SWA -13.
Agonis flexuosa, Cercis occidentalis, Arbutus 'Marina', Platanus racemosa, Quercus agrifolia — the tree palette read off phf22, SWA -8 and -12. NOT built: see `absent`.
Lomandra longifolia 'Breeze' or Carex divulsa — fine green tuft 0.6 x 0.6 m at the tower bases. Genus uncertain between the two.
Turf, tall-fescue blend, mown 0.06 m — the Sun Lawn (arcgis.ground#2369) and the Wellness Corridor lawn (arcgis.ground#1160). Blend probable.

eighthgathering.label: Eighth College — the four gathering places: the Meditation Pavilion, the Tea House, the court stair that replaces the 'amphitheatre', and the BBQ / fire-feature terrace.
eighthgathering.epoch: BUILT condition, 2024-2026. The published photographs (EYRC / Lawrence Anderson 2024-25; SWA Group, uploaded 2025-04) and the San Diego Architectural Foundation Open House site plan (2025-03) are the newest epoch and decide what exists. The 2021 Revelle town-hall deck is the DESIGN epoch and loses on existence wherever the two disagree — it is why three amphitheatre tiers shipped that were never built. The 2014 LiDAR is BLIND to this college (campus-lidar.json massHeights has no Eighth entry; campus-massing.js records LiDAR measuring Sankofa at parking-lot height), so no height here is a LiDAR height and the 'the LiDAR is smooth so there is no step' argument is void over Eighth. Google satellite over Eighth is mid-construction and is neither a colour nor an existence source.
eighthgathering.note: INVENTED class — photo-sourced detail per README. What is MEASURED here is the ground: every structure is anchored to a docs/data/campus-eighth.json ground ring copied verbatim into `measured` below, and where a photo estimate and the survey disagreed on a ground extent, the survey won and this file says so at the item. Photographs decide what exists, what it is made of and how it is put together; the survey decides where it stands and how far it may reach. Nothing measured may ever read from this section. Colours are data; the module holds no hex. Deterministic: every scatter is a hash of `seed`.

sources.what: EYRC / Lawrence Anderson, frontal dusk elevation of the Meditation Pavilion, 1799x1200. THE metric frame: the fascia band, the two measurable drums, the in-grade uplights, the seated figure that sets scale, the LED stair nosings in the foreground.
EYRC / Lawrence Anderson, Meditation Pavilion interior 3/4 from the west. Oculus proportion, bench end bracket, the standing stone in its gravel ring.

EYRC / Lawrence Anderson, Meditation Pavilion interior. The definitive assembly frame: floor-to-ceiling curved veneer segments with open vertical slots, LED strip at the wall base, ground-concrete floor, glazed oval oculus reading blue sky.
EYRC / Lawrence Anderson, the Tea House from the Ramble. Setting: cobble, boulders, rushes, agave.
EYRC / Lawrence Anderson, the Tea House, portrait frontal dusk. The batten glow, the portal reveal, the plinth.
EYRC / Lawrence Anderson, the Ramble / Sun Lawn edge. Both pole-luminaire families, inverted-U bike hoops, white precast planter cubes, the green Adirondack colour.

SWA Group, near-plan aerial. The ONLY overhead frame of the Meditation Pavilion: the hip and ridge creases that prove the roof is hipped, the THREE oval oculi that prove three lobes, the charcoal planter cubes.
SWA Group, Meditation Pavilion in daylight at eye level. People seated on the deck edge (which fixes the deck height at seat height) and the ground reading as shredded BARK, not gravel.
SWA Group, Meditation Pavilion dusk 3/4. The battered deck face, the gravel margin, the in-grade uplight row, the three LED-lit seat steps with people on them, the ovoid seat pods.

SWA Group, the Tea House at dusk, near-frontal, 2560x1440. THE metric frame for the batten module: FFT/autocorrelation at five scan heights returns 24-26 cycles PER FACE and a direct peak read at x 1150-1230 gives an 11.83 px pitch, which is the 26-per-face module this section ships. CORRECTION 2026-08-19: round one described this frame as giving '68/66/60 peaks' and attributed that count to one face; the cube spans x 1105-1935 with its corner at 1500, so that scan ran across BOTH visible faces and doubled the screen. Also the two plinth risers, the L-bench with an occupant, the shoe plates, the cobble bed, the pole light.

SWA Group, the fire-feature terrace in daylight, elevated 3/4. THE key frame: the 4 m glass-fronted linear fire feature in its precast block wall, nine lime-green Adirondacks, three black pedestal drink tables, teal wire chairs, plank benches, five conical precast planters, the grey grill counter with its red extinguisher post, the wide stair with its stainless handrail, the running-bond unit pavers, the artificial turf inset, and the blue eucalyptus mural.
SWA Group, the same fire feature at dusk, lit. Promotes the firebox from [estimated] to sourced in both states.

SWA Group, overhead oblique of the plaza. THE angular concrete plate paving mosaic photographed from above — irregular quadrilateral plates 1.2-2.5 m across in two greys and a tan over a fine checker-tile infill field. This is the courtyard signature the repo withheld for lack of per-plate geometry.

SWA Group, clean sunlit eye-level photograph of the whole basketball court. The 7-riser stair south of the court with its stainless pipe handrail on a mid-run standard, the low concrete seat wall beside it, the clipped hedge row on its retaining wall, and NO tiered zigzag anywhere east of the court.

San Diego Architectural Foundation Open House tour map — a north-up, labelled, BUILT-condition site plan. Registered to this world frame at 10.65 px/m on a 400 dpi render (see `frames.plan2025`). Source of the Tea House's true position, of the court stair's plan rectangle, and of the negative that retires the amphitheatre tiers.

UCSD Revelle College town-hall deck, slide 6 — the 2021 DESIGN site plan. Source of the pavilion's 1.96:1 drawn roof aspect and of its chain of THREE circles; also the ORIGIN of the zigzag tiered edge east of the basketball court that the built condition does not contain. DESIGN epoch: it loses to the 2025 plan and the 2024-25 photographs on existence.
The university's own page: 'Eighth College Plaza: grills, Zen Garden, Meditation Pavilion' — the second independent confirmation that the pavilion stands between Pulse and Azad.

EYRC / Lawrence Anderson, a full exterior stair with stainless pipe handrails. This section cites it twice and had not declared it: it is the frame arbitration measured the canonical Eighth handrail height on (0.896 m, from a bottom return at source y 935 against a base flange at y 1030 over a plaza ground plane fitted from two standing figures), which both this section's stairs extend. It is also one of the three frames that put the built terracing on the record against the blind 2014 LiDAR.

SWA Group, the calibration frame of the whole Eighth set: an L1 pole showing base and top with two people standing in the same plane, two bollard lights, a galvanised bike hoop. This section no longer builds any of that hardware — it went to eighthsiteworks in arbitration — but it is cited here for the second, shorter Ramble post-top family and must be openable by anyone checking that citation.

SWA Group, Scholars Cloister at close range: the bollard light resolving its cap and lens, and the paver field. Cited by this section only in the record of what it handed to eighthsiteworks, and declared so the citation can be opened.

plan2025.what: The 2025 Open House site plan registered to this repo's world frame. Reusable — do not re-derive.
plan2025.scaleDerivation: Colour transect across the surveyed basketball court (plan fill (231,214,188) against apron (237,228,199)): 241.0 px / 22.7 m = 10.617 px/m and 164.5 px / 15.4 m = 10.682 px/m, agreeing to 0.6 %. Adopt 10.65, anchored world (-185.9, 517.5) to plan px (905.5, 922.5).
plan2025.validation: Every ArcGIS Eighth massing ring overlays its drawn building within ~1.5 m across the whole 200 m site — the same order as this project's known 1.25 m Apple georegistration offset. Azad's drawn north facade lands at z 607.5 against the ring's 605.7.

spine.ringSource: docs/data/campus-eighth.json ground['courtyard-328'].points and ground['courtyard-329'].points, copied verbatim (ArcGIS ground rings, decimetres/10).
spine.openingDerivation: The Bamboo Garden's open spine is the gap BETWEEN the two surveyed courtyard rings, solved by sweeping z at 0.05 m and taking the worst case: courtyard-328's east edge never runs east of x -182.3 and courtyard-329's west edge never runs west of x -167.4 over z 584..591.9, so the measured opening is 14.9 x 7.9 m. Outside that z band the two rings close to within 1.5 m of each other and there is no opening at all. THIS RETIRES THE SHIPPED SCALE ARGUMENT: the eighth section's meditation area records the surveyed opening as '~11 x 8 m' and shrinks the pavilion to a 6.6 x 4.6 m slab to fit it. The opening is 14.9 m wide, the 2025 plan's own pavilion marker is 13.0 x 6.2 m and sits inside it, and phf47's photogrammetric 12.6 m and SWA-3's 14.3 m both land in the same place. Three independent reads agree and the shipped one was wrong.

teaHouse.gapDerivation: Sweeping z at 0.1 m across courtyard-1159 finds a lens-shaped gap between two lobes of the surveyed green polygon, 4.6-5.5 m wide and 4.7 m long over z 571.7..576.4, area 20.39 m2, centroid (-85.81, 574). The 2025 plan's Tea House highlight centroid converts to (-85.9, 575.3) — 1.3 m from that gap centroid, INSIDE the plan registration's own ~1.5 m validation residual. Two independent sources therefore put the Tea House in the same 5 m circle, 57 m east and 24 m north of where it currently ships. CLAIM LIMIT, recorded so nobody over-reads it: the gap's 20.39 m2 is within 8 % of this build's 18.9 m2 plinth and its 4.6-5.5 m width brackets the plinth's 4.2-4.5 m, but the gap is lens-shaped and the plinth does not nest inside it — the fit is CORROBORATIVE, not a surveyed footprint.
teaHouse.channelRotDerivation: Least-squares fit of the gap's own centreline: dx/dz = 0.3546 over the lens's 96 points, so rot = atan(0.3546) = 0.3410 rad, shipped 0.34. THIS IS THE DERIVATION OF teaHouse.rotY AND THE GATE ASSERTS THE TWO ARE EQUAL — round one left them as two independent numbers that happened to agree, which is a rotation that can drift away from the channel it was measured in with nothing to say so.
teaHouse.gapAreaDerivation: [derived] 20.39 m2 by the shoelace formula over the 96-point gap polygon above. The gate re-derives it; it exists so the gap cannot be quietly reshaped while the prose still calls it a 20.39 m2 lens.

courtStair.clipNote: The 2025 plan draws the stair 6.5 m wide from x -178.5. planting-bed-1760's measured east edge is x -177.8, so the plan rectangle overlaps the surveyed bed by 0.7 m. THE SURVEY WINS: the stair ships 5.8 m wide from x -177.8 and the bed is left alone.

meditation.label: The Meditation Pavilion, in the Bamboo Garden (the college's own page calls it the Zen Garden; both site plans call it the Bamboo Garden — same place).

The 2025 plan's tour marker for the pavilion converts to x -181.5..-168.5, z 584.5..590.7 and sits inside that opening; the marker's own linework is obscured by the tour's black-ring and green-box annotation, so the marker fixes POSITION only and the roof's size comes from the photogrammetry below. ARBITRATED: the competing 15.5 x 8.6 m box at z 586.5..595.1 is refuted by the surveyed rings themselves — it overruns courtyard-328/329's measured opening by 0.6 m in x and 3.2 m in z, and would be built on top of both rings.

roof.form: shallow HIPPED, dark blue-grey standing-seam metal, hip and ridge creases visible from above
roof.pitchNote: [estimated] 10 deg, the middle of the 8-12 deg band the crease geometry in SWA-3 supports. It reads flat from every eye-level frame, which a shallow hip does. No rung resolved the angle numerically; extends nothing but its own sourced hipped form.
roof.seamNote: 0.406 m (16 in) is the standard standing-seam panel width; the same class of named-product dimension as the 1.65 x 0.99 m PV module in the keeling section. The seam COUNT follows from it and the measured plate.
roof.eaveBattenNote: the continuous row of small blocks / rafter-tail battens along the eaves on the roof's upper surface (SWA-3, and in silhouette in phf47). Pitch [estimated] at 0.45 m, read against the 0.406 m seam it sits over.
roof.lengthDerivation: In EYRC phf47 the dark fascia band measures x 182 -> 1689 px (1508 px) at y 555-575 with BOTH tips inside the 1799 px frame. Scale in the drum plane is 95 px/m, from the seated woman (crown y=722 by dark-hair mask over x 1210-1236, deck contact y=803, 81 px / 0.85 m), cross-checked by the in-grade deck uplights reading 15 px = 0.16 m. Solving the horizon from the deck at y=807 (1.00 m below eye) and the soffit at y=608.5 (1.08 m above eye) gives y_h = 711.3 px, which lands on the seated woman's neck — correct for a ~1.6 m eye height. Depth ratio fascia:drums = (711.3-581)/(711.3-608.5) = 1.261, so the fascia sits at 0.793x the drum distance and the width is 1508 x 0.793 / 95 = 12.6 m. THIS CANCELS THE UNKNOWN FOCAL LENGTH AND CAMERA DISTANCE. Corroboration: SWA image 3, using the 37.2 m clear gap between the Pulse ring's z=568.5 and the Azad ring's z=605.7 as a ruler at the pavilion's depth (780 px => 21 px/m), gives 300 px => 14.3 m. 13.5 m is adopted between the two reads and inside the 14.9 m measured opening.
roof.depthDerivation: The 2021 plan's drawn roof rectangle is 135 x 69 px at 600 dpi = 1.96:1, so 13.5/1.96 = 6.9 m; SWA-3's foreshortened vertical read of 140 px is 6.7 m before de-projection. 7.3 m is adopted at the top of that band because the measured opening is 7.9 m deep and the roof must still clear the two surveyed rings, which it does by 0.30 m each side.
roof.fasciaDerivation: 31 px at y 550-581 in phf47, at the fascia's own scale of 95 x 1.261 = 119.8 px/m => 0.26 m.
roof.soffitDerivation: The screen top at y=608.5 (where the drum silhouette meets the lit soffit) to its base at y=798 at x=1150, with a dark shadow gap at 799-800, is 198 px / 95 px/m = 2.08 m. GAP DECLARED: this is one ratio in one frame and 2.08 m is low for a covered space. The range the frame supports is 1.95-2.20 m. No planning document, drawing or archive reached gives a pavilion section; the CEQA/EIR record at ceqanet.lci.ca.gov/2016111019 is the unexplored rung that would close it. ARBITRATED 2026-08-19: reproduced independently from phf47 without this section's own numbers — seated woman 87.5 px (rows 721.3/808.8), drum 194.5 px (rows 605/799.5), deck-row depth ratio 1.1054, so drum/seated = 2.457 = 2.09 m at a 0.85 m cross-legged sitting height. The competing 2.90 m read is refuted.

drums.derivation: phf47 orange-pixel runs at y=660 give x 504->910 (406 px) and x 917->1333 (416 px), tangent at x=913, at 95 px/m: chords of 4.27 m and 4.38 m. A cylinder shows its full diameter, so DRUM DIAMETER 4.3 m. The third lobe is [estimated] at 3.2 m, extending the two measured drums — the 2021 plan draws its left circle noticeably smaller. SOURCE CONFLICT declared and resolved in favour of THREE: phf47 resolves two, but the 2021 plan draws three chained circles and SWA-3 shows three oval oculi; two independent sources, one of them built-condition, say three. The chain spacings here are SOLVED, not read: each centre-to-centre distance is the smallest that keeps the two cylinders from intersecting at the built 0.8 m cross-axis offset, plus 0.06 m — because nothing may intersect.

screen.note: [estimated] panel width ~0.95 m, slot 60-90 mm (0.075 built), thickness 0.10-0.12 m (0.11 built) — read against the panel joints in phf49, which is the definitive assembly frame: floor-to-ceiling curved veneer segments with open vertical slots between them. TENSION RECORDED: phf49 shows 3-4 joints per visible drum face while half a 4.3 m drum is 6.75 m of face, which at 0.95 m panels would show six or seven. The 0.95 m figure is carried as the researcher stated it and is the first thing a drawing should correct. The slots are both the way in and the light source, so they are real geometry, never a texture.
screen.arcNote: Each drum is a run of cylindrical panel segments broken by two kinds of opening, and BOTH are derived, not chosen. (1) WHERE IT MEETS ITS NEIGHBOUR IN THE CHAIN the screen stops over exactly the angle the neighbouring cylinder occults — asin(r_neighbour / centre distance) each side of the bearing to it — because that is the arc over which the two chambers open into one another and a panel there would face its neighbour's wall. (2) FACING THE NORTHERN APPROACH one panel module is taken out with its slots either side: openingNorth = panelWidth + 2 x slot = 1.10 m of omitted face, the smallest opening this screen's own module can make, half of it each side of northBearing. Where the face left BETWEEN two openings is shorter than one panel module (panelWidth + slot) at that drum's own radius, no segment can stand in it and the two openings merge — which is why west ships one arc and mid, which has room everywhere, keeps three. Arcs are world angles, atan2(dz, dx), each written on the branch that makes it increase from its own start. THE ROUND-ONE ARCS WERE BROKEN: mid's third arc was written -2.803 for 3.480 and east's second ended 4.262 for -2.021, each an angle put on the wrong branch, which made those two arcs span 7.065 and 6.669 rad — more than a full circle — so each swallowed its own siblings, 78 pairs of panels were built exactly coincident, 12 of the 46 declared panels were phantoms, and the declared openings did not exist on mid or east at all. The gate now re-derives every arc from the rule above and separately refuses any span >= 2 pi, any overlap between two arcs of one drum, and any arc too short to hold one whole panel.

figures.height: [measured] 2.08 m — the screen runs deck to soffit, so it IS meditation.roof.soffitClear. The gate asserts the two are equal.
figures.panelWidth: [estimated] 0.95 m, read against the panel joints in phf49. TENSION RECORDED in `note`: phf49 shows 3-4 joints per visible drum face where 0.95 m panels would show six or seven. Carried as the researcher stated it and named as the first thing a drawing should correct. Extends nothing measured — it is the frame's own joint spacing at an uncertain depth.
figures.slot: [estimated] 0.075 m, the middle of the 60-90 mm band phf49 supports. Extends the panel module it interrupts.
figures.thickness: [estimated] 0.11 m, the middle of the 0.10-0.12 m band phf49 supports. Extends the panel module.
figures.panels: [derived] the sum of the three lobes' `panels`, which the gate re-derives from the arcs at this module.
figures.northBearing: [derived] -pi/2 rad. Angles here are world atan2(dz, dx) and +z is south, so -pi/2 is due north — the bearing of the approach into the Bamboo Garden's open spine. Not a reading: it is the frame's own north.
figures.openingNorth: [derived] 1.10 m of omitted face = panelWidth + 2 x slot = 0.95 + 2 x 0.075. The screen is a run of panels at a fixed module, so the smallest opening it can make is one panel taken out with the slots either side of it; the northern approach gets exactly that. Expressed as an angle it is openingNorth / (2 r) each side of northBearing, which is why it is wider on the small west lobe than on the two 4.3 m drums.

figures.diameterMeasured: [measured] 4.3 m. phf47 orange-pixel runs at y=660 give x 504->910 (406 px) and x 917->1333 (416 px), tangent at x=913, at 95 px/m: chords of 4.27 m and 4.38 m, and a cylinder shows its full diameter. The gate asserts every measured-tier lobe's 2r equals this.

bench.note: A continuous curved bench cantilevered off the inside face of each drum with NO visible legs, same blond veneer as the screen, square front edge, a continuous LED strip recessed in the shadow gap beneath it, and a short dark blade bracket at the free end. This retires the shipped absent entry 'Meditation pavilion and tea house interiors beyond the bench — no source.' The seat height is [estimated]: see `figures`, where the round-one 0.32 ratio is shown not to close against this drum's own measured screen height.

figures.seatHeight: [estimated] 0.42 m. THE ROUND-ONE DERIVATION DOES NOT CLOSE and is corrected here rather than carried: it claimed the bench-to-floor distance is 0.32 of the visible wall height in the same plane, but 0.32 of this drum's measured 2.08 m screen is 0.67 m, not 0.42 m, so the stated ratio cannot be what produced the figure. Demoted. It extends this college's own measured seat heights — meditation.deck.height 0.45 m, measured from people sitting on the deck edge in SWA-20/21, and teaHouse.bench.seatHeight 0.44 m, measured at 80 px / 182 px/m — and is the lowest of the three because a cantilevered bench sits below a plinth edge.
figures.depth: [measured] 0.45 m, the seat depth read in phf49 against the same 95 px/m scale that fixes the drum chords.
figures.ledGap: [derived] 0.06 m — the shadow gap under the seat is one seat slab deep, and `slab` is 0.06 m. phf49 shows the gap and the wash starting at its back, but nothing in the gap carries a scale, so it is tied to the member above it rather than guessed.
figures.slab: [estimated] 0.06 m seat slab. Extends the 0.11 m screen thickness this bench is cut from the same veneer as, at a little over half of it — the thinnest member phf49 resolves as a separate board.
figures.bracket: [estimated] a 0.06 x 0.28 x 0.40 m dark blade. phf48 shows it and no frame gives it a scale. Extends this bench's own measured 0.45 m depth: the blade runs 0.40 m of that, stopping 0.05 m short of the front edge, and is the same 0.06 m thickness as the seat slab it carries.

cube.ridgeNote: the ridge sits OFF-CENTRE at 0.62 of the width, so one slope is short and steep and the other long and shallow — a symmetric roof loses the object.
cube.sizeDerivation: [measured] EYRC phf44 — the ONLY frame that shows the whole cube unclipped, with two occupants seated inside. Left edge x 746.7, corner x 980, right edge x 1181.7 give projected faces of 233 and 202 px, so kS = sqrt(233^2 + 202^2) = 308.4 px; corner top 365, base 747, so height = 382 px and height/plan = 1.24 — the object is TALLER than it is wide, which no round-one value had. The occupants read ~70 px bench-to-crown; at 0.88 m erect sitting height and ~1.5 m behind the near corner, S = 3.874 D/(D+1.5) and H = 4.805 D/(D+1.5), giving S = 3.26-3.60 m and H = 4.05-4.47 m for any camera distance D = 8-20 m. Shipped at the D = 10 m solution: plan 3.4 m, ridge 4.18 m, eave 3.65 m (phf44's top edge falls 4.07 -> 3.57 m across the cube, a 0.5 m rise). SWA -23 corroborates from the other side (plan/height <= 0.67 with its top clipped at row 0) and is NOT usable for absolute scale, because its single occupant sits on the outboard end of the bench in FRONT of the cube's face plane. This refutes both round-one cubes: 5.3 x 5.0 m is out by 55%, and 3.6 x 2.8 m has the right plan but a ridge 1.4 m too low. THE RIDGE BEARING IS NOT RESOLVED — see absent.

figures.size: [measured] 3.4 m plan side — EYRC phf44, the only frame showing the whole cube unclipped. Projected faces 233 and 202 px give kS = 308.4 px against a 382 px corner height, so height/plan = 1.24; the two seated occupants at ~70 px bench-to-crown fix S = 3.26-3.60 m for any camera distance 8-20 m. Shipped at the D = 10 m solution. See sizeDerivation.

WHICH WAY IT RUNS IS NOT RESOLVED (see `absent`): SWA-23 puts the high point at the near corner and phf44 at the west face's left edge. battens.derivation: [measured] 26 battens per face at 0.119 m pitch. CORRECTION TO ROUND ONE: the '66 peaks over 801 px' scan of SWA -23 was taken across BOTH visible faces of the cube (which spans x 1105-1935 with the corner at 1500), and 66 was then attributed to one face — doubling the screen. Independent counts: FFT/autocorrelation at five scan heights on each SWA -23 face returns 24-26 cycles; a direct peak read at x 1150-1230 gives 11.83 px pitch (peaks 1152/1163/1175/1187/1199/1211/1223); prominence-filtered peak finding over each full face returns 24 and 26; and phf44's direct profile at x 760-880 gives 8.83 px pitch over a 233 px face = 22-26. Both frames converge on 26 +/- 3 per face, which over the 3.10 m battened face is 0.119 m. The bright bar occupies 55-60% of each period in both frames, so the batten face is 0.070 m and the gap 0.049 m; depth 0.050 m. This retires BOTH round-one screens: 40 at 0.13 across a 5.2 m face, and 66 at 0.050 across a 3.30 m face.
battens.facesNote: Both gable ends, both side walls AND the roof planes are the same batten screen. Roof battens run parallel to the ridge at the same 0.119 m pitch down each slope — the arbitrated pitch, not the round-one 0.050 m, which was a scan across both visible faces of the cube attributed to one.

figures.pitch: [measured] 0.119 m — 26 battens over the 3.10 m battened face. FFT/autocorrelation at five scan heights on each SWA-23 face returns 24-26 cycles, a direct peak read gives 11.83 px, and phf44's profile gives 8.83 px over a 233 px face. See derivation.
figures.face: [measured] 0.070 m — the bright bar occupies 55-60% of each period in both frames, so face = 0.58 x pitch.
figures.depth: [measured] 0.050 m — the batten's projection off the frame, read in the same profiles as the gap between bars.
figures.perFace: [measured] 26 per face, the count both frames converge on at +/- 3. The gate asserts battenedFace / pitch rounds to it and that the module builds 4 x 26.

glow.note: A warm LED source inside the cavity back-lights the battens so the whole cube glows through the slots at night. That glow is the object's entire identity after dark and a build that omits it fails the frame. Built as an emissive core inside the batten screen, not as a light, and STANDING ON THE BENCH: its foot is exactly the bench top, so it rests on the bench instead of passing through it, and in plan it stops one bench depth short of the batten inner face on every side, so no face of it is ever inside a solid.

figures.core: [derived] the clear cavity the screen encloses above the bench. In plan it is twice (cube.size/2 - battens.depth/2 - bench.depth) = 2 x (1.70 - 0.025 - 0.55) = 2.25 m: the battens' own inner face set back by one bench depth, which is the L-bench's own reach on the two closed sides, applied on all four so that a centred core stays square. In section it is cube.eave - bench.seatHeight = 3.65 - 0.44 = 3.21 m: it starts at the bench top, because below that the bench itself blocks the light, and stops at the eave, because above that the roof planes take over. THIS REPLACES the round-one 2.6 x 1.5 x 2.6 m core, which was carried unchanged through the cube's re-measurement and then intersected BOTH legs of the L-bench by 0.140 m; the gate re-derives both numbers and separately checks in 3D that the core enters neither bench leg.
figures.centreHeight: [derived] bench.seatHeight + core[1]/2 = 0.44 + 1.605 = 2.045 m above the plinth — the centre of the core the figure above derives, standing with its foot exactly on the bench top. The round-one 1.05 m did not reproduce its own stated arithmetic (0.44 + 0.75 = 1.19) and belonged to a core height that no longer exists.

poleLight.note: Luminaire family L1b: the college's secondary pedestrian post-top, slim round pole with a small square top-mounted head on a round concrete base (SWA-23, SWA-14, phf22). It ships at that section's L1b dimensions rather than this frame's own read, so the same product is one size across the college; eighthsiteworks.systems.l1bPole.items is empty by the arbitration's instruction, so this position is not a duplicate today, and `absent` records what has to happen if that list is ever populated.

It stands at the measured gap's east limit, where the cobble bed stops and courtyard-1159's east lobe begins, and runs the length of the bed clipped to the surveyed courtyard. Its section is the college's one guardrail product: specOwner eighthsiteworks.systems.guardrail, and every dimension is that spec's, not a fresh read.

The 0.55 x 0.15 m this section shipped is that step rounded.
figures.rail.x: [measured] -82.6, the easternmost extent of the measured gap — the point where the cobble bed stops and courtyard-1159's east lobe, the upper terrace SWA-23 shows the rail standing on, begins. RE-DERIVED: round one put the rail at -83.6 and called that 'the measured boundary'. It is not a boundary at all — the gap's east edge is a curve running from -83.44 to -82.68 and back to -83.59 over the rail's own z-run, so -83.6 stood INSIDE the cobble bed for two thirds of the run and outside it for the rest, which is 22 of 36 pickets buried under this section's own decal and the other 14 on bare ground.
figures.rail.z0: [derived] 572.988 — where the line x = -82.6 crosses INTO courtyard-1159, computed from the shipped ring. The bed's own north limit is 571.70, but the 1.29 m of rail north of 572.988 would stand on no surveyed ground at all, so the survey clips it. The gate re-derives the crossing from campus-eighth.json.
figures.rail.z1: [measured] 576.400 — the measured gap's own south limit, so the rail runs exactly the length of the bed it edges. Round one shipped 577.6, which is 1.2 m past the end of the thing it claims to be the boundary of.
figures.rail.height: [sourced] 1.067 m (42 in) — the canonical guard height for Eighth, owned by eighthsiteworks.systems.guardrail and the exact metric equivalent of the 2022 CBC s1015.3 dimension the product is built to. Four independent photographic reads across this college bracket it (1.06 / 1.066 / 1.067 / 1.07). This rail is the SAME product as every other guard in the college and now ships at the same size; the round-one 1.05 m was that value 'read a little lower at this distance', which is an impression, not a measurement.
figures.rail.picket: [sourced] 0.019 m (3/4 in round tube) — the canonical Eighth picket, owned by eighthsiteworks.systems.guardrail and INHERITED here rather than re-read, so the college ships one guardrail product at one size. The spec owner derives it from a scale-free ratio: solid fraction (picket width / pitch) reads 0.18 +/- 0.02 on its own guardrail crops, 0.18 x 0.1016 = 0.0183 m, and 3/4 in is the product step that lands on. Chased through specOwner; this section declares no frame of its own for it and does not cite one. The round-one 0.028 m was this figure 'read heavier at this distance', which is an impression, not a measurement.
figures.rail.pitch: [sourced] 0.1016 m (4 in) — the canonical Eighth picket pitch, owned by eighthsiteworks.systems.guardrail and INHERITED here rather than re-read. It is the direct expression of the CBC 2022 s1015.4 102 mm sphere rule, which needs no photograph to establish, and the spec owner measured 0.1046 +/- 0.005 m on its own guardrail crops. Clear opening 0.1016 - 0.019 = 0.0826 m, inside the 102 mm rule. The round-one 0.11 m was this figure 'read wider at this distance'.

courtStair.label: The stair south of the basketball court — the BUILT element that replaces the invented 'amphitheatre' tiers.
courtStair.anchor: measured.courtStair — the 2025 plan rectangle, clipped by arcgis.ground#1760
courtStair.retires: SOURCE CONFLICT, declared and resolved on epoch. The 2021 DESIGN plan draws a zigzag tiered edge east of the basketball court and the eighth section built three amphitheatre-tier items from it (x -161.8..-159.8, z 516..533). The 2025 BUILT plan draws no zigzag and no tier run there — that area is a narrow diagonal hatched edge strip consistent with arcgis.ground#2144 (x -158.9..-156.7, z 514.3..535.0, 16.7 m2), a planting/retaining edge — and SWA-16 photographs the whole court in clean sunlight with nothing tiered east of it. Two epochs; the newer one wins on existence. The tiers are retired (see `supersedes`) and what actually stands south of the court is built instead.

stair.derivation: The 2025 registered plan draws the stair as a band of 5-6 parallel lines over x -178.5..-172.0, z 534..538; SWA-16 resolves SEVEN risers. 4.0 m of run over 7 gives a 0.57 m tread at a 0.155 m riser, a 1.09 m total rise. The west edge is clipped from -178.5 to -177.8 by planting-bed-1760's measured east edge, so the shipped stair is 5.8 m wide, not 6.5.

landing.note: The Pulse massing ring's north face is at z 538.1 and the top nosing is at z 538.0, so a 0.10 m landing lip closes the stair against the building rather than stopping in mid-air.

cheek.note: A raking cheek wall each side, stepping with the treads and standing 0.12 m proud of the nosing line — real stair construction, and it is what keeps the flight from reading as floating slabs.

handrail.note: A stainless pipe handrail on a MID-RUN standard (SWA-16) — two end standards and one intermediate, which is exactly what the photograph shows.

courtStair.epochWarning: THE 'SMOOTH LIDAR SO NO STEPS' ARGUMENT IS VOID HERE. campus-eighth.js and campus-eighth-furniture.js both withhold every stair, terrace, retaining wall and seat wall on it. The 2014 LiDAR over Eighth describes a demolished parking lot; the site is demonstrably terraced (EYRC phf03's full exterior stair with stainless handrails, SWA-7 and SWA-16's stepped seating terraces, SWA-12's retaining walls and ramp, phf47/48's LED-lit stepped seat edges, phf22's ramped walk with picket rail). bbq.label: The BBQ / fire-feature terrace, on the surveyed courtyard north of Pulse Tower.
bbq.frameNote: Every position below is a LOCAL (u, v) in the measured terrace frame — u along courtyard-2375's own north-east edge, v across it into the courtyard. World = origin + u*(cos r, -sin r) + v*(sin r, cos r) with r = 0.36. Local coordinates are the [estimated] arrangement; the frame they sit in is measured, and every one of them is verified inside the surveyed ring.
bbq.unifiedNote: SOURCE CONFLICT, declared. The shipped eighth section puts the linear fire feature and four Adirondacks at (-112.5, 570.4) on courtyard-2369 and the grill counter at (-132.05, 531.12) on courtyard-2375 — two [estimated] placements 25 m apart. SWA image 14 photographs the fire feature, the Adirondacks, the conical planters, the grill counter AND the red extinguisher post in ONE frame, so they are one terrace. A sourced adjacency beats two independent guesses: the fire-feature population is brought onto courtyard-2375 with the grills, and the grills do not move because their arrangement is the one crop_grill.png shows.

arrangement.extendsPattern: the photographed adjacency of SWA image 14 and crop_grill.png — which objects stand beside which, and in what order along the terrace — carried onto the measured courtyard-2375 frame, whose origin and bearing ARE surveyed
arrangement.note: EVERY (u, v) AND EVERY rot IN THIS TERRACE IS [estimated]. Nothing registers the furniture to the surveyed ring: the ESRI z20 ortho has the whole terrace in deep afternoon shadow, the 2025 plan draws no furniture, and SWA-14/17/18 offer no landmark that both frames share. What IS sourced is the adjacency — the fire feature with its two arcs of Adirondacks and three drink tables, the grill counter with the extinguisher at its west end, the cafe-table run with its wire chairs, the picnic tables with their sage chairs, the plank benches, the conical-planter row along the back, the canopy, the service enclosure with its mural, and the stair leaving east. The subsystem DIMENSIONS are separately tiered per figure; only the positions are estimated.
arrangement.solve: SEPARATION SOLVE, not a hand arrangement. Every loose object's oriented footprint in this frame is checked pairwise against every other and against the fixed pieces (counter, fire wall, canopy posts, enclosure, stair); any pair whose minimum-overlap axis penetrates by more than `separation` (0.05 m) is a defect and the arrangement is moved along that axis until it is not, preserving the photographed adjacency and the row spacings. The gate re-runs the same SAT check over the shipped numbers, so the solve cannot rot. This replaces the round-one arrangement, in which 26 pairs interpenetrated by up to 0.79 m — a chair inside a planter — while every figure was stamped `measured`.
arrangement.tuckNote: THE ONE DECLARED EXEMPTION, and it is a vertical argument, not a licence. These eight chairs are tucked under their cafe table, which is what SWA-14 shows and what a cafe table is for. Their footprints overlap the table's by 0.099 m and NOTHING of the two objects meets in 3D: the chair's seat tops out at seat + slab = 0.48 m and the table top's underside is at height - 0.05 = 0.68 m, so `tuckClear` = 0.20 m of clear air separates them; and the chair's tall members — the two back legs that run to 0.82 m and the back slats welded to them — stand on the chair's local -v side, which is the side AWAY from the table, because each chair is rotated to face the table it is tucked under. The gate checks all three of those facts for every pair named here rather than taking the exemption on trust. No other pair on this terrace is exempt, and the canopy roof and the mural are excluded from the footprint check because they are overhead and wall-mounted respectively.

figures.separation: [derived] 0.05 m. The gate's own tolerance: any pair of oriented footprints on this terrace whose minimum-overlap axis penetrates by more than this is a defect. It is the drawing tolerance the bark decal's 0.02 m inset is set at, doubled, because two solids need more clearance than a decal edge.
figures.tuckClear: [derived] 0.20 m. Not a chosen figure: it is cafeTables.height - 0.05 (the top slab's underside, 0.68 m) minus wireChairs.seat + 0.03 (the seat slab's top, 0.48 m). The gate recomputes it from those declared figures rather than trusting the number here.

ORPHANED AND BURIED. The shipped ramp-light-edge runs (-177.6, 584.2) to (-177.6, 591.8) — 7.6 m straight down the middle of this section's measured Meditation Pavilion footprint (roof.rect x -181.6..-168.1, z 584.3..591.6), so it would ship UNDERNEATH the pavilion deck for its full depth. It is sourced to phf47 as 'a ramp with a continuous linear light strip under its rail', read at ~14 m in the photo and then 'fitted to the surveyed spine at 7.6 m' — i.e. its length was cut in half to make it fit the spine, which is the surveyed opening this section measures at 14.9 x 7.9 m and fills with the pavilion. This section's deck edge carries the same photographed light line as 20 in-grade uplights at 1.8 m centres, measured at 0.16 m diameter (15 px at 95 px/m in phf47), which is the object phf47 actually resolves.

ORPHANED BY THE RELOCATION. The shipped cluster is five boulders on a 2.6 m radius at (-144.5, 595.5), placed around the shipped tea house — which this section moves 57 m east onto the surveyed gap in courtyard-1159. Left in place it would be five boulders standing in the western Ramble around nothing, and the ground it stands on is eighthramble's. This section ships the setting the relocated object actually has: six boulders read in SWA-23, every one verified inside courtyard-1159.

ORPHANED BY THE RELOCATION, AND WRONG IN MATERIAL. The shipped patch is a 5.1 x 7.6 m rectangle at x -145..-139.9, z 594.2..601.8 drawn around the shipped tea house's old position; the object moves 57 m east, so the patch would be a bare gravel rectangle in the western Ramble with nothing in it. It is also angular gravel where SWA-23 shows rounded 40-80 mm cobble. Replaced by this section's cobble bed, which is CLIPPED to the measured gap polygon rather than drawn as a free rectangle.

absent: The three LED-lit stepped seat edges west of the Meditation Pavilion. MEASURED — three risers at 0.15 m with a ~0.60 m tread, counted in both phf47 and SWA-21, the 0.45 m total being exactly the deck height they climb to. Withheld on arithmetic: the measured spine opening is 7.90 m deep, the roof alone is 7.30 m, and a 1.80 m step run does not fit beside it. SWA-21 reads them running the full width of the Bamboo Garden, which would put them across courtyard-328 and courtyard-329, and no source gives the line. Better absent than a 30 m invented terrace edge.

The Meditation Pavilion's roof PITCH as a number. SWA-3's hip and ridge creases prove it is hipped; 10 deg is shipped as [estimated] inside the 8-12 deg band the creases support. No rung resolved it. The CEQA/EIR record at ceqanet.lci.ca.gov/2016111019 is the unexplored source that would close this and the soffit height together.

A second source for the pavilion's 2.08 m clear soffit. It rests on one ratio (198 px : 81 px) in one frame and 2.08 m is low for a covered space; the frame supports 1.95-2.20 m. No planning document, drawing or archive reached gives a pavilion section.

The Meditation Pavilion's third lobe as a measured object. Three lobes are evidenced (three oculi in SWA-3, three chained circles on the 2021 plan) but only two are measurable in phf47's elevation, so the west drum's 3.2 m diameter and its 2.2 x 0.9 m oculus ship [estimated], extending the two measured 4.3 m drums. No frame shows the third chamber from inside, and the 2021 plan's third circle could alternatively be a small entry lobe.
The Tea House interior beyond the L-shaped bench. SWA-23 and phf45 show only the bench and the glowing batten cavity.

The Tea House's rotation about its vertical axis as a sourced number. The 2025 plan's highlight is a pentagon and fixes position and rough extent, not a bearing; the shipped rotation is the measured gap's own centreline axis, labelled [estimated].

A third grill bay. Exactly two are photographed in crop_grill.png; SWA-14 shows the counter and the red extinguisher post but not the bays, so it does not change the count. The shipped instruction stands.

The multi-stem trees in the conical precast planters. SWA-14 shows them; campus-trees.js owns trees from a measured source and this project's rule for Eighth is that the correct tree work is subtractive. The planters ship with their soil surface only rather than putting a second tree population on one ground.
The second fire feature, the one under the covered arcade in SWA-17. It is real and it is photographed, but no source registers the arcade it stands in to this frame.

The BBQ terrace's position as a SURVEYED fact. courtyard-2375 is a real surveyed ring and everything here is verified inside it, but nothing ties the furniture arrangement to that polygon: the ESRI World Imagery z20 ortho has the whole area in deep afternoon shadow (usable only north of z~526), the 2025 plan draws no furniture, and SWA-14/17/18 give no landmark that registers. The repo's existing anchor is unrefuted and still unconfirmed. EVERY (u, v) AND EVERY rot ON THIS TERRACE IS THEREFORE [estimated], and they are owned in one place, bbq.arrangement, which also carries the separation solve that fixes the spacings. Round one stamped the same positions `measured` at 0.5 m round numbers and shipped 26 solid-solid intersections inside them.

The basketball court's own corrections — RESOLVED BY SIBLINGS, RECORDED HERE. SWA-16 falsified three shipped claims and all three are now owned elsewhere: EIGHTH_COLORS.courtKey #2f372f ('OLIVE/khaki, not UCSD gold') and courtLogo #576564 ('pale sage bone') are shadowed Apple samples, and the arbitrated sunlit values are courtSurface #404a5b, courtKey (the lanes' UCSD gold) #cf9443 and courtTrident #e1c44b, measured by ratio to the court's own white linework and carried by eighthsiteworks.colors and eighthcourtyards.colors; campus-eighth-court.js's absent entry 'no frame resolves a backboard, rim or pole' is falsified and the standards are built by eighthsiteworks.systems.courtHardware. NONE OF IT IS BUILT HERE and this section still does not write campus-eighth.json or campus-eighth-court.js. Kept in the record so the provenance chain is unbroken.

The clipped hedge row on its low retaining wall beside the court, the orange calisthenics rig, and the tan-brick Parking Elevator block — ALL THREE ARE NOW BUILT BY eighthcourtyards (court.hedge, calisthenics and parkingElevator), which owns the court-side hardscape. They are legible in SWA-16 and they are court-side structures rather than gathering places, so they are out of this section's remit but no longer out of the model. Named here so the hand-off is on the record rather than reading as an open gap.

The court's north edge wall/fence. The 2025 plan draws a long hatched linear bar at z 514-515.5, x -189.5..-160.5 which is the court's north edge, NOT seating as the amphitheatre reading assumed. It belongs to the court module.

Plant species as species. Sea lavender, deergrass, the clipped evergreen mounds and the clumping bamboo are all visual identifications at MEDIUM confidence or below, and SWA publishes only 'native and climate-adapted planting' — no schedule exists publicly. Only the rushes and the agaves ship here, and both ship as generic clump and rosette forms rather than named species.
Interior fit-out of either pavilion beyond what is photographed — the tea house's cavity above the bench, and anything in the meditation chambers other than the bench, the stone and its gravel ring.

A morning ortho of the southern two-thirds of Eighth. Everything south of z~526 is in tower shadow in the ESRI z20 capture and Google's z20 tiles over Eighth are STILL mid-construction (bare graded earth, tower cores, no landscape) — the repo's epoch rule confirmed first-hand rather than inherited. Any future pass needing footprints in the Bamboo Garden, the Ramble or the Backyard needs a different capture.

THE ANGULAR CONCRETE PLATE PAVING MOSAIC. Real and photographed from above in SWA -12, but it has no registered extent. It was clipped to arcgis.ground#2369 in this section's first draft; that is wrong three ways — arcgis.ground[3632] hole 176 punches #2369 out of the campus paved-surface survey as an exact 7-vertex, 351.6 m2 match (bbox delta 0.00 m), the SDAF OH! San Diego 2025 plan prints 'The Sun Lawn' inside that same ring, and ESRI orthoimagery registered sub-metre to the surveyed court shows one uniform mown lawn edge to edge. This section's own bbq.anchor is arcgis.ground#2375, 13 m away, which the paving survey does NOT punch out and which this section already surfaces as 0.30 x 0.60 m running-bond unit pavers from SWA -14. No frame ties the mosaic to a surveyed polygon, so it stays absent. Better absent than wrong.

THE TEA HOUSE ROOF'S RIDGE BEARING. That the top edge is not level is agreed by both frames and the 0.5 m rise across the cube is measured, so ridgeFrac 0.62 ships with the corrected eave 3.65 and ridge 4.18. WHICH WAY THE RIDGE RUNS IS NOT RESOLVED: SWA -23 puts the high point at the cube's near corner but clips the top of the object at image row 0, and EYRC phf44 puts the high point at the left edge of the west face and falls monotonically to the right. The two frames disagree about the direction and no other rung in the set fixes it, so the bearing is not stamped measured. Better absent than wrong.

SITE LIGHTING ON THE BBQ TERRACE — HANDED OVER, not withheld. This section shipped four 4.5 m poles, two 6.0 m poles and six bollards on courtyard-2375 at hand-set 0.5 m round coordinates, every one of them stamped measured with no derivation. eighthsiteworks owns the college's whole luminaire schedule after arbitration (L1 pedestrian post-top at a fitted 5.75 m, L2 at 7.0 m, the 0.91 m bollard), and its L1 item list already carries l1-11 at (-128.11, 528.77) and l1-12 at (-142.30, 535.92) — both anchored to courtyard-2375, i.e. this terrace. Two pole families on one ring is a double count, so this section builds none and instead keeps its furniture clear of those two positions; the clearance is gated.

BIKE PARKING ON THE BBQ TERRACE — HANDED OVER. This section shipped two runs of five inverted-U hoops at a 0.75 m pitch on courtyard-2375. eighthsiteworks.systems.bikeRack.ranks[0] `rack-swa4` is the same rank on the same surveyed ring — four galvanised hoops at (-127, 532), rotY -0.3796, at the arbitrated 0.762 m APBP module — and it is the one with a photographed frame behind it (SWA -4). This section builds no bike parking and keeps its furniture clear of that rank instead; the clearance is gated.

WHITE PRECAST PLANTER CUBES ON THE BBQ TERRACE — WITHDRAWN. This section shipped four ~1.0 m white cubes on courtyard-2375 citing EYRC phf22. phf22 is the RAMBLE / Sun Lawn edge, not this terrace: it shows the pale precast box that arbitration measured at 1.8 x 1.8 x 1.15 m with a sunlit albedo of #a49f8b and gave to eighthramble.systems.planterCubes. No frame in this set puts a planter cube inside courtyard-2375, and the 1.0 m size was a round number with no derivation. Better absent than wrong.

THE CHARCOAL PLANTER CUBES IN THE BAMBOO GARDEN — HANDED OVER. This section shipped two 1.2 m cubes fitted into the measured throats where courtyard-328 and courtyard-329 close to ~1.5 m. The cubes are real, but they are the same family eighthcourtyards.bambooGarden.planterCubes counts TWELVE of in SWA -3, at a size measured against people sitting on the rims (1.60 x 1.60 x 0.90 m) rather than fitted to a gap. Two owners on one island is a double count and the two sizes disagree; the throat fit is offered to that owner and nothing is built here.

THE BAMBOO ITSELF, AND ALL OTHER BAMBOO GARDEN PLANTING. This section owns only the Meditation Pavilion and the bark field inside the measured spine opening between courtyard-328 and courtyard-329; the garden island around it (arcgis.ground[3632] hole ring 193, 792.3 m2) is eighthcourtyards.bambooGarden, which ships its raked-gravel floor, its twelve planter cubes and their shrubs and holds itself out of this section's bark rect by name. So the absence of bamboo here is an ownership boundary, not a species judgement — and the species judgement stands too: the clumping bamboo is a MEDIUM-confidence genus read with no species, the same bar that keeps the agave a generic rosette.

A BUILT MEANS OF ACCESS ONTO THE MEDITATION PAVILION DECK. The deck stands 0.45 m above the bark field and this section builds no step onto it. The photographed access is the three LED-lit seat steps of absent[0], which are measured (3 x 0.15 m risers, ~0.60 m tread — exactly the deck height) and which do not fit: the measured spine opening leaves 0.70 m of clear width west of the roof and a run of steps needs 1.80 m. A step invented anywhere else on the perimeter would be a guess about which side people climb, and the 2025 plan's marker does not resolve it. The deck therefore ships as a plinth with a 0.45 m face all round and no access, which is the honest state of the sources; it is the one place in this section where a treated object is knowingly incomplete, and it is recorded here rather than papered over.

THE COLLEGE LUMINAIRE SCHEDULE IS eighthsiteworks', AND THIS SECTION KEEPS EXACTLY ONE POLE. Arbitration 2026-08-19 gave every luminaire on the BBQ terrace to eighthsiteworks and parked family L1b with an empty items[]; the tea house's own pole in SWA-23 is an L1b on a Ramble path and is the one this section still builds, because a photographed pole standing four metres from the object is part of the object's frame and withholding it would leave the tea house lit by nothing. It is built at eighthsiteworks' L1b dimensions (4.30 m, 0.09 m shaft, 0.56 x 0.10 m base) so the same product is one size across the college, and it carries specOwner eighthsiteworks.systems.l1bPole. WHAT IS ABSENT is the placement RULE: no source registers L1b positions to the survey, so this is one surveyed-adjacent read and not a schedule. If eighthsiteworks.systems.l1bPole.items is ever populated, this pole must be handed over in the same edit or the college gets two poles in one place.

eighthgathering.envelopeNote: Every solid and every decal vertex this section produces falls inside one of these boxes. They are derived from the surveyed anchor rings plus a declared margin — nothing here is free to wander into a neighbouring college.
eighthgathering.countsNote: What the module must produce, so a silent geometry change cannot pass. The SOURCED counts here are the ones the photographs give: 3 drums and 3 oculi (SWA-3), 3 standing stones (one per chamber), 2 seat pods and 3 slab stones (phf47/SWA-20/21), 26 battens a face x 4 faces = 104 on the tea house (SWA-23 and phf44 re-counted in arbitration: the round-one 66 was a scan across BOTH visible faces), 2 plinth risers, 7 court-stair risers (SWA-16), 2 grill bays (crop_grill.png — and still not three), 9 + 4 Adirondacks, 3 drink tables, 10 wire chairs, 4 cafe tables, 3 plank benches, 5 conical planters (all SWA-14). The rest follow from a sourced module dimension over a measured extent: 22 screen panels at 0.95 m + 0.075 m slot on the three drum arcs the opening rule leaves (the round-one 46 counted 17 phantoms, built by two arcs written on the wrong branch that each spanned more than a full circle and swallowed their own siblings; the gate now re-derives every arc from the rule and refuses an over-full or overlapping one), 66 standing seams at the 0.406 m product width across a 13.5 m plate, 20 in-grade uplights at 1.8 m centres round the deck, 92 eave battens at 0.45 m. The tea house roof battens (30) follow from the corrected 0.119 m pitch over the corrected 3.10 m battened face and the corrected eave 3.65 / ridge 4.18. The shoe blocks are 16, not 20: one block per six battens on four faces is five a face, but a shoe caps a batten base and the corner portal takes the base out of one bundle on each of the two faces it wraps — the four blocks that made 20 stood on the platform IN the doorway, under no batten, with the shoe rail running across the opening beside them. The plate mosaic and its checker infill are GONE: arcgis.ground#2369 is the Sun Lawn and this section paints nothing on it, so there is no `mosaicPlates` count to pin. NO SITE LIGHTING, BIKE HOOPS OR PLANTER CUBES ARE COUNTED HERE: all three families were handed to eighthsiteworks, eighthramble and eighthcourtyards in arbitration 2026-08-19, so poleA/poleB/bollards/bikeHoops/whitePlanterCubes/meditationPlanterCubes are gone from this list and from the module, and the gate asserts the module no longer produces them. SOLIDS AND DRAWS ARE PINNED HERE TOO: 1423 solids in 52 draw calls, so a silent change of geometry fails even where it changes no family count. 1423 is the HONEST figure: with the broken arcs the same module built 1555, of which 132 were exact duplicates standing inside their own siblings, and the gate's old floor of 1500 was a number only those duplicates could reach.

eighthramble.label: The Ramble — Eighth College / Theatre District Living & Learning Neighborhood, the landscape spine
eighthramble.epoch: BUILT CONDITION 2024-2025. SWA Group landscape; HKS design architect with EYRC, Kitchell design-build; construction Jan 2021 - Nov 2023, project complete 2024, photographed 2024-25. The 2020 UC Regents design rendering is a DEAD EPOCH here and nothing is built from it: it draws large pink/orange/purple flowering perennial drifts, mature canopy shade and people sitting on the boulders, and the built photographs show a sparser, younger, more structural rush-and-deergrass matrix with mulch and crushed rock visible between plants and trees at about 0.4 of mature size. Newest epoch wins.
eighthramble.note: INVENTED class, photo-sourced tier. Nothing in this section is a measurement of this campus except the rings under `measured`, which are copied verbatim from the ArcGIS facilities survey. The 2014 LiDAR under this site is a PARKING LOT — it is blind to everything here — so no height, grade or surface below comes from it, and the module never sculpts terrain: everything seats on `surfaceAt` as the drawn ground currently stands. No public planting schedule for this project exists (CEQA 2016111019, both UC Regents packets, plandesignbuild.ucsd.edu, SWA, EYRC and HKS all return nothing), so every species named here is a photograph-morphology read off the 2024-25 built set and is labelled as such. This section is read by nothing measured and is a source for nothing.
eighthramble.confidence: HIGH on the surveyed geometry — the 29 bed rings, the bed-to-bed walk moduli, both bridge footprints and the 1.0668 m (42 in) guard height are computed from campus-arcgis.json and measured against a scaled figure, not estimated. HIGH on the three structural plant masses, the boulder drift language, count band and size distribution. MEDIUM on the accent planting (Baccharis, Dianella, Agave) and on the arroyo braid's stone grading. LOW / UNRESOLVED on: the golden-flowered subshrub's species, the tan-DG vs grey-concrete walk conflict, check-weir dimensions, bed-by-bed species assignment, and any close-range read of the north and south reaches, for which no published photograph exists. The luminaire and bike-rack readings this section used to carry went to eighthsiteworks in the 2026-08-19 arbitration and are no longer claimed here. EVERY SYSTEM WHOSE GEOMETRY IS NOT MEASURED IS NOW LABELLED `estimated` AND NAMES THE PATTERN IT EXTENDS — that retier covers `areaDrains` and `minorFixtures`, whose own colour provenance said the frames resolve them only as a dark rectangle, a grey box and two red verticals.

sources.what: 'a series of stepped basins and bioswales known as The Ramble'; 10 acres, exponential ecology, native and climate-adapted planting, permeable paving.

Near-plan oblique: the braid running the full length of the central reach, the boulder drift as white dots along the swale margin, tan walks against grey plazas, two flush area drains in the invert, the bike-rack run and lamp on the west bridge's landing, three stairs in one frame.

The measurement frame: the crossing figure that sets 0.00688 m/px and gives the 1.066 m guard, the deck edge beam at 0.28 m, the picket band whose FFT closes on 0.108 m pitch, the one photographed check weir under the bridge, Agave in the wash, Verbena in the foreground.

Midday, neutral: three sunlit boulder colour medians, the deergrass spike mass at the right edge, Juncus with rust-orange lateral seed clusters at 1x, the tan stucco wall behind the stair, the 6.1 m lamp against an adult figure.

The definitive boulder-drift frame (14+ legible in one bed, none showing a ground gap or under-shadow), the 8-unit P-loop bike-rack run scaled off a 700c wheel, the mulch shadow line at the walk lip, the grey broom-finished concrete walk that conflicts with SWA -9.
Midday, neutral light: the tan decomposed-granite loop walk west of Sankofa, sampled sunlit and in shade; Juncus masses; Agonis and Platanus at built size.

The Ramble and Sun Lawn at eye level: the full-height elevation of luminaire family A, the funnel-head family B beside it, the planter cubes, a bike-rack run, the ramped walk with a picket guard, the golden-flowered subshrub at 7x.

The Tea House setting at close range: the crushed rock resolved as FLAT-FACED ANGULAR stones, not rounded river cobble; the blue-grey Juncus form beside the green one; Baccharis mounds, Dianella strap-leaf fans and Agave rosettes in the wash; the bark mulch shreds.
The Tea House from the second side; the wash running right up to the board-formed plinth face.

p.2 site plan prints key letter F (THE RAMBLE) in THREE places — a north reach between Pulse and Podemos, the central reach between Sankofa and Azad, and a south reach by the mid-site parking elevator — and supplies the full A-K legend. p.4 is the design rendering this section deliberately does NOT build from.
Team, completion, and the Lawrence Anderson photography credit that dates the built set.
'The Ramble follows historic drainage patterns and links five residential towers'; earth-toned materials referencing La Jolla's coastal cliffs.
2022 California Building Code 1015.4: the 4 in (102 mm) sphere rule, the constraint that closes the picket pitch at 0.108 m given a 0.025 m round tube.

Every ring in `measured` is copied verbatim from ground[] (decimetres / 10). Areas are shoelace, centroids are polygon centroids, and the walk moduli are pairwise polygon-to-polygon minimum distances — all recomputed by tests/campus-photo-eighthramble.test.mjs against this same file.

colorSources.wayfindingDark: [estimated] SWA -5, right of the Tea House: a dark slim rectangular column, no legible face.
colorSources.juncusFoliage: [estimated] Read from the SWA -6 and -9 Juncus masses. Flower and culm interleave at every sampling scale, so a region median returns mud and this is a visual read, not a measurement.
colorSources.juncusSeed: [estimated] The rust-orange lateral seed clusters, read from SWA -6 at 1x and phf44 at 6x. Interleaved with green culms.
colorSources.juncusElkBlue: [estimated] phf44 at 3x shows blue-grey clumps beside green ones in the Tea House reach. No clean sample is possible at that exposure, so this is the green form's read shifted to a blue-grey cast at the same tone, which is the only difference the frame actually supports.
colorSources.muhlenbergiaFoliage: [estimated] The basal blade clump in SWA -6 right edge and SWA -13: fine, grey-green, and distinctly greyer than the Juncus beside it. Visual read.
colorSources.muhlenbergiaSpike: [measured] Median over SWA -6 (1700,380)-(1900,470), the tawny spike mass at the right edge. Note this is markedly LESS saturated than the shipped eighth.colors.grassStraw #c9c05a, which this section supersedes for the Ramble.
colorSources.verbenaFlower: [estimated] Read from the SWA -5 foreground and SWA -6 lower-left masses. A region median returns mud because flower and foliage interleave at every pixel scale sampled.
colorSources.verbenaFoliage: [estimated] The fine ferny grey-green mound under the umbels, same frames.
colorSources.goldenRaceme: [estimated] EYRC phf22 at 7x — dense golden-yellow terminal racemes in bloom September 2024. Visual read; the plant's own species is unresolved.
colorSources.goldenFoliage: [estimated] The small crowded linear dark-green leaves under those racemes, same crop.
colorSources.baccharisFoliage: [estimated] phf44 at 3x — very fine bright-to-dark green mounds in the crushed-rock wash. Visual read.
colorSources.dianellaLeaf: [estimated] phf44 at 3x — a stiff blue-grey fan of flat strap leaves, distinct in the same frame from the round-culmed Juncus beside it.
colorSources.agaveLeaf: [estimated] phf44, SWA -5, -6, -8 — an open blue-green rosette, consistent with 'Blue Glow' or A. desmettiana.
colorSources.agaveMargin: [estimated] The pale-to-red leaf margin on the same rosettes; the single feature that makes the genus legible at this distance.

measured.note: ANCHORED TO THE ARCGIS FACILITIES SURVEY, NOT TO OSM. campus-3d.json's simplified OSM rings for Sankofa, Azad, Pulse and Podemos cover seven of these beds between them; the ArcGIS survey does not — no bed vertex here falls inside any TDLLN massing ring. The Ramble's beds are not drawn objects: they are literal HOLES punched in one campus-wide walk multipolygon (arcgis.ground[3632], 214 rings). That is why the bed-to-bed gaps ARE the paved widths with zero inference, and why the walk strips this section builds are derived from the gaps rather than drawn. Rings are verbatim from campus-arcgis.json (decimetres / 10); areas are shoelace; centroids are polygon centroids.

reaches.note: Three separate reaches, not one corridor — the UC Regents Sept-2020 site plan prints key letter F three times. The central reach is the sourced one: every published close-range photograph of the Ramble is inside it. The north and south reaches have NO close-range photograph in the published set, so their planting extends the central reach's sourced pattern and is labelled [estimated] at the system.

beds.withheldReason: SURFACE WITHHELD, RING VERBATIM. `kind` stays the survey's own letter (green) because it is gated as a verbatim copy of campus-arcgis.json ground[i].k; the withholding is carried by `surfaceWithheld` instead. arcgis.ground#2369 is THE SUN LAWN (SDAF OH! San Diego 2025 plan, label inside the ring; arcgis.ground[3632] hole 176 excludes it from paving; ESRI ortho shows uniform mown turf edge to edge). It is mown turf, not bark mulch and bunchgrass. The ring stays in this list because measured.walkPairs[9,12,13,29,30,35] derive paved gaps from its geometry; only its SURFACE is withheld.

SURFACE WITHHELD, RING VERBATIM. `kind` stays the survey's own letter (green) because it is gated as a verbatim copy of campus-arcgis.json ground[i].k; the withholding is carried by `surfaceWithheld` instead. arcgis.ground#1160 carries TWO surfaces: a mown lawn over its west and centre and decomposed-granite bunchgrass planting over its east arm and south of z 530. Bark mulch and a 0.72 planted fraction over the whole 1,521.9 m2 would turf-over the lawn. The dividing edge is unresolved (see absent), so this bed's SURFACE is withheld. The ring stays in this list because measured.walkPairs[22] derives a paved gap from its geometry.
