bridges.source: [measured] docs/data/campus-arcgis.json ground[4039], 27.6 m² inside an 8.10 x 3.46 m rotating-caliper box = 98% fill, i.e. a true rectangle. Segments 0 (z=613.5, 3.2 m) and 2 (z=605.4, 3.4 m) are the two ends; each carries the guard except a centred 2.40 m opening, which is what leaves the ~0.4-0.5 m return around each end that SWA -5 shows.

[measured] docs/data/campus-arcgis.json ground[2990], 17.9 m² inside a 5.60 x 5.40 m box = 59% box fill. The research inventory read that fill ratio as 'an L or T'; the RING says it is a right TRIANGLE — a 5.60 m south leg along z=602.5, a 5.40 m east leg along x=-142.3, and a north-west hypotenuse. The deck-plus-overlook-landing reading of SWA -2 survives: the landing is the wide south-west half of the triangle. Guarded on the five swale-facing segments (0-4); the hypotenuse (5-9) is the approach off the paving and carries no guard.

measured.massNote: Verbatim from campus-arcgis.json massing[]. A ring is used as a clearance ring only where `clearance` is true, i.e. where it swallows no surveyed ground feature — see the SURVEY-vs-SURVEY entry in `absent`. They are here ONLY as clearance rings — nothing in this section reads their heights, and their `gisHeight` is recorded purely to keep the record honest: for every TDLLN mass except Sankofa Base it is exactly levels x 3.048 m (10 ft), i.e. a FORMULA, not a survey. The 2014 LiDAR has no height for any of them.

clips.why: The east bridge is a NOTCH cut out of planting bed 2703 — the bed's ring runs down x=-128.4 and east along z=603, leaving the bridge outside it. A bounding-box fill of bed 2703 would stand 30-odd plants on the bridge deck. Nothing planted, no boulder and no fixture may fall inside this ring.
The west bridge's triangular deck sits in a notch of planting bed 331 the same way. Same rule.
The surveyed walkway that threads between beds 326, 332 and 324. It is paving, not bed, and carries no planting or boulders.

mulch.label: Shredded bark mulch — the default bed surface
mulch.description: Coarse shredded / gorilla-hair bark mulch, individual ribbon shreds 50-150 mm long and resolvable at eye level. It is the DEFAULT surface of every bed in `measured.beds` except where the arroyo braid replaces it.
mulch.dimensions: 75 mm (3 in) laid depth — the California WELO / LEED standard bed mulch depth, corroborated by the measured 0.05-0.10 m drop from the walk lip visible as a shadow line in SWA -8. Extent = every bed polygon, minus the braid.
mulch.builtNote: `shredLength` DRIVES the mulch decal's world texture tile: campus-materials.js lays barkEucalyptus's peel ribbons at fbm(u, v, 10, 3, 3), i.e. three ribbon lengths down one tile, so a tile of 3 x the 0.10 m mean shred puts a shred on screen at its sourced size. `depth` (0.075 m) and `lipDrop` (0.05-0.10 m) are RECORDED, NOT BUILT, and deliberately so — see absent: a decal on campus-overlay.js's ladder has no thickness, and the ladder's rung spacing is a draw-order device, not a survey of grade.

arroyo.label: The arroyo — a braided ANGULAR crushed-rock wash
arroyo.description: The Ramble's signature surface. phf44 at 3x resolves the individual stones as FLAT-FACED, IRREGULAR, ANGULAR crushed rock — not rounded river cobble — cream / buff with scattered purple-grey and rust pieces. On the ground it is a BRAIDED CHANNEL occupying the swale invert, splitting and rejoining around the boulders. The shipped model reduced this to one 1.8 x 10.1 m rectangle; the rectangle primitive is wrong and is superseded.
arroyo.dimensions: Stone 40-90 mm, mode ~60 mm — measured against the adjoining boulders, whose long axis is scaled to the 1.07 m bridge guard; equals a nominal 2 in / 3 in crushed cobble, the standard bioswale energy-dissipation grading. Braid width meanders 2.0-4.5 m inside the sourced 2-5 m band, over the ~55 m length of the central reach.
arroyo.formNote: [estimated] The braid CENTRELINES are derived, not photographed: each runs the surveyed bed chain of its reach, and every quad the module emits is clipped to a bed polygon, so this system cannot put crushed rock on a walk, on a bridge or outside the survey. It extends the sourced braid pattern read from SWA -2, where the pale braids run the full length of the central reach.
arroyo.builtNote: `stoneMode` DRIVES the wash decal's world texture tile: campus-materials.js lays lavaRock's lumps at fbm(u, v, 12, 12, 4), i.e. twelve stones across one tile, so a tile of 12 x the 0.060 m modal stone puts a stone on screen at its sourced size. `stoneSize` is the band that mode sits in.

dgWalks.label: Tan stabilised decomposed-granite garden-loop walks
dgWalks.description: The Ramble's internal loop walks, built from the surveyed bed-to-bed gaps in the 1.80 m (6 ft) and 2.10 m (7 ft) modular bands. SWA -9, in midday neutral light, shows the walk through the bed west of Sankofa as distinctly tan / buff; SWA -2 shows every walk inside the Ramble reading tan against grey paving elsewhere on site.
dgWalks.dimensions: Width = the surveyed gap, which clusters on 1.76 / 1.78 / 1.80 / 1.83 / 1.84 m and on 2.03 / 2.10 / 2.10 / 2.11 m. Flush concrete or steel edge band 0.10-0.15 m wide on both sides (SWA -8) — `edgeBand` is RECORDED, NOT BUILT, see `absent`: a 0.10 m band on a decal that has no thickness is a colour change with no evidence behind its colour.
dgWalks.widthsNote: `widths` [1.80, 2.10] is not a free figure and is not what the module lays out: it is the list of `measured.walkBands` bands this material is assigned to, and the width of any one walk is the surveyed bed-to-bed gap, recomputed from the rings. It is declared here because it is the load-bearing half of the `conflict` below — the tan-DG / grey-concrete split is made BY THE SURVEYED MODULUS and by nothing else — so the test holds it against `measured.walkBands`: every band whose material is `dg` must appear in this list, and every entry in this list must be such a band. Round one left both width lists unread by anything, which let the split be reassigned without a single gate moving.
dgWalks.conflict: DECLARED, NOT RESOLVED: SWA -8 (evening, warm light) shows a walk through the same landscape that is unmistakably pale grey broom-finished concrete, and the colour difference survives the light difference — SWA -8 is warm light and still reads grey, SWA -9 is neutral light and reads tan. The stronger reading is that TWO materials coexist, so this section splits them by the surveyed modulus: the 1.80 and 2.10 m garden loops are tan DG, the 2.40 m primary through-walks are grey concrete. Nothing in the sources proves that division.
dgWalks.gritSizeSource: [estimated] 3-9 mm, mode ~6 mm. Extends the sourced material identification (stabilised decomposed granite, the standard 3/8 in-minus product these walks are built from): no frame in the set resolves an individual grain, so the grain is taken from the product grading rather than measured. It DRIVES this walk's world texture tile — campus-materials.js scatters decomposedGranite's larger stones at n(u, v, 40, 40), forty across a tile, so the tile is 40 x 0.006 m.

concreteWalks.label: Grey broom-finished concrete through-walks
concreteWalks.description: Cast-in-place grey concrete with tooled transverse score joints, broom finish, carrying the through-routes across the Ramble and the wider paved edge the planter cubes and bike-rack runs stand on. Reads neutral pale grey even under warm evening light.
concreteWalks.dimensions: 2.40 m (8 ft) primary walk; the wide paved band runs 3.9-7.0 m in the survey. Score joints transverse.
concreteWalks.widthsNote: `widths` [2.40, 6] is the other half of the same split — the list of `measured.walkBands` bands assigned to grey concrete, held against that table by the same test as `dgWalks.widths`. 6 is the WIDE PAVED EDGE band, whose own surveyed span is 3.9-7.0 m and whose label is its centre, not a nominal width; the 2.40 m entry is a true 8 ft modulus.
concreteWalks.aggregateSizeSource: [estimated] ~5 mm. Extends the sourced material identification (cast-in-place grey concrete, floated and broom-finished): the mottle a floated slab reads at is its fine aggregate, and 5 mm is the standard pea-gravel top size for a walk mix. It DRIVES this material's world texture tile — campus-materials.js speckles smoothConcrete's aggregate at fbm(u, v, 128, 128, 2), 128 across a tile, so the tile is 128 x 0.005 m. The same tile carries the two bridge decks, which are the same material.

boulders.label: Granite boulder DRIFTS along the slope toes and arroyo margins
boulders.description: Rounded to sub-rounded GRANITE — the weathered exfoliated pillow shape of Peninsular Ranges granodiorite, not angular quarry rubble. They are laid as a DRIFT along the toe of each slope and along the arroyo margins, longest axis roughly parallel to the drift line, at 1.5-4 m spacing, occasionally touching in pairs. NEVER a radial cluster: the shipped model's four radial clusters of 4-6 stones are the wrong form as well as the wrong count.
boulders.dimensions: Long axis 0.6-1.6 m, mode ~1.0 m. Exposed height 0.35-0.80 m, mode ~0.50 m. L : W : exposed H = 1.0 : 0.75 : 0.55. EVERY boulder is set with about a third of its vertical axis below grade — in SWA -8 at 2x no boulder shows a visible ground gap or an under-shadow — so the primitive is a partly-buried ellipsoid whose flat cut is the mulch / gravel line, not a sphere resting on the surface. Scaled against the 1.07 m bridge guardrail in SWA -5 (itself 0.00688 m/px off the crossing figure) and against adult figures in SWA -6 and -8.
boulders.count: 14+ legible in ONE bed in SWA -8; 12+ more in one SWA -6 frame; readable as white dots along the whole swale margin in SWA -2, giving 60-90 over the central reach against the shipped model's ~20 in total.
boulders.drawNote: [measured-consuming] The long axis and the exposed height are drawn on a TRIANGULAR distribution about their own sourced modes — longAxisMode 1.00 m over [0.60, 1.60], exposedHeightMode 0.50 m over [0.35, 0.80] — from ONE uniform variate per stone, so the long stones are also the tall ones. Round one averaged two hashes instead, which is a symmetric draw about the BAND MIDPOINT and put the built medians at 1.100 m and 0.575 m, i.e. exactly the midpoints of [0.60,1.60] and [0.35,0.80] and 10% and 15% off the modes it declared. THE STATISTIC TO CHECK IS THE MODE AND THE MEAN, NOT THE MEDIAN: a triangular draw on a band its mode does not sit in the middle of is skewed, so its median is offset by construction (0.6 + sqrt(0.5 x 1.0 x 0.4) is not 1.0; the closed form gives 1.052 for the long axis and 0.540 for the exposed height, and the build returns 1.049 and 0.539). Its MEAN is (lo + hi + mode)/3 exactly — 1.0667 m and 0.5500 m — and the build returns 1.068 and 0.551 over 128 stones, and its densest 0.10 m / 0.05 m bin is the one centred on the declared mode. Both are gated. The two modes are not in the L : exposed-H = 1.00 : 0.55 ratio measured on individual stones (1.00 x 0.55 = 0.55, not 0.50); the ratio describes one stone and the modes describe the population, so the population statistic drives the draw and proportions[2] stays as the single-stone description it is. proportions[1] (0.75) drives the built width.
boulders.marginOffsetSource: [estimated] The drift stands OFF the channel edge by 0.40-1.20 m. Extends the sourced reading 'linear drifts along the arroyo margins' (SWA -2 down the central reach, SWA -8 at 2x in one bed): no frame gives a measurable stand-off, so the band is derived from the stone itself — the near limit is half a modal long axis (0.50 m) rounded down to 0.40 m, which is the closest a modal stone can sit without its own body overhanging the wash, and the far limit is one modal long axis (1.00 m) plus that same half-stone, at which point a stone reads as scattered in the bed rather than as an arroyo margin. Nothing sourced fixes it more tightly.

planting.label: The planting matrix — three structural masses and an accent layer
planting.mixNote: [estimated] The three structural masses carry >=70% of the planted area (sourced); the split BETWEEN them, and the 28% left as bare mulch and wash, is inferred from the 2024 frames, where mulch and crushed rock are visible between plants in every one. Planting is laid as DRIFTS on a 4 m coarse lattice, not as a shuffled mix, because that is what a planting plan does and what the aerial banding in SWA -2 shows. Bed-by-bed species assignment is NOT possible from the published set — see `absent`.

juncus.spacingNote: 0.60 m (24 in) triangular; clumps touch at 2024 maturity
juncus.diagnostic: The inflorescence is borne LATERALLY about three quarters of the way up a leafless cylindrical culm. No grass does this, which is why the identification is confident even without a schedule — and why the module models the lateral seed cluster rather than a terminal one.
juncus.culmDiameterNote: 7 mm — the culm is round and near-parallel-sided in phf44 at 6x, which is half of why the identification is safe. It DRIVES the built culm's section: the module cylinders it at exactly this diameter. Round one hard-coded radii of 0.0025 and 0.0045 m and left the sourced figure unread.

juncusElkBlue.note: The blue-grey cultivar, identical form and size to the species, used in the Tea House reach — beds 331 and 326, where phf44 at 3x shows blue-grey clumps sitting beside green ones. Built as the same clump geometry in juncusElkBlue.

muhlenbergia.diagnostic: A basal clump of fine grey-green blades with stiff narrow straw-coloured flowering spikes held vertically well ABOVE it; the spike-to-foliage ratio measures 1.5:1. Both parts are modelled — a single cone loses the whole plant.

verbena.taxon: Verbena lilacina 'De La Mina' (Cedros Island lilac verbena)
verbena.diagnostic: Flat-topped umbel-like clusters of small five-lobed lilac flowers held 0.15-0.25 m above a fine ferny grey-green mound, flowering in a September frame. V. bonariensis is EXCLUDED — its clusters ride 1.5 m bare wands.

golden.spacingNote: [estimated] scattered as individuals through the Juncus matrix
golden.diagnostic: FORM FULLY RESOLVED, SPECIES NOT. Upright open broom-like habit 0.9-1.2 m; leaves small, linear, crowded, dark green, 10-20 mm; dense golden-yellow terminal racemes 0.15-0.30 m long, one per branch tip, in bloom September 2024. It is one of the three most conspicuous plants in the corridor and is ABSENT FROM THE SHIPPED MODEL ENTIRELY. Shipped as the form with the taxon marked unresolved rather than omitted; the moment a source names it, only the taxon string changes.
golden.leafLengthNote: `leafLength` 10-20 mm, linear, crowded — RECORDED, NOT BUILT. The module builds this plant as branches and terminal racemes, which is what makes it legible at 40 m; individual 15 mm leaves are below the size at which an instance earns its place, and drawing them would cost more instances than the whole rest of the section. Kept because it is part of the diagnostic that identifies the form.

dianella.extendsPattern: Extends the same subject's sourced planting pattern (the Juncus / Muhlenbergia / Verbena matrix read from SWA -6, -8, -9 and phf44); the form and size are measured off phf44, only the taxon is inferred.
dianella.diagnostic: A stiff blue-grey fan of flat STRAP leaves 8-12 mm wide radiating from a central point — distinct in the same frame from the round-culmed Juncus beside it.

baccharis.extendsPattern: Same sourced matrix; form and size measured off phf44 and SWA -2, taxon inferred.
baccharis.diagnostic: Small dense mounds of very fine foliage, evenly spaced THROUGH THE CRUSHED-ROCK WASH, never in the mulch. Built at the 2024 size (0.5-0.8 m across), not the mature 1.5-1.8 m.
baccharis.matureWidthNote: `matureWidth` 1.5-1.8 m is the PUBLISHED MATURE SPREAD of the taxon, RECORDED AND DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT — the module builds `builtWidth` 0.5-0.8 m, which is what the 2024 frames show, because this planting was two growing seasons old when it was photographed. It is kept because it is the figure that makes the epoch argument checkable: if a later source shows the mounds closed up, the swap is builtWidth -> matureWidth and nothing else moves.

agave.extendsPattern: Same sourced matrix; rosette form and the pale/red margin are measured off phf44 and SWA -5/-6/-8, genus is probable and species is not resolved.
agave.taxon: Agave sp., probably 'Blue Glow' or A. desmettiana
agave.matureSizeNote: `matureSize` 0.6-0.9 m across is the taxon's PUBLISHED MATURE ROSETTE, RECORDED AND DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT, exactly as `baccharis.matureWidth` is: the module builds `builtWidth` 0.35-0.50 m, the size the 2024 frames read at two seasons old. Same epoch argument, same one-field swap if a later frame shows them grown in.
agave.diagnostic: An open rosette of 20-30 straight lanceolate leaves with a pale / red margin and a terminal spine. ALWAYS a single specimen in the crushed-rock wash, never in mulch; ~12 legible in the central reach.
agave.leafRiseNote: 0.55 — the rosette stands 0.55 of its own width tall in phf44 and SWA -5, which is what makes it an OPEN rosette rather than the tight ball of a young Agave. It DRIVES the built leaf angle: a leaf reaching w/2 sideways and 0.55w upward stands at atan(1 / (2 x 0.55)) = 0.738 rad from vertical, and the module spreads its leaves +/- 0.40 rad about that. Round one hard-coded the band 0.35-1.15 rad — whose midpoint is 0.75 rad, so the form was right and the sourced figure that gives it was unread.
agave.countCentralNote: ~12 legible in the central reach in phf44 and SWA -5/-6. This is a COUNT BAND, not a placement: the module latticed the wash at `spacing` and the test checks the built central-reach count against this figure rather than trusting it. Round one declared it and checked nothing.

planting.supersededClaim: This replaces the shipped eighth `grass-field` items, whose own source line says the grasses are 'generic bunch-grass cones, deliberately not an identified species'. That is the exact failure the ultra standard names.
planting.plantedFractionNote: 0.72 is the complement of the `bare` weight in `mix` and must stay so: the mix is the partition that produces it, and the test recomputes 1 - bare rather than trusting this number. It is the sourced '>=70% of the planted area carried by the three structural masses' expressed as the matrix's own planted share.

bridges.label: Two surveyed swale crossings
bridges.description: Flat cast concrete slab decks with a shallow edge beam, guarded on their swale-facing edges. Built from the surveyed rings VERBATIM, not from a span-and-width pair: the shipped ramble-bridge-1 (span 5, width 2.4) and ramble-bridge-2 (span 7, width 3) are both superseded.
bridges.dimensions: Edge beam 0.28 m deep — 40 px in SWA -5 between the deck line and the underside of the fascia at 0.00688 m/px, the scale set by the crossing figure. The shipped `deck 0.25` is 0.03 m shy.
bridges.fasciaSource: [estimated] 0.06 m. The edge beam's DEPTH (0.28 m) is measured in SWA -5; its thickness on the face is not — the fascia is seen edge-on in every frame. 0.06 m extends the same slab: a cast concrete deck's downstand face reads as a thin band against the 0.28 m depth, and 60 mm is the smallest section that will not read as paper at the distance this deck is seen from. Round one carried it as a bare 0.06 in the module.

guardrail.label: The Ramble's universal picket guard
guardrail.description: Vertical round-tube pickets between a larger round top rail and a bottom rail, standing on the bridge deck. Clear-anodised or hot-dip galvanised aluminium, matte cool light grey. The shipped model has no bottom rail.
guardrail.derivation: HEIGHT MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: in SWA -5 the crossing figure stands 240 px crown-to-deck; at 1.65 m for an adult female that is 0.00688 m/px at her depth, and the top rail runs 155 px above the deck at her x, so 155 x 0.00688 = 1.066 m — the 42 in California guard, which is 1.0668 m exactly and is the canonical 1.067 this section now ships. PITCH AND SECTION ARE NOT THIS SECTION'S ANY MORE: an FFT of the picket band over SWA -5 x 1200-1450 gave a projected 10.0 px, and round one rescued that with an INVENTED 50-55 deg obliquity factor to reach 0.108 m at a 0.025 m tube. Both figures are retired — the arbitrated values (0.1016 m pitch, 0.019 m picket, 0.0826 m clear opening) come from a grid-masked autocorrelation of the same frame that this section's FFT could not do, and are owned by eighthsiteworks. See `specOwner`.
guardrail.specOwnerNote: THE GUARD SPEC IS NOT THIS SECTION'S. Height 1.067 m, picket 0.019 m at 0.1016 m centres, 0.0826 m clear opening, top rail 0.048 m and bottom rail 0.033 m are the canonical Eighth values arbitrated 2026-08-19 and owned by eighthsiteworks, which is the only section that models the kerb that carries a rail on a walking surface. This section applies them ONLY to the two surveyed BRIDGE DECKS it builds — the deck is the carrier there, not a kerb, and eighthsiteworks CLIPS both bridges out of its own placer precisely so they are not railed twice. This section's own earlier pitch (0.108 m via an invented 50-55 deg obliquity factor) and picket (0.025 m) are retired.
guardrail.railGeometryNote: [measured-consuming] THE DATUM IS DECK-TO-TOP-OF-RAIL. `height` 1.067 m is measured from the walking surface to the TOP of the top rail, so the rail's CENTRE is one half tube below it (1.067 - 0.048/2 = 1.043 m) and a picket stops one whole tube below it, at the rail's underside (1.067 - 0.048 = 1.019 m). eighthsiteworks, which owns this spec, builds exactly that. Round two placed the rail centre AT 1.067, standing the built guard 1.091 m — 24 mm over the canonical figure — and ran the pickets to 1.067, i.e. 48 mm into the rail's lower half. Both are corrected and both are now gated against the built scene rather than against the declaration.
guardrail.shoesAbsentNote: NO BASE SHOES, RETIRED 2026-08-19. Round two declared `shoeSpacing: 1.5` and `shoe: [0.11, 0.012, 0.11]` and built 37 of them. Not one of the four figures had a source, a derivation, or a mention in `specOwnerNote`, which enumerates the canonical spec as height / picket / pitch / clear opening / top rail / bottom rail and stops. They are deleted rather than re-derived — see `absent`.

checkWeirs.extendsPattern: Extends the ONE weir actually photographed under the SWA -5 bridge along the braid. SWA's own project text names 'a series of stepped basins'; no frame resolves a weir dimension.
checkWeirs.label: Check weirs in the stepped basins
checkWeirs.description: SWA -5 shows, in the swale under the east bridge, a low pale horizontal concrete band running across the channel with crushed rock on both sides — a check weir. Built as a low band across each braid at 12 m intervals, standing `bandProud` above the wash. The sourced 0.20-0.35 m STEP is deliberately not built: a step needs an invert grade, and no source measures one here. The downstream ROCK APRON is not built either — see absent: it is the same 40-90 mm angular crushed rock as the channel it would sit in, so building it would emit geometry indistinguishable from the wash decal already there.
checkWeirs.dimensions: Band 0.35 m across the channel (`bandWidth`), spanning the channel bank to bank, standing 0.04 m proud (`bandProud`). The 8-15 m interval, the band width, the proud height and the 0.20-0.35 m step are all estimated; the only measured fact is that at least one weir exists and spans the channel.
checkWeirs.bandProudSource: [estimated] 0.04 m. Extends the one sourced observation there is — SWA -5 shows 'a LOW pale horizontal concrete band running across the channel' under the east bridge, so the band is proud of the crushed rock (it is legible as a band against it) and far below the 0.20-0.35 m STEP the SWA project text implies, which needs an invert grade nothing measures. It is now the ONLY figure that positions this object: the band is built as a box of 2 x bandProud centred on the wash rung of campus-overlay.js's ladder, so exactly bandProud stands above the wash and the rest is under it. Round one declared this 0 (flush), then stood the band ~0.05 m proud anyway on a local lift constant of 0.02 plus an undeclared 0.06 height — a figure declared and then contradicted by the geometry.
checkWeirs.bandSpanSource: The band spans the channel EXACTLY — SWA -5 shows it running bank to bank — so its built length is the braid's own local half-width x 2 and there is no multiplier. Round one carried an undeclared 2.1x, i.e. a 5% overhang into each bank that no source states.

areaDrains.label: Flush grated area drains
areaDrains.positions: [estimated] at declared fractions along the central braid and on the primary walk — SWA -2 resolves them as rectangles in the invert but cannot be registered to the survey.
areaDrains.description: Rectangular grated area drains set flush in the crushed rock of the swale invert, and a matching type flush in the paving. Dark grey cast-iron or galvanised grate, no raised frame — so no hovering geometry, and the built grate's top is exactly the rung of the surface it sits in.
areaDrains.extendsPattern: EXISTENCE is sourced — SWA -2 at 3x resolves rectangular grates in the swale invert and SWA -14 one flush in the paving — but this section's own colorSources entry says those frames resolve them 'only as dark rectangles', so no dimension is measured off them and the tier is estimated. It extends the standard cast product these are: 0.60 x 0.60 m is the 24 in square catch-basin grate and 0.45 x 0.60 m the 18 x 24 in rectangular one, which are the two sizes a landscape architect specifies for a bioswale invert and a walk respectively. Round one shipped these as `sourced`, which its own colour provenance contradicted.
areaDrains.grateThicknessSource: [estimated] 0.03 m, the standard cast-iron / galvanised grate section. It is the ONLY figure that positions this object vertically: each drain is a slab of exactly this thickness whose TOP sits on the rung of the surface it is set into — the arroyo rung for the two swale drains, the walk rung for the paved one — which is what makes it flush, as the description requires. Round one used an undeclared local lift of 0.005 plus an undeclared 0.05 thickness, so the grate stood 5 mm proud of a surface it says has no raised frame.

planterCubes.label: Precast planter cubes
planterCubes.description: Near-white precast concrete cubes standing on the PAVED edge of the Ramble. The four shipped cubes are corroborated in size but stand at x=-135.5, which is inside planting bed 2703 — a 1.8 m cube in the middle of a rush matrix. They are re-seated here on the surveyed wide paved band, which is the only paving in the survey broad enough to take them. ARBITRATED 2026-08-19: HEIGHT CORRECTED from 0.9 to 1.15 m. In phf22 the box images left edge x 856.3, corner 914.2, right edge 936.7, top y 718.3, bottom 758.3, so its projected plan diagonal is sqrt(57.9^2 + 22.5^2) = 62.1 px against a 40 px height — plan/height = 1.55, not the 2.0 that 1.8 x 1.8 x 0.9 implies. At the corroborated 1.8 m plan that is 1.16 m tall.
planterCubes.note: SWA -14 shows a SECOND, different planter family on the courtyard side — tall tapered round GFRC pots and dark grey square GFRC cubes. That belongs to the courtyard team and is not built here.
planterCubes.spacingSource: [derived] 3.90 m on centre = the 1.80 m cube plus a 2.10 m clear pass. Both terms are this section's own measured figures: the cube's plan dimension is corroborated in phf22, and 2.10 m is the 7 ft walk modulus the ArcGIS survey itself clusters on in `measured.walkBands`, i.e. the clear width this landscape actually uses to walk past something. No frame shows two consecutive cubes with the gap between them, so the on-centre spacing is not measured; it is derived from two figures that are. Round one carried a bare 4.
planterCubes.soilSource: [estimated] The planted mass inside the cube. Extends what phf22 shows — a multi-stem tree standing in a mulched mass that reads level with, and just below, the cube rim. wallThickness 0.12 m is the section a 1.8 m precast planter cube is cast at, so the soil face is inset 0.24 m on each plan axis; soilRecess 0.02 m is the reveal of the rim above the mulch; soilDepth 0.08 m is the visible mulch layer, not the root volume, which is not modelled. Round one carried 0.24, 0.06 and 0.08 as bare numbers in the module with nothing declared.

teaHouseSetting.label: The Tea House setting — the Ramble's contribution to an already-modelled object
teaHouseSetting.description: The Tea House stands IN the crushed-rock wash, which runs right up to the board-formed plinth face. The wash under and around it is Ramble material — the same 40-90 mm angular crushed rock as the arroyo — not a separate 'pale angular gravel', which is what the shipped tea-gravel rectangle implies. The branch braid runs through the Tea House, so the setting needs no separate patch; the shipped rectangle is superseded by the braid.
teaHouseSetting.handoff: The stepped plinth (2 steps, top step ~0.15 m, ~0.30 m total above the surrounding wash) is recorded here for whoever owns the tea-house object — the shipped item carries a single 0.35 m plinth. This section does not touch that object.
teaHouseSetting.builtNote: NOTHING IN THIS BLOCK IS BUILT BY THIS SECTION and that is the point of it: the Tea House object belongs to eighthgathering, and the wash it stands in is already emitted by `systems.arroyo` because the branch braid runs through it. `plinthSteps`, `plinthTopStep` and `plinthTotal` are a HANDOFF and are RECORDED, NOT BUILT — they describe eighthgathering's object, and this section would be reaching into another agent's system if it drew them. Round one also carried a `washReach: 0`, a zero-valued field that encoded 'no separate patch is needed' as a dimension; it is deleted rather than left to be read as a measurement of nothing.

minorFixtures.label: Minor site fixtures observed in the Ramble

utilityCabinet.source: SWA -4 right — a grey utility / valve cabinet on the walk edge.
utilityCabinet.sizeSource: [estimated] 0.90 w x 1.10 h x 0.60 d. Extends the standard pad-mounted landscape utility enclosure — a 36 x 44 x 24 in NEMA 3R cabinet, which is the size an irrigation controller and its valve manifold take. The frame gives the family and the colour, not the dimension.

fdcBollard.source: SWA -2 and -14 — red fire-department-connection bollards on the paved edges.
fdcBollard.sizeSource: [estimated] 0.20 m diameter x 1.00 m above grade. Extends the standard protective bollard the fire-department connection stands in: a 6 in Sch.40 pipe sleeved to about 8 in (0.20 m) finished, set 1.0 m proud, which is the ordinary California FDC-guard dimension. The frames give two red verticals, not a diameter.

wayfindingColumn.source: SWA -5, right of the Tea House — a freestanding dark slim rectangular wayfinding / blue-light column at the Ramble edge.
wayfindingColumn.sizeSource: [estimated] 0.34 w x 2.40 h x 0.16 d. Extends the standard freestanding campus wayfinding / blue-light column: 2.40 m is the height at which a slim column carries a legible map panel above a crowd and is the common product step, and 0.34 x 0.16 m is the panel-and-post section that carries it. THIS FIGURE IS ALSO THE HOVER CEILING for the whole section — it is the tallest object the Ramble now builds, since the luminaires went to eighthsiteworks — so the test pins it rather than reading it, or the ceiling could be raised by the very thing it bounds.

minorFixtures.positionNote: [estimated] Each family's EXISTENCE is sourced; no dimension is, and none of the three can be registered to the survey — so each is seated on a declared walk-strip centreline at a deterministic fraction along it, which guarantees it stands on paving and not in a bed.
minorFixtures.extendsPattern: EXISTENCE is sourced — each of the three is plainly in a named frame — but this section's own colorSources entries say those frames resolve the cabinet 'only as a grey box', the FDC 'only as red verticals' and the wayfinding column with 'no legible face', so NO DIMENSION here is measured and the tier is estimated. Each family extends the standard product it obviously is, recorded per family in its own `sizeSource`. Round one shipped the geometry as `sourced` while its colour provenance said the opposite; that contradiction is what this retier fixes.

supersedes.why: Its own source line says the grasses are 'generic bunch-grass cones, deliberately not an identified species'. Replaced by Juncus patens, Muhlenbergia rigens and Verbena lilacina modelled as plants, each with a diagnostic feature (the lateral inflorescence, the 1.5:1 spike-to-foliage ratio, the flat-topped umbels above a ferny mound), and by a drift layout on the surveyed bed polygons rather than a rectangle.
Same failure, and its extent was a rectangle fitted by eye through beds 332 and 331; the replacement runs the surveyed bed rings and carries the same three taxa as drifts.

Same failure, on a 11.6 x 3.1 m rectangle spanning the gap between beds 364 and 2703 — a strip of grass laid across what the survey says is paving. The replacement cannot cross a walk because it is clipped to the bed rings.
A 15.6 x 7.1 m rectangle standing in for a bed. The mulch field now runs every surveyed bed polygon minus the braid, at the sourced 75 mm depth with the measured walk-lip drop recorded.
Same: a 7.1 x 2.1 m rectangle standing in for part of bed 410. The mulch field now runs the ring.

A 1.8 x 10.1 m rectangle for the arroyo. phf44 at 3x resolves it as a BRAIDED channel of flat-faced angular crushed rock 40-90 mm that splits and rejoins around the boulders and runs the full ~55 m of the central reach; the rectangle primitive is wrong.
Modelled as a separate 'pale angular gravel around the tea house'. phf44 and phf45 show the Tea House standing IN the Ramble's own wash, which runs to the plinth face; the branch braid carries it.

A radial cluster of 4 stones on a 3 m radius. SWA -8 at 2x and SWA -6 show LINEAR DRIFTS along the slope toes and arroyo margins, 60-90 in the central reach alone, every one bedded a third into the ground with no visible ground gap. Radial clusters are the wrong form as well as an 4x under-count.
Same form and count correction: a radial cluster of 4 on a 2.5 m radius beside bed 332, replaced by drifts down both arroyo margins.
Same: a radial cluster of 5 on a 3 m radius beside bed 364.
Same: a radial cluster of 6 on a 3.5 m radius beside bed 353.
Same form correction in the Tea House reach: a radial cluster of 5 becomes part of the continuous drift down the branch braid that runs past the Tea House plinth.

Modelled as a 5 x 2.4 m rectangle 'shortened to fit' walkway-2990. The survey's own ring is a right TRIANGLE — 5.60 m south leg, 5.40 m east leg, 17.9 m² — and is now built verbatim, with the guard on the five swale-facing segments and the hypotenuse left open as the approach. The deck edge beam is 0.28 m, not 0.25.

Modelled as a 7 x 3 m rectangle. The survey's ring is a true 8.10 x 3.46 m rectangle (98% box fill) and is now built verbatim, with the guard returning around both ends past a centred 2.40 m opening. The guard gains the bottom rail and the base shoes the shipped model has neither of.

RE-CLAIMED 2026-08-19, ON POSITION. Round two dropped this entry believing the cube had gone to eighthsiteworks with bike-rack-b. It had not. eighthsiteworks' own supersedes[4] is explicitly self-narrowed — it supersedes the four cubes' HEIGHT and COLOUR, withdraws its round-one claim that they do not exist, and says in terms that 'the eighthramble section now owns it'. Nobody was left claiming the POSITION. The shipped item stands at (-135.5, 602), which is inside planting bed arcgis.ground#2703 (x -142.2..-106.6, z 590.0..625.4) — the 1.8 m cube standing in a rush matrix that this system exists to correct — and campus-eighth.js draws it. Leaving it unclaimed while this section re-seats four cubes on the surveyed paved band ships FIVE cubes, one of them still in the bed. Same correction as ramble-planter-2/3/4: correct in size, wrong in position, re-seated onto the surveyed wide paved band. Height 0.9 -> 1.15 m and colour are eighthsiteworks' corrections, carried here.
Same: correct in size, standing inside planting bed 2703. Re-seated on the surveyed wide paved band, which is the only paving in the survey broad enough to take a 1.8 m cube.
Same: correct in size, standing inside planting bed 2703. Re-seated on the surveyed wide paved band.
Same: correct in size, standing inside planting bed 2703. Re-seated on the surveyed wide paved band.

eighthramble.supersedesNote: This list names ONLY items in the shipped eighth section's `ramble` and `teaHouse` areas. It used to reach into the `furniture` area as well, for the lights and racks standing on a Ramble bed; those left in the 2026-08-19 arbitration and the clause naming them left with them. The meditation-area standing-boulder, gravel-field and slab-stone items are NOT superseded here — they belong to the Meditation Pavilion, whose own conflict (SWA -3 shows a dark folded pitched roof with THREE circular oculi, contradicting both the repo's flat-roof model and the phf47/48/49 read) is that team's to settle. The furniture-area poles 1-6, the fire feature, the fire seat wall and the adirondack chairs are left alone: they sit in the gathering and courtyard zones. ARBITRATED 2026-08-19: thirteen entries left this list. bike-rack-b was claimed by BOTH this section and eighthsiteworks and goes to eighthsiteworks; pole-7, pole-8 and bollard-1..10 are orphaned by the deletion of this section's luminaire families A, B and C, which eighthsiteworks' fitted schedule supersedes as a family (its supersedes[0] and [2] name pole-1..8 and bollard-1..10). A section may not claim to replace a shipped item it no longer builds. CORRECTED 2026-08-19 (same day, later pass): ramble-planter-1 was removed with bike-rack-b on the belief that eighthsiteworks had taken it. It had not — eighthsiteworks narrowed its own entry to the four cubes' HEIGHT and COLOUR and handed ownership back here — so the cube was left claimed by nobody while this section re-seated four cubes, which would have shipped five. It is restored above, on POSITION.

withheld.note: Systems that are photographed and dimensioned but NOT built HERE. CORRECTED 2026-08-19: the first draft gave the reason as "the 2014 LiDAR under this site is a demolished parking lot: the drawn surface falls a smooth 3.2 m over 150 m with no step anywhere, so there is no measured grade to hang a riser, a retaining face or a ramp on". The first clause is true and the conclusion does not follow — that is exactly the dead-epoch argument the project law declares VOID over Eighth, because 2014 LiDAR of a parking lot proves nothing about a 2023 college, and EYRC phf03 photographs a full exterior flight with both rails. The real reason is scope: none of the four photographed flights and none of the surveyed wall runs is in the Ramble. eighthcourtyards.levelChange builds the stairs, the retaining and the seat walls on the canonical guard and handrail spec eighthsiteworks owns. What is still genuinely unbuildable is anything that needs the SWALE INVERT, which no source measures — see absent. Every figure is preserved here as this section's contribution to the sections that do build them.

stairs.derivation: The frontal run in SWA -6 gives a rail inclination of 30 +/- 3 deg (rail from (650,383) to (833,277), slope 0.579); rise/run 0.53-0.62 brackets it; inside CBC 11B (riser 102-178 mm, tread >= 279 mm) the only modular pairs in that window are 152/279 (0.545) and 165/279 (0.591), and 152/292 sits at the middle of the measured band. Broad cast-in-place, NO cheek walls on the Ramble runs — the treads die into the planting. At least three separate stairs are visible in SWA -2 alone.

retainingAndSeatWalls.description: Two families. (1) Smooth-troweled stucco / plaster over CMU, warm tan, FLUSH SQUARE TOP and no projecting coping — the SEAT WALL family, which stands on flat ground and needs no grade at all. (2) Pale grey precast / CIP concrete RETAINING walls at the plaza edges, again with a flush cap. Neither is built HERE, and the reason is scope, not terrain: both families are outside the Ramble, and eighthcourtyards.levelChange.retaining and .seatWalls build them on the canonical guard and handrail spec eighthsiteworks owns. Round one gave the reason as 'there is no measured grade for them to retain', which is the dead-epoch argument the project law declares VOID over Eighth — and which in any case never applied to a seat wall.

rampedWalks.description: SWA -4 and EYRC phf22 show the SAME ramped walk from the SAME camera position: a picket guard on the uphill side and a stepped concrete edge on the downhill side, running down into the swale, roughly 1:20 over about 12 m. It is a ramp, not a bridge — and the shipped ramble-bridge-1 sits on it. NOT BUILT, and the reason is NOT that the drawn ground is flat — that is the dead-epoch argument the project law declares VOID over Eighth, since the 2014 LiDAR here is a demolished parking lot. The real reasons are two, and both are about registration rather than grade: (1) every walk in this section is DERIVED from a surveyed bed-to-bed gap, and no derived strip can be identified as the photographed ramp — the frame carries no surveyed control, so building it means choosing a strip, which is a guess; and (2) a ramp is defined by its FALL, and the fall belongs to the swale invert, which no source measures at all (see absent). Registration would fix the first; only a new elevation source fixes the second.

walkEdgeBand.description: A flush concrete or steel edge band on both sides of every DG walk (SWA -8). At 0.10-0.15 m it is below the resolution the walk strips are built at and would only add z-fighting against its own walk; recorded, not built.

absent: THE SWALE ITSELF. SWA calls the Ramble a stepped drainage corridor, and the invert is the whole point of it — but the 2014 LiDAR under this site is a parking lot, so there is NO measured surface for the swale and any modelled depth would be invention. Everything here seats on surfaceAt as the drawn ground currently stands. The braid, the boulders and the weirs run FLAT along a corridor that in life falls. This is the single largest thing missing from this section and it cannot be fixed without a new elevation source.

Stairs and their handrails — RETIRED AS A WITHHOLDING, RE-POINTED AT ITS OWNER. The riser/tread pair, the round-tube rail, the intermediates and the two tread colours stay fully derived in `withheld` and are this section's contribution. What is NOT a reason to leave them out is the argument this entry used to give: 'there is no measured grade change anywhere in the drawn terrain for a flight to bridge'. That is the DEAD-EPOCH argument — the 2014 LiDAR under Eighth is a demolished parking lot and is blind to a 2023 college, so its smoothness proves nothing about built grade, and eighthcourtyards.levelChange.epochNote retired exactly that argument in the same pass. The flights themselves are owned elsewhere: eighthcourtyards.levelChange.stairs builds S1 (15 risers counted in phf03, with its step-light positions) and eighthgathering.courtStair builds the court flight, each with the canonical handrail spec eighthsiteworks.systems.handrail declares. This section builds no stair because none of the four photographed flights is in the Ramble, not because the terrain is smooth.

Retaining walls and seat walls — RETIRED AS A WITHHOLDING, RE-POINTED AT ITS OWNER. Both families stay photographed and dimensioned in `withheld`. The reason this entry used to give — 'nothing to retain on a surface that falls 3.2 m over 150 m with no step' — is the same DEAD-EPOCH argument the project law declares VOID over Eighth: the smooth surface is 2014 LiDAR of a parking lot that no longer exists. The walls are real and they are built by eighthcourtyards.levelChange.retaining (W1, tan integral-colour cast-in-place, with the 26.8 m court-north run measured) and eighthcourtyards.levelChange.seatWalls. This section does not build them because they are not Ramble geometry, not because the terrain is flat.

The ramped walks — SWA -4 and phf22 show one clearly, at 1:20 over ~12 m with a picket guard uphill and a stepped edge downhill. NOT BUILT, and NOT for the dead-epoch reason round one gave ('a 5% ramp needs a 0.6 m fall the drawn ground does not have'), which is the argument the project law voids over Eighth. Two real reasons: the frame carries no surveyed control, so no derived walk strip in this section can be identified as the photographed ramp without guessing which one it is; and a ramp is its FALL, which belongs to the swale invert that no source measures (see the first entry in this list). The full schedule survives in `withheld.rampedWalks`.
The 0.20-0.35 m STEP at each check weir. The weir band ships flush; the step needs the invert grade that no source measures.
The 0.10-0.15 m flush edge band on both sides of every DG walk (SWA -8). Below the resolution the walk strips are built at, and it would only z-fight its own walk.

The 0.05-0.10 m drop from the mulch surface to the walk lip. Both surfaces are decals on campus-overlay.js's shared ladder, and that ladder's rung spacing is a DRAW-ORDER device, not a survey of grade — using it to express a real 75 mm level change would be a lie about what the number means.

Bed-by-bed species assignment. This section can say what grows in the Ramble and what the bands look like from the air, but no published photograph can be registered to the ArcGIS polygons well enough to say 'bed 364 is deergrass'. The repo's registration machinery (.cache/eighth-furniture/Hw.npz, H_w2ref3.npy, register.py) was fitted to the courtyard and the basketball court, not the Ramble. Registering SWA -2 to the bed polygons is the single highest-value follow-up and would convert this gap and the spacing gap into measurements.

The species of the golden-flowered subshrub. The FORM ships — it is one of the three most conspicuous plants in the corridor and omitting it was the shipped model's biggest planting miss — but no rung names it. Candidates in order of fit: Ericameria ericoides, Isocoma menziesii, Solidago velutina ssp. californica, Peritoma arborea.

Plant SPACING as a measurement. 0.60 m for Juncus and Dianella, 0.90 m for Verbena, 1.20 m for Muhlenbergia and Baccharis are nursery and industry practice corroborated against the photographs, not ruler measurements. No frame in the published set can be registered tightly enough to the survey to measure a spacing directly.

Trees. Agonis flexuosa is the dominant Ramble tree (4-5 m at the 2024 photo date against a 7-9 m mature), with Platanus racemosa, Cercis occidentalis, a standard-trained broadleaf evergreen (Rhaphiolepis 'Majestic Beauty' or comparable) and retained mature Eucalyptus — all identified, none built. campus-trees.js owns trees from a measured source and 45 LiDAR canopies already stand on this ground; a second tree population on one landscape is the failure the shipped eighth section already declares. The correct tree work here is subtractive.

Tree stakes. Paired blond timber stakes, ~0.05 m diameter standing 2.0-2.5 m, are on every young tree in SWA -8 and -2. Not built, because this section does not own the trees they belong to and stakes without their tree is worse than neither.

arcgis.ground#349 (32.0 m², x -118.7..-105.5, z 700.3..707.4). The research inventory lists it in the south reach; it is 47 m south of the nearest south-reach bed, sits against the Market Hall, and is the ONE ring in the whole set that campus-eighth.json does not register. Left out rather than claimed.

arcgis.ground#1160 is built (1,521.9 m², the largest ring in the whole Ramble) but is NOT registered in campus-eighth.json — this section registers it against campus-arcgis.json directly and says so, rather than silently inheriting a registration it does not have.

LIGHT EMISSION, and the absence of any luminaire at all. REWRITTEN 2026-08-19: this entry used to read 'Every luminaire here is built as its daytime object — pole, yoke, collar, head', which stopped being true when luminaire families A, B and C went to eighthsiteworks in the same pass (see the entry below). THIS SECTION BUILDS NO LUMINAIRE OF ANY KIND. What survives, and is worth keeping on the record, is the emission half: nothing this section emits carries an emissive material or a light source — not a lit soffit, not a point light, not a glow card. The scene's lighting is campus-postfx.js's business, and whether the Eighth luminaires emit is eighthsiteworks' declaration to make, not this one's.

The north and south reaches' PLANTING is [estimated] throughout, extending the central reach's sourced matrix. No close-range photograph of either exists in the published set; SWA -9 covers the north reach's Sankofa edge and nothing else. Their bed rings, walk gaps and extents are measured; only what grows in them is inferred.
Interior planting variation — bulbs, annuals, groundcover between the structural masses, and any seasonal change. One September 2024 condition is modelled and nothing else.

SURVEY vs SURVEY, DECLARED AND NOT RESOLVED. Two ArcGIS MASSING rings contradict the ArcGIS GROUND layer over the same square metres: 'TDLLN - Sankofa Base' (massing#461, 13 points, h 4.3 m) and 'TDLLN - Sankofa Mid' (massing#489, 7 points, h 30.5 m) between them cover planting beds 353, 354, 355, 358 and 373, slices of 2703 and 1159, and the WHOLE of surveyed walkway 4039 — which is one of the two photographed bridges. The ground layer wins here, on three grounds: campus-eighth.json already registers and campus-eighth.js already paints all seven of those rings, so the disagreement is not this section's to create; the ground layer is per-feature and fine (2,779 green rings campus-wide) where the massing layer is a single 13-point and a single 7-point extrusion envelope over an articulated podium; and SWA -2, SWA -9 and EYRC phf22 show the Ramble running in the OPEN alongside Sankofa's brick base with both bridges over open swale. Those two rings are therefore excluded from this section's building clearance and the other four (Sankofa Tower, both Podemos masses, Pulse Tower) are kept. If the massing layer is later shown right, everything inside those two rings comes out.

campus-3d.json's SIMPLIFIED OSM RINGS FOR THE TDLLN TOWERS SWALLOW SEVEN OF THE SURVEYED BEDS this section anchors to. 'Sankofa' is 9 points spanning x -133.6..-42.9, z 573.6..623.2 and covers #2703, #353, #354 and #355; 'Azad' covers #326; 'Pulse' covers #2375; 'Podemos' covers #372. Those rings are not the authority here and nothing in this section is checked against them: the ArcGIS facilities survey is self-consistent — zero bed vertices fall inside any TDLLN massing ring — and campus-massing extrudes the ArcGIS ring for these masses anyway, because the 2014 LiDAR has no height for a single one of them. Recorded because a footprint gate written against campus-3d.json will fail this section for entirely the wrong reason.

The Meditation Pavilion roof — SETTLED IN THE SAME PASS, not handed on. This section surfaced the conflict: SWA -3, a built 2024-25 oblique aerial, shows a DARK FOLDED PITCHED metal roof carrying THREE circular oculi over a glowing timber interior in a brown raked-gravel field, contradicting the repo's flat-roof-plus-oval-oculus model. eighthgathering.meditation resolved it and builds it — a 13.5 x 7.3 m shallow hipped standing-seam plate solved by cancelling the focal length between two known heights and cross-checked against a 37.2 m surveyed ruler, three oculi, a 2.08 m clear soffit, and the field's material corrected from raked gravel to shredded bark. Not this section's system; recorded here so the observation keeps its provenance.

THE SURFACE OF arcgis.ground#1160, the largest ring in the college. This section claimed it as one 1,521.9 m2 mulch-and-bunchgrass bed; a sibling section claimed the identical ring as one 1,521.9 m2 mown lawn. Both are wrong: ESRI z20 orthoimagery registered sub-metre to the surveyed basketball court shows a mown irrigated lawn over the west and centre and decomposed granite with boulders and a serpentine walk over the east arm, and the SDAF 2025 plan's hatch density agrees (59.1% dark over the east arm, matching Ramble bed #2703 at 53.6%, against 18.1-27.8% over the middle and west). No surveyed edge divides them and no classifier available here separates mown turf from bunchgrass, so the boundary is unresolved and this bed's mulch and planting are withheld. Its ring is retained only as the geometric neighbour that derives walkPairs[22].

Luminaire families A, B and C — superseded in arbitration by eighthsiteworks.systems.l1Pole / l2Pole / bollardLight, which is the only fitted metrology in the set. This section's head-aspect measurement (6:1) survives inside the canonical L1 shade.

Single-post P-loop bike racks - WITHDRAWN. The SWA-8 reading was of a staple hoop seen edge-on. At 10x on swa-4 the fixture resolves as two separate legs with a gap between them and a flange at each foot, which is an inverted-U, not a P-loop. Bike parking is eighthsiteworks.systems.bikeRack.

The check weirs' downstream ROCK APRON. `SWA -5` shows crushed rock on both sides of the pale band and the system declares a 1.2 m apron; it is not built and the field is removed, because the apron is the SAME 40-90 mm angular crushed rock as the channel it would lie in and `systems.arroyo` already paints that channel. Emitting it would add geometry that is by its own description indistinguishable from what is already there — a claim with no visible content.

The golden subshrub's 10-20 mm LEAVES, the Juncus's individual leaf sheaths, and every other plant part below about 40 mm. The three structural taxa ship as the parts that carry their identification — lateral inflorescence, spike above blade, umbel clear of mound, raceme at branch tip — and stop there. This is a deliberate floor, not an oversight: the matrix already costs 36,000 instances, and a 15 mm leaf is smaller than the pixel it would occupy at the distance this landscape is seen from.

THE GUARD'S BASE SHOES. A bolted base plate under a picket guard is an ordinary detail and it is very likely there in life, but nothing resolves it: SWA -5 is the only frame that reads the guard at all, and the arbitration's own picket finding puts a 19 mm picket at 3.4 source px in that frame, which is already the blur limit — a 110 mm plate is under two px and a 12 mm plate thickness is a fifth of one. Round two shipped `shoeSpacing: 1.5` and `shoe: [0.11, 0.012, 0.11]` anyway: four figures with no source, no derivation, and no place in the canonical spec eighthsiteworks owns, which carries a KERB under its guard and no shoe at all. Nor is a shoe at 1.5 m centres a coherent claim in a guard whose only declared members are pickets at 0.1016 m centres and two rails — it aligns with nothing. Better absent than wrong: the shoes are deleted and the pickets land on the deck, which is what the deck-carried guard on these two bridges does. If a frame or a drawing ever resolves the base detail, it comes back with a derivation.

l1Pole.label: Luminaire family L1 — pedestrian post-top pole
l1Pole.derivation: M1 single-view metrology, SWA -4: pole B base on plaza paving yb=583 px, shade top yt=327 px; the horizon is solved from two people standing on that same paved plane (yb 572 / delta 69 and yb 514 / delta 42) giving y_h=423.8; the ratio to a 1.68 m person is 3.454, so 5.80 m. Re-solved from a different person pair (yb 646.7 / delta 115 and yb 571.7 / delta 68.4, y_h=461.6) it gives 5.70 m — two independent horizons 1.7% apart. The nearest catalogue class is an 18 ft (5.49 m) pole plus a 0.26 m fixture rise; the 16 ft class at 5.14 m falls outside the bracket. Shaft diameter: phf22's silhouette gives shade/shaft = 3.9 and swa-4 gives baseCover/shaft = 2.8; 4.5 in (0.114 m) is the standard step satisfying both. Head geometry re-measured in arbitration off phf22 at 7x (masked-grid, sky segmentation): shade diameter/depth = 5.1 and shade/shaft = 5.46, which supersedes the 3.9 shade/shaft figure quoted above and gives shade 0.62 m on the 0.114 m shaft.
l1Pole.assemblyNote: CONFLICT RESOLVED IN ARBITRATION, not carried. The 0.11 m disagreement between the phf22 head read (0.46 m) and the swa-4 one-block read (0.57 m of 25 in 256 px) is settled by direct measurement of the phf22 sky silhouette at 7x: shade 43.7 source px and yoke 26.4 source px against a constant 8.0 px shaft, i.e. shade 0.12 + yoke 0.38 = 0.50 m. The swa-4 25-px read was the coarse one. The collar therefore returns to its own measured 0.13 m (10.3 x 9.3 source px). Grade 0.00 -> lower concrete drum top 0.25 -> second concrete step top 0.35 (pedestalStep, measured in the same arbitration) -> base cover top 0.60 -> shaft to 5.07 -> fitter 5.07-5.12 -> collar 5.12-5.25 -> yoke 5.25-5.63 -> shade rim 5.63 -> crown 5.75.
l1Pole.yokeOrientation: The yoke's PLAN orientation is not resolved per instance in any frame — the fixture is a round shaft under a round shade and only the two-blade yoke has a direction. It is set per pole from the section's pinned seed, so it is stable across reloads and is not a claim about any particular pole.

shade.crownNote: [derived] The crown over the rim ring is a SPHERICAL CAP and carries no dimension of its own: its base radius is shade.diameter/2 and its rise is shade.domeRise, which fixes the sphere radius at (R^2 + h^2)/(2h) = 0.5305 m and the cap's half-angle at asin(R/r) = 0.6238 rad. buildL1 constructs it from those two measured figures. It used to be a truncated cone whose top radius was `shadeR * 0.35`, a bare fraction that lived in the module and appeared nowhere here.

placement.rule: One pole every 20.0 m along the perimeter of every surveyed PAVED polygon of at least 40 m2, held 1.2 m inside that polygon's edge, single-side (swa-9 and swa-2 both show single-file runs, never staggered), rejected within 3.0 m of any Eighth massing ring and within 9.0 m of an already-placed pole. 20 m is 3.5x the solved 5.75 m mounting height, inside the sourced 18-22 m bracket.

l1Pole.observedDensity: swa-12 = 8 poles in one ~90x60 m courtyard (1 per 675 m2); swa-14 = 6 in ~50x35 m (1 per 290 m2); swa-9 = 5 single-file on one DG walk; swa-2 = 6+ flanking the main walk; swa-7 = 4; swa-4 = 4; phf22 = 3; phf03 = 1. Per-frame observations, not a site census.
l1Pole.source: [measured] EYRC phf22 (clean sky silhouette at 7x: shade, warm diffuser band, V-yoke, conical fitter), phf03; SWA -4 (calibration), -14 (pedestal and base cover at 7x), -2, -7, -9, -12, -13, -16. Positions [estimated] by the placement rule. PRODUCT IDENTITY UNRESOLVED and deliberately not invented — see absent[].

pedestalStep.note: [measured] swa-14 at 7x: the pole base is TWO concrete steps, not one. Shaft 92 crop px; step 456 crop (ratio 4.96 -> 0.56 m); lower drum 664 crop (ratio 7.2 -> 0.80 m). eighthcourtyards' and eighthramble's 0.55 m 'base' is this step, which is why they disagreed with the pedestal.

l2Pole.label: Luminaire family L2 — street / drop-off area light
l2Pole.heightTier: [estimated] — no frame gives a solvable base + top + same-plane person. In phf26 these poles reach roughly Survivance's L2 sill line while L1 poles reach only the head of the ground storey, which puts them in the 6.1-7.6 m (20-25 ft) class. 7.0 m is the middle of it.

pole.squareNote: [measured] 0.20 m. The 8 in square pole is the reference dimension the 2.85 head ratio is applied to; every [estimated] figure on this fixture is a multiple of it and says so.
pole.stubAboveArmNote: [estimated] 0.15 m = 0.75 x the pole square. phf19 resolves a short stub above the arm but not its length. Extends pole.square.

arm.note: [estimated] — phf19 sees this fixture end-on and resolves NO arm dimension. All three extend the one measured figure on the fixture, the 0.20 m square pole: section 0.10 = half the pole square (the arm is visibly a lighter member than the mast), projection 0.25 = 1.25 pole squares, drop 0.08 = 0.4 pole squares. They are proportions of a measured member, not measurements. Recorded in absent[].

head.lengthNote: [measured] 0.60 m — the 2.85 x pole-width ratio above, stepped to the product length.
head.note: [estimated] width and both thicknesses. width 0.30 = half the measured length, which is the aspect a wedge street head of this class carries; thickAtArm 0.11 and thickAtNose 0.06 are 0.18 and 0.10 of the measured length and give the taper phf19 does show as a silhouette. Extends head.length. Recorded in absent[].
head.rootFractionNote: [derived] 0.5. The head is a linear wedge from thickAtArm to thickAtNose and the module draws it as TWO boxes, each carrying its own end thickness. The break that makes the two-box silhouette equal the wedge's is where rootFraction*thickAtArm + (1 - rootFraction)*thickAtNose equals the wedge's mean thickness (thickAtArm + thickAtNose)/2 — and for any linear taper that is exactly mid-length, independent of the two thicknesses. So the fraction is 1/2 by arithmetic, not by preference. It replaces a bare 0.42 inside buildL2.

l2Pole.derivation: [measured] head LENGTH only. phf19 at 10x: head 57 px against a 20 px pole width = 2.85, so an 8 in (0.203 m) square pole gives a 0.578 m head, stepped to the 0.60 m product length. The pole's own 0.20 m square is the ONE absolute this fixture carries and every other figure below is expressed against it, because phf19 sees the head end-on and gives no width, no thickness and no arm.

placement.rule: Along the OUTER side of the two surveyed southern walks (walkway-4074, walkway-3044) — the vehicular edge — stepped 3.0 m outside the walk polygon at not less than 12 m separation, rejected within 4.0 m of any massing ring. The two families never mix in any frame: L2 is confined to the vehicular edge, L1 to the pedestrian interior, and this rule keeps that true.
placement.conformance: [derived] Same predicate as the bollards, and l2-4 is the same false alarm: its nearest surveyed edge is 0.275 m away, but that edge is part of a degenerate spur in walkway-3044's ring where the polygon doubles back on itself (its vertices [-84.2, 645.9] -> [-82.5, 643.8] -> [-80.4, 640.9] and [-80.5, 640.8] -> [-84.5, 646] retrace the same sliver). Thirteen of the ring's vertices sit at 3.00-3.13 m from l2-4, which is the 3.0 m step the rule declares. The pole is on the vehicular edge where the rule puts it.

l2Pole.source: [sourced] EYRC phf19 (head, arm and square pole at 10x), phf26 (a rank of four along Theatre District Drive at dusk). Mounting height and positions [estimated].

bollardLight.label: Bollard light
bollardLight.derivation: M1+M3, SWA -4: the bollard at x 807-820, top yt=592, base at the planting edge yb~655. Against y_h=461.6 / hc=2.70 m it solves 0.88 m; against y_h=423.8 / hc=3.61 m it solves 0.98 m. 36 in (0.91 m) is the only standard product step inside 0.88-0.98 — 42 in (1.067 m) falls outside. Body square 0.13 m: the swa-4 13 px width is the projected DIAGONAL, not a side — the bollard is near corner-on there (two faces at different luminance), and a square seen corner-on projects side x (cos+sin) ~ 1.35x, so 0.19 m projected = 0.14 m side. Two independent FRONTAL reads settle it at 0.13 m: eighthcourtyards at 148 px/m in swa-7, eighthramble in swa-8/-2/-14. Cap 0.15 m keeps the measured 0.01 m oversail per side. Lens 0.10 x 0.16 m: the swa-7 glazed panel reads about 0.17 of the visible body height.

cap.oversailNote: [measured] 0.01 m per side. cap.square 0.15 = body.square 0.13 + 2 x 0.01, so the cap and the body are one arithmetic statement and cannot drift apart. (Round one shipped cap 0.17 against a derivation that computed 0.19, with the body back-solved from neither; the arbitration's frontal 0.13 m body settles all three.)

lens.widthNote: [measured] 0.10 m — two independent frontal reads (eighthcourtyards at 148 px/m in swa-7; eighthramble in swa-8/-2/-14), the strongest figure in the lens.
lens.heightNote: [measured, weakest] 0.16 m — the swa-7 glazed panel reads about 0.17 of the visible body height. Arbitration ranked this the weakest number in the canonical bollard: eighthcourtyards' 0.05 m is under-resolved (under 8 px at its own scale) and this section's round-one 0.23 m is not supported by the s_swa7_bollard silhouette, so 0.16 m is the middle read, not a measurement with its own error bar.
lens.belowCapNote: [estimated] 0.06 m = twice the measured 0.03 m cap thickness. No frame resolves the reveal between the cap's underside and the lens head. Extends cap.thickness.
lens.proudNote: [estimated] 0.004 m. The lens is FLUSH-glazed in swa-7 — there is no visible shadow line at its edge — so this is a glazing tolerance rather than a projection, and 4 mm is the smallest value that keeps the glass from co-planar z-fighting with the body it sits in. It is a rendering minimum, not a claim about the product.

placement.rule: Every observed instance stands where a paved or DG walk meets a planting bed, so the rule is exactly that: sample each surveyed planting-bed ring every 10.0 m, step 0.6 m OUT of the bed, and keep the point only if a surveyed paved polygon contains it or lies within 2.5 m of it; reject within 2.0 m of massing, within 7.0 m of another bollard and within 2.0 m of an L1 pole. The lens faces the walk (away from the bed).
placement.conformance: [derived] The rule offsets from a SAMPLE POINT on the ring, so the standoff is the distance to the edge the point was stepped from — not to the nearest edge anywhere. bl-1 is the case that looks wrong and is not: it lies exactly 0.600 m from planting-bed-1143's edges 12-17 (the run it was stepped from) and 0.254 m from edge 11, which turns away at the corner immediately north of it. planting-bed-1143 has 108 vertices of which 52 are degenerate (under 5 cm apart), so nearest-edge distance is not the rule's predicate and must not be tested as if it were. What IS testable and IS the rule: the point must lie OUTSIDE the bed, no further from the bed than the standoff, and inside walkReach of its declared walk. All 21 shipped bollards satisfy that.

guardrail.label: Guardrail — picket guard at every level change
guardrail.heightSource: [measured] 1.067 m (42 in). Four independent photographic reads bracket it — eighthcourtyards 1.06, eighthramble 1.066, this section 1.067, azad 1.07 — and 1.067 m is the exact metric equivalent of the 2022 CBC §1015.3 dimension the product is built to, so it is the one value in that bracket that is derived rather than rounded. It is measured from the WALKING SURFACE at the kerb's foot to the top of the top rail, with the kerb inside that dimension, which is what buildGuardrails builds. THE CODE CLAUSE IS NOT A CLAIM ABOUT THE DRAWN GROUND: see this section's drawnGroundCheck. On the real site every one of these rails stands at a bioswale, terrace or retaining edge; on the ground this project actually draws — 2014 LiDAR that predates Eighth's 2023 regrade by nine years — there is no such drop under any of them, and the section says so rather than letting the citation imply one. The 192 px span quoted in round one is rail-top-to-KERB-top, not rail-top-to-walk, and must not be used as the 1.067 m scale.

picket.derivation: [measured] Solid fraction (picket width / pitch) is scale-free and reads 0.18 +/- 0.02 in both swa-5 crops (3.4-3.8 source px of picket against a 19.3 px pitch). 0.18 x 0.1016 = 0.0183 m; 3/4 in (0.019) round tube is the product step. THIS CORRECTS the earlier 1 1/2 in read: its '8 px of bright width' was the blur envelope of a 3.4 px picket, not the picket core, and with it goes the claim that the rail is denser than code minimum - at 0.18 solid fraction it is an ordinary picket guard. Clear opening 0.1016 - 0.019 = 0.0826 m, which passes the 102 mm sphere with 19 mm to spare.

guardrail.pitchDerivation: [measured] Grid-masked autocorrelation of swa-5, re-run in arbitration because the drawn 10 px grid overlay produces false peaks at every multiple of the grid step. Clean fundamental: r = 0.88 at 19.1-19.4 source px right of the crossing figure, corroborated by a monotone run of consecutive picket diffs 18.08 / 17.69 / 18.08 / 18.08 / 18.65 / 18.85 / 19.04 / 19.62 / 19.42 / 20.19 / 20.19 / 20.77 / 20.58 across src x 1157-1428 (the rail approaches the camera to the right, which is why a single 700 px band average understates it). At src x ~1300 the guard spans 197 px (top rail top y 458, walk edge at the rail line y 655), so 19.3/197 x 1.067 = 0.1046 +/- 0.005 m. The 4 in (0.1016) module is inside that bracket and is the direct expression of the CBC 2022 1015.4 102 mm sphere rule.

topRail.note: [measured] 1 1/2 in Sch.40, OD 0.0483 m, shipped 0.048. Measured at 5.7-8.2 source px in s_swa5_railv at 6x against 185 px/m at that station, and read as ROUND by two sibling sections. buildGuardrails draws boxes, so it ships as a 0.048 m square section of the right size; the round profile is the declared residual.

bottomRail.note: [measured] 1 in Sch.40, OD 0.0334 m, shipped 0.033 — distinctly thinner than the top rail in the same frame. `above` 0.065 m is the rail's centre height over the kerb top, and `picketStopsBelow` 0.010 m is the gap between the picket foot and the underside of that rail; both come from arbitration's read of the same crop. `depth` is 0.033 and EQUALS `thickness`, because a round 1 in Sch.40 tube shipped as a box is square in section. CORRECTED 2026-08-19: it used to repeat the top rail's 0.048 because buildGuardrails drew both rails from one box width, so the bottom rail shipped 45 % over-wide and this note was bent to match the bug. The module now carries a per-rail depth through the loop.

kerb.note: The guard is never fixed directly to the walking surface — in every frame the bottom rail sits just above a raised concrete kerb or edge beam. The kerb is what carries the rail, and it is what seats on surfaceAt. DATUM MADE EXPLICIT IN ARBITRATION: the 1.067 m guard height is from the WALKING SURFACE at the kerb's foot to the top of the top rail, so the picket panel standing on the kerb is 0.917 m. buildGuardrails already builds it this way (rails at ground + G.height). The swa-5 upstand reads ~0.03-0.05 m at that station, not 0.15 m; the 0.15 m figure is retained because no other section models the kerb at all, and it is listed as unresolved. TIERED [estimated] 2026-08-19 and recorded in absent[]: 0.15 x 0.14 m is NOT measured. The only frame that shows the upstand, s_swa5_deck between two pickets, reads 0.03-0.05 m at that station's scale. It is retained rather than corrected because no sibling section models a kerb at all, so there is no second read to arbitrate against — and because the picket pitch is coupled to it (a 0.05 m kerb would pull the pitch from 0.1016 m toward 0.090 m). It extends the pattern every frame DOES show: the bottom rail never lands on the walking surface, it lands on a raised concrete edge.

handrail.label: Handrail — ramps and graded walks
handrail.heightSource: [measured] phf03, arbitration re-measurement. The bottom return's top edge is at source y 935 and the terminal post's base flange lands on the paving at y 1030 = 95 px. The plaza ground plane is fitted from two standing figures - the man with the bicycle (feet y 1005, 160 px for 1.75 m = 91 px/m) and the scooter rider (ground y 1070, 237.5 px for 1.79 m = 130 px/m) - giving k = 0.60 and a horizon at y 853.3, so the scale at the post base is 106 px/m. 95/106 = 0.896 m, inside CBC 11B-505.4's 864-965 mm band. The earlier 0.87 m was the code minimum assumed from a hip-height impression, not a measurement.

tube.note: ADA §505.7.1 requires a 32-51 mm circular gripping surface; 1.5 in nominal is the product step and phf03 is consistent with it. Confirmed in arbitration: the phf03 return reads 4.6 source px at 106 px/m = 0.043 m, i.e. 1 1/4 in Sch.40 (OD 42.2 mm). eighthcourtyards' 0.040 is not a product step.

terminalPost.note: [measured] phf03 at 5x: the rail does not meet a separate post at the bottom - it bends through 90 degrees and runs to the paving as the SAME 1 1/4 in tube on a base flange. Only the intermediate balusters up the flight are thinner (post.diameter 0.038, ~3.3 source px against the rail's 4). Before that date this key existed in the data, was asserted by the suite, and nothing rendered it.
terminalPost.bendRadiusNote: [estimated] 0.084 m = 2 x tube.diameter, the centreline radius of the quarter bend that turns the gripping rail down to the paving. phf03 shows a TIGHT return with no visible elbow fitting — the tube is bent, not welded — and 2 x OD is the tightest centreline radius a 1 1/4 in Sch.40 tube takes cold without a mandrel, so it is the smallest radius the photographed detail can be. It extends tube.diameter, which is measured. Recorded in absent[].

handrail.intermediateRailNote: [estimated] 0.55 m. phf03 shows a second, lower rail on both stainless runs but gives no dimension for it — the flight's own nosings, which would scale it, are hidden behind the descending figure. 0.55 m extends the measured 0.90 m top rail at the proportion a two-rail ADA assembly carries (0.61 of the gripping height), and it clears CBC 11B-505.10's requirement that a lower rail not obstruct the extension. Recorded in absent[].
handrail.clearWidthNote: [estimated] 1.80 m — the spacing BETWEEN the two rails of a run, not a measurement. CBC 11B-405.5 sets the floor at 1.219 m (48 in) clear between handrails on an accessible ramp; phf03's flight is visibly wider than that but has no object across it to scale, and 1.80 m is the common campus ramp module. Extends the code minimum. Recorded in absent[].

bikeRack.extendsPattern: The FORM — a surface-flange-mounted inverted-U staple hoop in a short run set parallel to the walk, bikes on both faces — is MEASURED in swa-4 and swa-2. The DIMENSIONS extend the standard US staple-rack product because no frame in the set resolves a hoop square-on.

hoop.bendRadiusNote: [estimated] 0.12 m = 2 x hoop.tube, the same cold-bend rule the handrail terminal uses: 2 x OD is the tightest centreline radius a 2 3/8 in Sch.40 tube takes without a mandrel, and every staple rack in the four sightings is a single bent tube with no elbow fittings. CORRECTED 2026-08-19: it was a bare 0.20 that arbitration asserted without deriving, gated only by 'smaller than half the hoop width'. Extends hoop.tube, which is the APBP product module. Recorded in absent[].

bikeRack.dimensionNote: [estimated] 30 in x 33 in on 2 3/8 in Sch.40 tube at 30 in (0.762 m) o.c., the APBP module. The 0.838 m hoop height is corroborated by a scale check on swa-4: the hoop reads 24.7 source px against a 0.686 m 700c wheel at ~30 px/m = 0.82 +/- 0.06 m, which excludes the 0.90 m read. The 30 in o.c. spacing is eighthcourtyards' 0.76 and eighthramble's 0.75 rounded to the product module; the tube is NOT resolvable in any frame (60 mm = 1.8 source px at 10x) and stays at the product step. NOTE the correction: the shipped eighth bike-rack item uses tube 0.025 m — a 1 in bar, which is a sign post, not a rack. No staple rack is built at 25 mm.

planterA.label: Planter family A — round tapered 'vase' precast
planterA.soilNote: The soil is recessed 0.12 m below the rim and finished with decorative gravel. No sample window in swa-14 reaches the recess without the rim’s own shadow in it, so the recess ships in the MEASURED planterCharcoal — the darkest tone this section actually sampled on site — rather than in an invented gravel hex.

rim.note: [estimated] profile section. The rim's DIAMETER (1.92 m), the foot (0.74 m) and the height (1.56 m) are measured off swa-14 at the solved 88 px/m; the rolled section is not — at that scale a 0.09 m torus is 8 px and sits inside the frame's blur. thickness 0.09, proud 0.02 and wall 0.06 extend the measured 1.92 m rim at the proportions a precast vase of this family carries (a rim about 1/21 of the diameter, a wall 2/3 of the rim). What is measured is that the rim IS a rolled half-round standing proud of the body, which is what makes the object read as a vase rather than a bucket.

planterA.derivation: M1, SWA -14: the front planter's front rim is at y=413 and its base at y=550, so 137 px. The horizon is solved by tying the independently solved L1 pole (5.75 m, base y=900, top y=78) to a person on the plaza (yb=420, delta=113), giving y_h~0 and hc=6.25 m — an elevated camera, which swa-14 plainly is. 6.25 x 137/550 = 1.557 m. At the resulting 88 px/m the rim measures 169 px = 1.92 m and the foot 65 px = 0.74 m.
planterA.observed: 5 fully in frame in The Social plaza (swa-14), two more partly out of frame. Each holds one single-stem 5-6 m tree over a gravel mulch — the TREE is campus-trees.js's population, not this section's, and none is added here.

signage.label: Signage — building wordmark lockups and applied street numbers
signage.textMechanism: THIS REPO HAS NO TEXT MECHANISM. Letterforms are NOT modelled and NOT faked: what ships is the measured EXTENT of each element as a blank extruded solid at the measured relief — the word band, the underline rule, the cap-height tick, the numeral band. A viewer sees a correctly sized, correctly placed, correctly coloured applied-letter lockup with no legible glyphs, which is what this project can honestly claim.
signage.standoffNote: [derived] ZERO: `standoff` is the clear air gap BEHIND each element's back face, and the module places every solid at standoff + relief/2 so the back face lands exactly on the drawn massing plane. Round one held it 0.30 m proud to clear 'the deepest declared rain-screen in this project' (Keeling's 0.20 m proud + 0.06 m panel) — but no Eighth mass ships a rain screen. campus-eighth.js and campus-photo-eighth.js contain no proud/skin/standoff geometry at all and the masses are drawn at the survey ring, so the clearance was 0.29 m of open air behind five solids on three buildings, and the round-one test enshrined it. When a facade module for Sankofa, Podemos or Survivance ships a measured skin, this number becomes that skin's depth and nothing else in the block moves.

wordmarks.aboveWalkNote: [estimated] 1.6-2.0 m — the wall base is hidden by planting in every frame.

The 36-gallon square receptacle module is 0.61 m square, so a pair is 1.22 m; the 105:87 px width:height proportion then puts the base at y~684, exactly where the planting swallows it, confirming ~1.00 m. The arched throat measures 38 px of a 50 px bay, giving 0.44 m wide, and its head sits 0.10 m below the lid.

placement.rule: Every observed unit stands on paving hard against a planting-bed edge with its back to the bed. The rule is exactly that: one pair per surveyed courtyard, at that courtyard's closest approach (within 3.0 m) to any surveyed planting bed, set 0.9 m inside the courtyard and facing away from the bed; plus swa-16's court-side pair north of the surveyed court.

items.note: COLLISION REPAIR 2026-08-19: slid 1.25 m along the courtyard edge from (-86.64, 568.83), where the 1.22 x 0.61 m surround overlapped plaza-object-13's neighbour plaza-object-8 (-87.17, 569.64, 1.25 x 1.17 m), one of campus-eighth-furniture.js's 17 two-frame-confirmed measured detections. It does NOT keep the 0.900 m inset exactly, because the courtyard edge is not straight there: the repaired unit stands 0.971 m from the nearest ring segment, 0.071 m further in than the rule's step. swa-16, court-side. 1.2 m clear of planting-bed-1760's south edge and 2.1 m north of the surveyed court's north edge.
