waste.detailNote: [estimated] THE JOINERY. At 8x on a 105 px object one pixel is 12 mm, so no member under about 50 mm is resolvable and none of these was measured: lid.thickness 0.02 and lid.oversail 0.01 (a lid reads as one dark line), lid.tab [0.09, 0.02, 0.05] (a bright fleck at the lid's front edge in swa-4 — a pull tab is what it is, its size is not), mullion 0.03 and cornerPost 0.04 (the surround reads as a frame, and 30/40 mm are the smallest members that draw as one). trafficBollard.label: Bollards (non-lighting) — stainless traffic/security rank at the Theatre Drop-Off
trafficBollard.extendsPattern: Extends the bollard-light height, 0.91 m, which is SOURCED in swa-4 and which this rank reads level with in phf19. Only the round section and the brushed finish are measured.

cap.profileNote: [derived] The cap is a SPHERICAL CAP over the full sleeve and so carries NO dimension of its own: base radius = diameter/2 = 0.110 m, rise = 0.020 m, and those two fix the sphere outright at R = (0.110^2 + 0.020^2) / (2 x 0.020) = 0.3125 m with a half-angle asin(0.110/0.3125) = 0.3597 rad. This is the same argument as l1Pole.shade.crownNote. CORRECTED 2026-08-19: the module drew the cap as a truncated cone with an `r * 0.86` top — a bare fraction that lived in the code, that this section had never seen and that nothing derived. A domed cap is also what a standard stainless sleeve ships with; the cone's flat top was never sourced either.

trafficBollard.dimensionNote: [estimated] — 8 5/8 in nominal sleeve is the standard size; the phf19 read is foreground-blurred and cannot be measured directly.
trafficBollard.observed: 4 or more in a line along the drop-off / plaza edge (phf19, at 60-175 x, 950-1020 y). No other frame shows them.

placement.rule: In a line 1.5 m outside the surveyed walkway-4074 edge at 1.5 m o.c., rejected within 4.0 m of massing.

detectableWarning.label: Detectable-warning surfaces at curb ramps

panel.tileModuleNote: [derived] Cast detectable-warning tiles ship as a 24 in (0.61 m) square module, which is why CBC fixes the depth at 24 in: the panel is EXACTLY three tiles across (1.83 / 0.61 = 3) and one deep (0.61 / 0.61 = 1). The module repeats the paving texture once per tile, so this is the number that makes the joint pattern the photographed one. CORRECTED 2026-08-19: buildWarnings had 0.61 written into it twice as a bare texture divisor — a dimension this section owns, living in the code, free to drift away from panel.depth with nothing to say so.

dome.derivation: [derived within the code band] Every figure is CBC §11B-705.1.1 read at a stated point in its band, not chosen: baseDiameter 0.023 m = 0.9 in, the band's floor (0.9-1.4 in), because phf19's tiles read fine rather than coarse; topDiameter 0.014 m = 60.9% of the base, inside the required 50-65%; height 0.005 m = 0.2 in exactly, which the code fixes rather than banding; pitch 0.051 m = 2.0 in, the centre of the 1.6-2.4 in band, in the ALIGNED grid the code requires. The panel is 0.61 m (24 in) deep by rule and 1.83 m (72 in) wide, which is the full width of the ramps phf19 shows.

detectableWarning.spec: CBC §11B-705.1.2.2 / ADA 2010 §705 — 24 in deep, full ramp width, domes 0.9-1.4 in base diameter, 0.2 in high, 1.6-2.4 in on centre in an ALIGNED grid, high contrast.
detectableWarning.rungNote: The panel is a lifted decal on campus-overlay.js's ladder, not a solid; the truncated domes are real 5 mm solids standing on it. It is on `carpet`, one rung ABOVE the `pad` rung campus-eighth.js repaints walkway-4074 and walkway-3044 on. Round one had it on `pad` — the same lift, the same renderOrder 2 and the same polygon offset as the walkway underneath it, i.e. a guaranteed z-fight with its own host surface. The panel must always sit exactly one rung above whatever draws the walk it marks; eighthcourtyards' paving block moved up for the identical reason.
detectableWarning.observed: 2 resolved in phf19 (the drop-off crossing at 300-400 x, 940-960 y, and the plaza curb ramp at 60-100 x, 960-980 y). Every curb ramp in the drop-off zone must carry one.
detectableWarning.source: [sourced] EYRC phf19, 2024-25; 2022 CBC §11B-705. Positions [estimated] at the southern extremity of each surveyed southern walk.
detectableWarning.seatingRule: THE WHOLE TILE LIES ON THE WALK IT MARKS. A detectable warning is a surface of the walking surface: all four of its corners must fall inside the surveyed polygon its item names, not just its centre. Round one placed both panels with their centres ON the walk boundary — dw-1 was 0.051 m from walkway-4074's edge and dw-2 0.305 m from walkway-3044's — so two of the four corners of each 1.83 x 0.61 m tile hung over ground the walk polygon does not cover, i.e. half of a lifted paving decal sitting one rung above nothing it is a decal OF. REPAIR 2026-08-19: each panel is slid in its OWN frame (u along the 1.83 m width, v along the 0.61 m depth) by the nearest point on a 0.05 m grid at which all four corners fall inside its walk, searched nearest-first so the result is re-derivable — dw-1 by u +0.95, v +0.05 (0.95 m); dw-2 by u +0.65, v +0.10 (0.66 m). Neither leaves the walk's southern extremity, neither rotates, and the rule that put them there is unchanged; only the sub-metre position along the ramp mouth, which the rule never fixed, has moved. The test re-checks all four corners of every panel.

items.note: SEATING REPAIR 2026-08-19: slid u +0.95, v +0.05 from (-71.25, 662.02), where two corners of the tile lay outside walkway-4074. See seatingRule.
SEATING REPAIR 2026-08-19: slid u +0.65, v +0.10 from (-93.96, 650.34), where two corners of the tile lay outside walkway-3044. See seatingRule.

detectableWarning.geometryNote: The panel FOLLOWS the drawn ground: the module builds it as a subdivided grid whose every vertex is sampled on surfaceAt, and every dome is sampled at its own (x, z). Round one placed one flat quad and all 385 domes at the panel-centre height, which on a 1:12 fall cut the upslope edge 0.076 m into the ground.

ancillaryLighting.label: Ancillary site lighting — festoon, cove, canopy soffit downlights and wall sconces
ancillaryLighting.extendsPattern: Existence is MEASURED in phf26/phf19/swa-13; every dimension extends the proportions read in those frames against Eighth's own sourced canopy and storey geometry.

sconce.note: Small dark rectangular wall boxes above doors (swa-13 at 1440-1470 x, 400-420 y; phf26). Wall-mounted, so the measured massing wall carries them and nothing hovers.
sconce.dimensionNote: [estimated] EVERY DIMENSION. swa-13 resolves the sconce as a small dark rectangle 30 x 16 px at 1440-1470 x, 400-420 y with no scale on the wall beside it; phf26 shows the same family lit. size [0.22, 0.12, 0.10] holds the measured 1.85:1 face aspect of that rectangle at the smallest commercial wall-box that reads at storey scale, and lens [0.16, 0.02, 0.01] is the bright band across its lower face at the same aspect. atDoorHead 2.4 m extends the storefront head height the same frames show the box sitting just above. festoon.note: Warm point sources on a sagging catenary under the Market Hall canopy (phf26). NOT BUILT — the canopy soffit that carries it is not this module's geometry and has not shipped; a catenary strung in open air is a hovering object. ancillaryLighting.source: [estimated] EYRC phf26, phf19; SWA -13. Existence measured, dimensions estimated. Only the wall sconces ship.

courtHardware.label: Court hardware — the falsification of two shipped absent[] entries
courtHardware.falsifies: campus-photo-detail.json eighth.absent[0] ('Basketball hoop, backboard, court fencing and court-side seating — no legible photo in the reference set') is falsified by one clean sunlit eye-level photograph, SWA -16. campus-eighth-court.js is a DIFFERENT case and the round-one wording got it wrong: its 'nothing in the nine frames resolves a backboard, a rim or a pole' is a code COMMENT standing over geometry that is drawn anyway — the module BUILDS a Muir-spec hoop assembly (a 3.95 m pole set back 1.9 m, a 1.5 m arm, a 1.83 x 1.07 m backboard, a 0.225 m ring and a net, carried verbatim from campus-recreation.js) and counts it. So there is no omission to falsify there; there is a DUPLICATE to retire, and it is named in this section's supersedes. The surveyed 22.7 x 15.4 m court rectangle and campus-eighth-court.js's parametric trident geometry are unaffected and survive.

backboard.note: [measured] A 54 x 42 in (1.372 x 1.067 m) institutional glass backboard, NOT the 72 x 42 regulation board. Measured on the near-frontal FAR hoop in SWA -16 against the coplanar 24 x 18 in shooter's square (37.36 x 27.32 px, subpixel column/row profiles): board frame centrelines 86.31 x 66.02 px = 2.310 and 2.417 squares = 55.4 x 43.5 in, and the square-to-board-edge offsets read 5.7 in below and 23.3 in above, which is the 42-in board layout. Aspect measured independently on both hoops after affine rectification of the board plane (VP_z = 3180.3 px): 1.275 far, 1.308 near, against 54:42 = 1.286; the far board's RAW pixel aspect is 1.297 and the local perspective factor is >= 1, so 72:42 = 1.714 is arithmetically excluded. Absolute cross-check: the calibrated ground homography (f = 1543 px, camera 1.55 m, horizon 667.5) puts the far board at Z = 24.0 m, which turns its 66.02 px height into 1.03 m; 36 in would need Z = 21.4 m and 48 in Z = 28.5 m, and neither fits the surveyed 22.7 m court. The visible aluminium frame band is 0.04 m (6.0 px at the near board's 160.7 px/m z-scale). This supersedes BOTH round-one values: courtyards had the width class right and the height wrong, siteworks the height right and the width assumed from a catalogue it never measured. The 0.06 m panel thickness is corroborated by the near board's right frame imaging 14 px against the left's 6 px — the 8 px surplus is the board's side face at 156 px/m in x = 0.058 m.
backboard.frameNote: [measured] 0.04 m — 6.0 px at the near board's 160.7 px/m z-scale (arbitration).
backboard.bottomBelowRimNote: [derived] 0.1524 m (6 in) — the board's bottom edge below the rim ring's plane, which is what sets the board's centre height and, through it, the standard's rise. It was a bare 0.15 written into the module as a literal and is now data. It is derivable twice over: the arbitration's own subpixel read of SWA -16's far board puts the shooter's-square bottom (which is level with the rim by rule) 8.7 px = 5.7 in above the board's bottom edge, and 6 in is the layout dimension every 42 in board is built to. The board centre therefore sits rim.height + backboard.height/2 - bottomBelowRim = 3.4291 m above grade.
backboard.frameDepthNote: [derived] 0.10 m = backboard.thickness + backboard.frame. The measured 0.04 m band is the aluminium channel's visible FLANGE on the playing face; a channel that grips a 0.06 m glass panel and shows that flange is one flange width deeper than the glass, standing 0.02 m proud of each face. It was a bare `thickness + 0.02` literal inside buildCourt.

net.note: [estimated] 0.40 m long, 0.44 m top and 0.30 m bottom diameter. The nets are white and legible in SWA -16 but they hang against a bright sky and no edge of one is resolvable; the length is the 15-18 in rule band's middle and the two diameters are the rim's own 0.4572 m taken in a little at the top for the loops and to the standard choke below. Extends rim.diameter.

rim.tubeNote: [derived] 0.02 m — a 5/8 in (15.9 mm) rim tube is the rule dimension, and the shipped 0.020 m is that plus the ring's weld fillet; it is also what makes the 18 in inside diameter image at the 31.2 px outer the frame shows.
rim.projectionNote: [derived] 0.1524 m (6 in) — the regulation offset from the board FACE to the rim's near edge, which puts the rim centre 15 in off the board and is used unchanged from the rule book. CORRECTED 2026-08-19 twice over: the shipped figure was a bare 0.15 rather than the 6 in it says it is, and buildCourt measured it from the board's CENTRE instead of its face, which pulled the rim 0.030 m too close to the glass. Both the datum and the number are now the rule book's, and the test recomputes the built rim's near edge against the built board's face.

standard.note: Single-post galvanised GOOSENECK with a diagonal brace strut. [measured] The pole stands 0.20 m OUTSIDE the surveyed baseline, on the concrete apron, and the arm reaches 1.42 m, so the board face lands 1.22 m (4 ft) INSIDE the baseline and the rim projects a further 0.15 m over the court — the regulation overhang. In SWA -16 the near standard's base is at image (1518, 1041.5) against a tile edge at row 1027.9, which is 0.17-0.23 m through the calibrated ground homography; the board centre column solves to a 1.35 m horizontal reach from the pole axis. Round one had this inverted on both sides: pole 1.2 m out, board face on the baseline.
standard.riseDerivation: [derived] rise = rim.height + backboard.height - backboard.bottomBelowRim + armDiameter/2 = 3.048 + 1.067 - 0.1524 + 0.0508 = 4.0134 m, and the test recomputes it from those four fields rather than reading the number. Every term is derived or measured: the rim at the regulation 3.048 m, the arbitrated 1.067 m board, the 0.1524 m (6 in) by which the board's bottom edge hangs below the rim plane, and half the arm. It is the height at which a gooseneck's arm passes just over the top edge of the board it carries, which is what SWA -16 shows. Round one carried a bare 4.1; the intermediate 4.0158 came from a bare 0.15 that lived as a literal inside the module rather than as data.
standard.armDiameterDerivation: [derived] 0.1016 m — 3 1/2 in Sch.40 (OD 101.6 mm), the next product step below the MEASURED 0.114 m (4 1/2 in) mast. The arm is visibly a lighter member than the mast in SWA -16 and one step is the smallest difference that reads as such. Round one carried a bare 0.10.
standard.braceFromNote: [estimated] 2.2 m = 0.548 of the derived rise. SWA -16 resolves the diagonal brace strut as a line but its foot on the mast is behind the near standard's own pole and below the far standard's horizon, so no frame gives the springing point. It extends the rise. Recorded in absent[].
standard.braceDiameterNote: [estimated] 0.073 m — 2 1/2 in nominal Sch.40 (OD 2.875 in = 73.0 mm), the next product step below the arm's 3 1/2 in Sch.40. SWA -16 resolves the diagonal strut as a LINE only and gives it no width; it is visibly a lighter member than the arm it braces, and one product step is the smallest difference that reads as such. Extends standard.armDiameter. It was a bare `tube(0.035, ...)` — a 0.07 m member — inside buildCourt with no entry here and no gate. Recorded in absent[].
standard.braceToArmNote: [derived] 1.3035 m = setBack - backboard.thickness - backboard.frame/2 - braceDiameter/2. The strut ties as far out along the arm as the board it carries allows and no further: the backboard ASSEMBLY's back face is at setBack - thickness - frame/2 = 1.34 m from the mast axis, and a tube whose centreline stops one brace radius short of a plane cannot reach it with any point of its end cap. There is no free parameter in it. It replaces `armLength * 0.35` and `armLength * 0.7`, two bare fractions that lived in buildCourt and put the strut's plan run at 0.994 m for no stated reason. The strut's own springing point ON THE MAST is still braceFrom, which remains [estimated] — see absent[].

courtHardware.source: [measured] SWA -16, 2024-25, read at 3x and 2.6x. The board is the 54 x 42 in INSTITUTIONAL size, measured against the coplanar shooter's square and cross-checked by the calibrated ground homography — NOT the 72 x 42 in FIBA/NCAA regulation board this line used to cite, which the same frame arithmetically excludes (see backboard.note). What the rule book still supplies unchanged is the 3.048 m rim height, the 18 in inside rim diameter and the 6 in board-bottom-below-rim layout. Positions of the two standards are DERIVED FROM THE SURVEYED COURT RING. POLE DIAMETER [measured] 0.114 m (4.5 in): the near standard's base silhouette is 30 px at 257.7 px/m (f = 1543, Z = 6.39 m); neither round-one section measured it and both asserted 0.14 m.

l1bPole.label: Luminaire family L1b - secondary pedestrian post-top, Ramble paths
l1bPole.heightDerivation: [sourced] Reads at ~0.70 of the L1 poles standing in the same frames (SWA -4, -8, -22); 0.70 x 5.75 = 4.03 and the 14 ft ladder step is 4.27, so 4.30 m. Corroborated independently by eighthcourtyards, which sees a second mounting height of 4.0-4.5 m on the Ramble paths.
l1bPole.dimensionNote: [estimated] EVERYTHING EXCEPT THE MOUNTING HEIGHT. The 4.30 m is a same-frame ratio to the solved L1 pole and is [sourced]; head.diameter 0.30, head.depth 0.22, pole.diameter 0.09 and spacing 18 m are not measurements and no frame in the set resolves them. They extend two things: the head is described as a small inverted cone in SWA -8 and phf22 and is read at about half the L1 shade's 0.62 m; the pole is one product step below the L1's measured 0.114 m shaft, which is the smallest difference that reads as a lighter member; the 18 m spacing is the L1 rule's 20 m taken down in proportion to the mounting height (4.30/5.75 x 20 = 15.0, rounded up to the 18 m the sibling section reports). NONE OF IT SHIPS: items is empty by the arbitration's own instruction and the test asserts it stays empty, so these figures are a record of what was seen, not geometry on screen.

THE RETAINED DROP EVERY GUARD IN THIS SECTION BELONGS TO. All ten runs are photographed at a bioswale, terrace or retaining edge — that is why the product is a 42 in guard — but NOBODY has modelled the level change itself, and on the ground this project draws there is none. Sampled on makeSurfaceSampler, the largest cross-fall under any run at 2 m either side is 0.221 m against the 2022 CBC §1015.3 trigger of 0.762 m (see drawnGroundCheck). The reason is the epoch, not the survey: the terrain here is 2014 LiDAR of the parking lot Eighth was built on, nine years before the 2023 regrade these terraces belong to, and campus-lidar.json has no massHeights entry for any Eighth mass. This section builds the RAIL, whose existence is measured in 11 of the 14 photographs, and declares the DROP absent. Building a guessed 0.9 m terrace under each run to justify the rail would be inventing measured-looking ground, which is the one thing worse than a rail on flat pavement.

Same cause as the guards' missing drop: the drawn surface is the 2014 parking lot. The rail spec ships; the grade is absent.

groundDatum.derivation: [derived] Every one of this section's 36 anchor polygons is a campus-eighth.json `ground` feature, and campus-eighth.js draws ALL of them as a lifted decal on campus-overlay.js's `pad` rung (its surfaceMeshes() opens `const rung = "pad"`), which is +0.09 m above the terrain triangle. Anything this module seats on the raw surfaceAt therefore stands 0.09 m BELOW the paving a viewer can see — measured over all 86 fixture positions the median burial was 0.090 m and the worst 0.237 m, which swallowed most of the 0.15 m guard kerb and a third of the L1's 0.25 m pedestal. So the datum for everything this module stands on the ground is surfaceAt + overlayLift("pad"), taken from campus-overlay.js rather than written down as a number here.
groundDatum.residual: Where a sibling photo section later drapes the SAME polygon on a higher rung — eighthcourtyards' paving block declares `carpet` (+0.13 m) — a fixture on the pad datum will read 0.04 m low inside that polygon. Two rungs of paving over one polygon is that section's conflict to resolve, not this one's; the pad rung is what campus-eighth.js SHIPS today, and a fixture 0.04 m into a decal is a far smaller lie than one hovering 0.04 m over the ground everywhere else.
groundDatum.exception: detectableWarning is NOT on this datum: it is itself a decal lying ON the paving, so it climbs one rung further (see systems.detectableWarning.rung).

measuredObstacles.rule: This section is INVENTED and every position in it is [estimated]. Where an estimated position lands on a MEASURED shipped object, the measured object wins and this section moves — the same precedence the survey already has over the photograph for ground extents. Two shipped sets are checked: campus-photo-detail.json `eighth.items` in area `bbq` (the grill counter, two grill bays, the extinguisher bollard, the canopy, the service enclosure, four picnic tables and eight café chairs, all measured off crop_grill.png), and campus-eighth-furniture.js's PLAZA_OBJECTS (17 blobs confirmed in BOTH Apple frames ref3 and ref8 at 1.5 m, which is the strongest positional evidence anywhere in Eighth). The check is a plan-footprint overlap with a 0.30 m margin, and the test re-runs it against those two files rather than against a copy kept here — a copy would go stale the moment either ships a new object.
measuredObstacles.found: Round one collided in eight places: bike hoops rack-swa4#0 and #1 through bbq-table-3 and bbq-chair-6 (one leg landed on the table's exact centre), waste-1 through plaza-object-8, gr-terrace-2375 through bbq-table-1, bbq-table-2 and the bbq canopy, and hr-1159's right-hand rail through plaza-object-13. All eight are cleared below.
measuredObstacles.repair: Each fix is the SMALLEST displacement that clears, taken on a deterministic search so it can be re-derived: point items step on a 0.25 m radial grid from their declared position (16 bearings, nearest first); runs slide perpendicular to their own line in 0.25 m steps (positive first, then alternating) and, only if no offset clears the whole length, are trimmed to their longest clear sub-run. Every repaired position is re-checked against its own system's declared placement rule, against both massing sets, against the section envelope and against the shipped objects.

drawnGroundCheck.what: Every guard and handrail run in this section, sampled every 0.5 m on makeSurfaceSampler(campus-lidar.json.terrain) — the DRAWN triangle, not the bilinear height. `alongFall` is the total rise and fall along the run's own line; `crossFall` is the largest height difference between points 2 m either side of it, perpendicular. Recorded because the guard's code justification (2022 CBC §1015.3, a 30 in = 0.762 m drop) and the handrail's (a ramp, 1:20 = 0.05) are claims about the BUILT site, and this is what the drawn ground under them does instead. The test recomputes every figure from campus-lidar.json and fails on a drift of more than 0.005 m, so this block cannot go stale while a run moves.
drawnGroundCheck.verdict: NOT ONE RUN MEETS THE TRIGGER ITS OWN CODE CITATION RESTS ON. The largest cross-fall under any GUARD at 2 m either side is 0.221 m against the 0.762 m (30 in) CBC 1015.3 trigger — a factor of 3.4 short. The steepest HANDRAIL run falls at 0.0267 (1:37) against the 1:20 ramp trigger. (Two guard runs do exceed 1:20 ALONG their own line — gr-terrace-1159 at 1:19 and gr-terrace-2369b at 1:26 — which is a graded walk, not the retained drop a guard exists for; a guard is triggered by cross-fall, and there is none.) The rails ship anyway, because their EXISTENCE is measured in 11 of the 14 photographs and the epoch rule says the 2014 LiDAR is the wrong witness over ground rebuilt in 2023 — but the drop and the grade they belong to are NOT modelled by anybody, and that is declared in absent[] rather than implied away by a code citation.

placementConstants.note: EVERY CONSTANT IN EVERY `placement` BLOCK IS [estimated]. Not one of them is read off a photograph, because no frame in the 2024-25 set resolves a full run of anything with both ends visible. What each extends: L1's pitch 20 m is 3.5x the SOLVED 5.75 m mounting height and its inset 1.2 m is one pole height's worth of kerb clearance at that scale; L1's separation 9 m and massClearance 3 m, L2's separation 12 m and massClearance 4 m, and bikeRack's 3.0/4.0 m are rejection radii chosen so the rules cannot stack two fixtures or push one into a wall — they are generator hygiene, not site facts. bollardLight's standoff 0.6 m IS the one constant with a photographic basis: every observed bollard stands about half its own height clear of the bed edge, and 0.6 m is that at the sourced 0.91 m height; its pitch 10 m, separation 7 m and walkReach 2.5 m are not. waste's 0.9 m inset and 3.0 m bed proximity, trafficBollard's 1.5 m out at 1.5 m o.c., and l2Pole's 3.0 m standoff extend the same practice. Changing any of them changes where fixtures stand and nothing else; none may be read as a measurement.

eighthsouthservice.label: The south and service edge of Eighth College (TDLLN), UC San Diego: The Backyard, the Market Hall wing's roof, and the South Parking Entrance portal
eighthsouthservice.epoch: Built condition 2024-25. Construction Jan 2021 - Nov 2023; residences occupied fall 2023; project complete 2024. The STATION8 Public Market inside the Market Hall is fitted out but UNOPENED (UCSD Guardian 2026-02-09), so the hall reads as a finished but dark shell. The 2014 LiDAR is BLIND to every entity in this section - campus-lidar.json massHeights has no entry for massing[462] or massing[464], because the 2014 flight measured the parking lot this neighbourhood replaced. No LiDAR height is read anywhere below and none may be.
eighthsouthservice.note: The tenth subject of the Eighth pass: everything south and west of the courtyards that the other nine left with no cover. It exists because `eighthCourtDining` died before producing anything and a completeness critic then probed (-180,640), (-205,675), (-150,700) and (-120,660) and got nothing back from any section. What ships here is only what a source actually resolves: three built systems and a long, specific `absent` list. Two structural findings shaped it. FIRST, the 2025 Open House San Diego site plan is a BUILT-CONDITION, north-up, uniformly-scaled drawing that this section registers to the surveyed ArcGIS ground rings to a median 0.25 m - so for the first time in this college a plan can be read in world coordinates, and `planRegistration` records exactly how. SECOND, the campus GIS ground layer has HOLES over the 2023 construction. Point-in-ring tests against ALL 4,335 arcgis.ground polygons return NOTHING at (-180,640) and (-178,650) inside The Backyard, NOTHING at (-120,662) in the Market Hall Plaza and NOTHING at (-120,680) on the Market Hall's own apron. The only cover anywhere in this quarter is two campus-wide blankets - #3632, a 124,686 m2 4,507-vertex `walk` spanning x -223..235, z -186..702, and #4331, a 44,128 m2 `road` - which reach the courtyard's east side and the whole drop-off forecourt but describe no feature of this neighbourhood and cannot anchor one. There is therefore no surveyed ring to paint these surfaces on, and nothing is painted on them except where the envelope itself can be cut from surveyed BUILDING lines - which is what The Backyard is.

sources.what: massing[462] 'TDLLN - Survivance' h 6.1 levels 2 (the Market Hall / dining wing), massing[464] the 11-storey tower, massing[452] Azad, and ground#4038 (the Ramble-side walk). Rings copied VERBATIM, decimetres/10.

Open House San Diego tour site plan, San Diego Architectural Foundation. One page, BUILT CONDITION, north up. Its site plan is a single embedded 973x1526 raster at 150 ppi (pdfimages image 0) - that raster, not the page render, is what `planRegistration` is fitted to. It labels The Backyard, Loading Dock, Market Hall, Market Hall Plaza, Theatre Drop-Off, North Parking Entrance, South Parking Entrance, and carries the teal Restaurant/Retail tenancy fill this section traces.

EYRC / Lawrence Anderson, Market Hall Plaza at eye level from the north-east, midday. The wing's SLOPING STANDING-SEAM METAL roof plane and its pale metal eave fascia, the plaza concrete, the undercroft shade. Every colour in this section that is not carried from the shipped eighth palette is sampled here.

EYRC / Lawrence Anderson, dusk aerial from the south-east. The wing's roof read as one large folded metal plane oversailing the storefront; the walled service court cut into the west lobe's roof; the mid-site parking-elevator pavilion; the plaza's rectangular raised basin.

SWA Group gallery image UCSD_UC-San-Diego_Theater-District_Living-Learning-1.webp, aerial from the south-east in daylight. The wing's WEST LOBE roof reads as a FLAT PALE DECK with a rectangular walled court cut through it and an inner parapet inside that court - the material break this section clips the roof on. Also the plaza basin in daylight (blue).

EYRC / Lawrence Anderson, Survivance from the south-west at dusk. The garage portal with the applied address 9145 at its head. Used for EXISTENCE of the south portal only - it is a tungsten-cast dusk frame and no colour is taken from it.

11-page design presentation. Its site plan carries the A-K legend the recon dossier could not find (A Wellness Corridor, B Bamboo Forest, C Sun Lawn, D THE BACKYARD, E Public Plaza, F Ramble, G The Social, H Scholars Cloister, I Ridge Walk, J Replacement Basketball Court, K University Gateway) and labels PARKING ELEVATOR x2, PARKING ENTRANCE x2, DINING HALL, RESTAURANT, RETAIL and THEATRE DISTRICT DROP-OFF. Its Ground Level Plan colours the whole south-east lobe of Building 3 as RETAIL/RESTAURANT. Design epoch.

Four subterranean parking levels connected to only three of the towers, ~1,200 spaces. The reason a portal exists in the wing's south face at all.

The college's own shipped, provenanced palette and its sourced barbeque family (grill-counter 4.6 x 0.75 x 0.92 m with drop-in grill bays 0.9 x 0.62 x 0.35 m at sill 0.92). Every [estimated] figure in The Backyard extends THAT pattern rather than inventing one.

sources.what: Regulation table: playing surface 2.740 x 1.525 m, 0.760 m above the floor; net assembly 1.830 m long, 0.1525 m high, extending 0.1525 m beyond each side line; side and end lines 20 mm wide, centre line 3 mm wide. Real product dimensions, not a guess at a table.

planRegistration.raster: openhouse.pdf, embedded image 0 (pdfimages -png), 973 x 1526 px at 150 ppi - the site plan itself, extracted rather than re-rendered so the label layer and the page transform never enter the measurement
planRegistration.model: world_x = originX + mPerPx * px ; world_z = originZ + mPerPx * py. Uniform scale, no rotation: the plan is north-up and its line-work is axis-aligned to the world frame (the surveyed basketball court, which is axis-aligned in world, is axis-aligned on the plan).
planRegistration.fit: Three parameters fitted by exhaustive search over mPerPx in [0.235,0.275] step 0.00025 then refined to 1e-4, originX/originZ over +-10 m. Cost = mean over 9,224 points, densified at 0.4 m along the edges of ALL 74 surveyed rings of docs/data/campus-eighth.json ground, of min(distance-to-nearest-plan-edge, 5 px), where the plan edge map is the top 7% of the Sobel gradient magnitude.
planRegistration.check: INDEPENDENT, and 150 m from where the fit's weight sits: the surveyed basketball court arcgis.ground#3898 is 22.7 x 15.4 m at x -185.9..-163.2, z 517.5..532.9. Read off the registered plan its painted rectangle is 22.2 x 15.4 m at x -184.9..-162.7, z 516.9..532.3 - the z dimension exact, x 0.5 m short (the survey ring carries an apron the plan does not paint), position within 1.0 m.
planRegistration.note: This registration is used for EXTENT and IDENTITY only. Nothing in this section takes its POSITION from the plan where a surveyed ring can give it instead, and the two figures that do (the tenancy trace and the portal's run along the face) carry the p90 as their tolerance.

conflicts: THE DRAWN PRISM WINS, AND IT SWALLOWS THE SOUTH RAMP. massing[462]'s south edge is the segment (-201.9,680.6)-(-153.6,680.1). The registered Open House plan puts the wing's above-grade south WALL at z ~ 672.0 and draws a 8.3 m deep vehicular forecourt/ramp between that wall and the Scholars Drive South kerb at z ~ 680.3 - i.e. the whole ramp lies INSIDE the surveyed footprint, which is 8.6 m further south than the wall. That is 6.5x the registration's p90, so it is not registration error: the surveyed ring is describing the four-level garage below, not the building above. campus-massing.js extrudes the ring, so the ramp apron cannot be drawn - it would be inside a solid mass. The portal therefore ships as an opening ON THE DRAWN FACE at z 680.x, carrying only the plan's measured WIDTH and its position along the face; the apron, the ramp and the flanking retaining walls are in `absent`.

THE NORTH PARKING-ELEVATOR PAVILION'S POSITION. eighthcourtyards.parkingElevator is [estimated] at centre (-197, 526) on arcgis.ground#2374, 'the pale slab immediately WEST of the court'. On the 2025 built plan that ground - x -203..-190, z 508..536 - is a hatched PLANTING bed with no structure drawn on it, and the only surface objects near the court are a low bleacher wall along the court's north edge at z ~ 514 and two small blocks south of the court at z 534..538. This section does not build a replacement (no frame resolves the block against a surveyed ring) but it records that the shipped estimate is contradicted by the newest plan, so the next pass does not inherit it silently.

THE MARKET HALL WING'S ROOF MATERIAL, resolved AGAINST the shipped reading. campus-photo-survivance.js draws the whole wing roof as `roofMembrane`. Three built frames disagree, and they disagree in two different directions on two different parts of the same roof: over the SOUTH-EAST (Market Hall) lobe phf19 and phf17 show a sloping STANDING-SEAM METAL plane with a pale metal eave fascia; over the WEST lobe SWA Learning-1 shows a FLAT PALE DECK with a rectangular walled court cut through it. This section supersedes the single-material plate with a two-material plate clipped on a line taken from the surveyed ring itself. The FALL is still not built - see `absent`.

supersedes.what: the single flat `roofMembrane` plate over the whole massing[462] ring (tower punched out) and its perimeter trim run, built by buildWing() in docs/js/campus-photo-survivance.js
supersedes.why: one material for a roof that three built frames show in two materials, split on the lobe line. This section rebuilds the SAME plate geometry - same ring, same punched hole, same 0.55 x 0.12 m perimeter trim, carried verbatim from that section rather than re-derived - in standing-seam metal over the Market Hall lobe and pale deck over the remainder. Both plates over one ring would z-fight, so survivance's roof plate AND its trim instancing must be removed when this merges; nothing else in buildWing() is touched.
supersedes.removeFrom: docs/js/campus-photo-survivance.js buildWing(): the `plateGeometry(wingRing,[towerRing])` mesh, the `trims` loop and its instanced mesh, and bins.counts.wingRoofHoles / bins.counts.wingTrims

supersedes.what: 'THE MARKET HALL WING'S FOLD AND PITCH ... no source gives a ridge line or a pitch'
supersedes.why: half retired. The ridge line no longer needs a source: the roof is a uniform-slope hip and the straight skeleton of the surveyed ring determines its ridge with no free parameter. What is still missing is the PITCH alone, and this section's `absent` says so in those terms rather than as 'the fold'.

This section is the receiver and it did not resolve it either: the basin's EXISTENCE is now confirmed in two independent frames and its form described, but no frame or plan gives its size or its position against a surveyed ring, so it stays absent - here, with the frames named.

envelope.note: ALL FOUR edges are surveyed lines. wingRoof.label: The Market Hall wing's roof plate - one plate over massing[462] with the tower punched out, in TWO materials split on a surveyed line
wingRoof.lidRule: Seated on the DRAWN lid: median surfaceAt over the ring's vertices + massing[462].h (6.1 m), never below the highest vertex ground. Identical to the rule campus-photo-survivance.js uses, because both must land on the same plane campus-massing.js extrudes.

divider.note: BOTH ends are ring vertices of massing[462] (indices 14 and 6), so the split runs corner to corner and no new point is invented. Signed side = (p-a) . (b.z-a.z, -(b.x-a.x)); POSITIVE is the Market Hall lobe. Every one of the eight ring vertices of the south-east lobe is positive and every one of the other six is negative, so the line separates the two lobes exactly - metal half 1958.4 m2, deck half 2199.0 m2, sum 4157.5 m2 = the ring's own area. THE TOWER STRADDLES IT: massing[464]'s two eastern vertices (-112.5,669.2) and (-118.5,686.8) are on the Market Hall side, because the hall's north-west corner really does tuck under the tower. That makes (metal half minus tower) TWO DISCONNECTED REGIONS, which no single outer-ring-with-one-hole shape can express - asked to, three.js earcut silently fills 334 m2 of the gap. So the plate is triangulated ONCE over the whole ring with the tower punched out, and its TRIANGLES are split by the line. The gate re-derives the covered area from the built buffers: 2474.3 m2 = ring 4157.5 - tower 1683.2.

metal.source: EYRC phf19 (midday, from the north-east) and phf17 (dusk, from the south-east) both show the south-east lobe roofed in a sloping STANDING-SEAM METAL plane, not membrane. Colour sampled from phf19 at (620,762)-(700,776), median of 1,120 px.

deck.source: SWA Learning-1 (daylight, from the south-east) shows the west lobe as a FLAT PALE DECK - a walled rectangular court is cut through it with its own coping and an inner parapet inside. Colour sampled from Learning-1 at (195,495)-(275,525), median of 2,400 px.

tenancy.label: the STATION8 Public Market tenancy - what the Market Hall actually is
tenancy.verification: STATION8 Public Market is published at 20,000 sf = 1,858.1 m2 (UCSD Guardian 2026-02-09; Fox5 San Diego). massing[462].levels = 2, so 929.0 m2 per level. The traced fill measures 933.5 m2 by raw pixel count (15,190 px at 0.2479 m/px) - +0.5% on an independent published area. The 990.5 m2 figure is the DOUGLAS-PEUCKER BOUNDARY at 1.0 m, which runs on the outside of the fill and so carries about half a line-width all round; the pixel count is the number that verifies.
tenancy.source: the teal RETAIL/RESTAURANT tenancy fill on the registered 2025 Open House plan, traced by Moore-neighbourhood boundary walk and simplified at 4 px = 1.0 m, which is the registration's own p90. Corroborated by the 2020 design deck's Ground Level Plan, which colours the identical lobe of Building 3 as RETAIL/RESTAURANT.
tenancy.geometryRole: DATA ONLY. Nothing is drawn from this polygon: it lies 2-6 m inside the surveyed ring (a tenancy boundary, not a wall), and the roof is split on the surveyed `divider` instead. It ships because it is the first source that says WHICH PART of massing[462] is the Market Hall, and because it verifies against a published area.

wingRoof.construction: One THREE.ShapeGeometry over massing[462] with massing[464] punched out, then a per-triangle Sutherland-Hodgman split on `divider` into two raw position buffers, each given an up-facing normal and a UV mapped over the wing's own bbox. Two plates, one hole, no polygon boolean, exact area bookkeeping.

southPortal.label: the South Parking Entrance - the vehicle portal into the four-level Theatre District Parking Structure, address 9145

derivation.head: 3.05 m = massing[462].h / massing[462].levels = 6.1 / 2. The wing's OWN drawn storey, which is the datum every Survivance element already solves on. Walter P Moore publishes the four subterranean levels it serves. Nothing else about it is taken from phf26 - it is a tungsten-cast dusk frame and no colour comes from it.

southPortal.note: An opening PLANE on the drawn face, held 30 mm proud so it does not z-fight, not a recess: the recess depth is not resolved by any source and a guessed reveal would be an invented dimension on a measured wall.
