roof.note: The 4.3 m plinth roof is a large DARK grey flat surface with a LIGHT edge band all the way round — the single most conspicuous ground-level plane in every aerial of Sankofa. It reads as a service roof, not an accessible terrace: no furniture, no planting, no set-back rail in any frame. It is laid as strips CLIPPED against the tower and Mid rings, so the roof exists only where the plinth actually has one — 2508.6 m² gross less the 1079.7 m² tower plate and the 589.4 m² Mid plate leaves ≈ 840 m² exposed. The edge band is dropped on any segment whose midpoint falls inside the tower or the Mid.

storefront.source: phf19 (2024-25) at eye level; phf17 (2024-25) lit at dusk; the 2 in × 4½ in centre-set storefront system, which is the framing profile every North American shopfront of this kind is built from
storefront.note: Full-height glazed shopfront with dark mullions and spandrel louvre panels between bays. 28 bays over the surveyed 50.30 m gives 1.796 m — half the tower's sourced 3.539 m bay. The head and the spandrel PARTITION the surveyed 4.3 m plinth exactly (3.6 + 0.7), which is where both come from; the mullion is the standard system's 2 in face on a 4½ in depth rather than a rounded 0.09.

amazon.source: the 2025 Open House plan places the Amazon block on roughly the northern half of this 26.93 m edge; eighth.ucsd.edu sankofa-layout-info.pdf (2025-08-05) puts the lockers on the first floor
amazon.note: Stored as the FRACTION the plan actually gives — half the edge — and multiplied by the surveyed 26.93 m to 13.465 m by the module, instead of a typed 14.0.

brick.measured: Course pitch 12.1–12.5 px and head-joint repeat ~14.5 px, by FFT on the SWA Learning-9 2× crop
brick.extendsPattern: Sankofa Base's own sourced cream long-format brick in running bond — the BOND and the material are sourced, and the UNIT is now named rather than rounded: nominal 4 × 4 × 12 in utility brick, which lays at a 101.6 mm course and a 304.8 mm unit, a 1 : 3 course-to-length ratio that matches the visual read of a long thin brick
brick.note: No in-plane absolute reference exists in any frame (the guardrail and the lamp post are at different depths, and the tower storey behind is at a different distance), so no product can be CONFIRMED — see absent. The FFT's raw 1 : 1.18 course-to-head ratio would be a near-square unit, which contradicts the visual read and is most likely a harmonic of the true head repeat. The wall therefore ships at the nearest standard long-format modular unit rather than at an invented 0.095 × 0.29, declared [estimated], and replaced the day a drawing appears.

canopy.extendsPattern: the projection (1.20 of the sourced 3.539 m bay) and the fascia depth (0.14 of the sourced 3.2004 m storey) are scaled in the SWA Learning-9 and phf19 crops rather than measured; the gusset leg is 0.56 of the projection in the same crop
canopy.source: SWA Learning-9 (2024-25) — fascia, soffit, gusset; phf19 (2024-25) — the same canopy family at eye level; phf17 (2024-25) — the canopy line lit at dusk
canopy.note: A broad FLAT cantilevered canopy wrapping the plinth above the storefront and over the wordmark wall: a thin light-grey metal fascia band with a knife-edge chamfer at its outer edge, a flat top plane, a dark grey soffit with recessed downlights, and a triangular gusset where it turns a corner. It is the strongest horizontal in every eye-level photograph of the building. Built on the south-east storefront face, the north-east end and the north (Ramble) wall. The soffit sits at 3.6 m, which is the storefront head — the two align in phf19 and that alignment is where the figure comes from. THE GUSSET IS BUILT: one triangular plate filling the outside corner at base ring vertex 9, where the storefront run and the Amazon run meet, with a 2.38 m leg along each canopy edge. An earlier draft declared gussetLength and built nothing.

colonnade.extendsPattern: the column face is 0.21 of the sourced 3.539 m bay in phf22; the glazed wall's setback is not an estimate at all — it is the MEAN of the two surveyed perpendiculars from the ends of base ring edge 10→11 to the tower's north-west face line, 1.391 m and 1.830 m
colonnade.source: phf22 (2024-25) — the primary close-range frame; phf17 (2024-25) — lit soffits at night; campus-arcgis.json massing[461] and massing[488] for the recess
colonnade.note: On the Ramble side the tower is carried on a row of rectangular concrete columns with a recessed glazed wall set back behind them, forming a covered undercroft with bike racks parked under it. The CLEAR HEIGHT is not stored: it is the drawn plinth lid less the drawn ground under each column, solved per column by the module, and an earlier draft carried a duplicate 4.3 literal that nothing read.

bikeRacks.extendsPattern: the standard North American inverted-U (staple) bike rack, which is the form phf22 shows: NPS 2 Schedule 40 pipe at 60.3 mm OD (ASTM A53), 36 in (0.914 m) above grade, 24 in (0.610 m) between legs, at the 30 in (0.762 m) minimum on-centre pitch every rack-layout guide uses. The FORM is sourced from the photograph; the millimetres are the product step, not a measurement
bikeRacks.source: phf22 (2024-25) — bike racks parked under the colonnade
bikeRacks.note: One run of inverted-U hoops under the colonnade, built as two vertical legs and a semicircular top so the hoop is its full 0.914 m tall — an earlier draft drew a bare half-torus of radius width/2 and every hoop stood 0.305 m, less than half a real rack. The RUN's true extent is still not resolved by any frame, so the count of 8 is a fill of the photographed undercroft and not a count of resolved hoops; see absent.

signage.position: on the cream brick, under the canopy, on the Ramble side
signage.style: applied dark-charcoal sans-serif capitals with a HORIZONTAL RULE under the word that extends past it at both ends — the rule is part of the mark, not a shadow, and it is what makes the sign read as UCSD's Eighth College signage family
signage.measured: On the SWA Learning-9 2× crop: letters 205 px wide, cap height 33 px, underline 270 px. Cap height : word length = 1 : 6.2, and the underline overruns the word by 16% at each end.
signage.note: Recorded, NOT rendered — the same standard the shipped argo and blake sections hold: lettering needs a text mechanism this repo does not have, and inventing one is not detail. Every number in this block is therefore a RATIO carried for a future text pass, and none of them is read by the module; that is the point of the block, not an oversight. The absolute size is unresolved (no in-plane reference in any frame; UCSD's campus signage standard was not located), so the 0.20 m cap height is the [estimated] figure a future pass should start from, not a claim.

frontPorch.source: the 2025 Open House built-condition plan names 'Front Porch' as a large orange-hatched RAISED DECK immediately west of Sankofa Mid, drawn as a rectangular platform with steps and a ramp edge; the 2021 Revelle deck slide 6 is the design-epoch antecedent; 2022 CBC 1011.5.2 and 1012.2/1012.3 for the flight and the ramp
frontPorch.note: A real, named, built entity and the principal residential entry to the whole building — and it lies OUTSIDE every ArcGIS massing ring, so it is created here as new ground geometry rather than cropped from the survey, and seated on surfaceAt on the overlay ladder's carpet rung. Its outline is scaled off a drawing against the Mid's surveyed 14.80 m west end, which is what gives the plan its scale; the east edge is pulled back to x −129.8 so it clears the plinth's surveyed west wall at x −129.3 by 0.5 m. The deck plane is one flat level taken from the median drawn surface under the rect plus the lift, with a kerb carried DOWN to the lowest drawn surface under the rect so no ground passes under it. THE LIFT AND BOTH ACCESS ROUTES ARE CODE, NOT TASTE: CBC 1012.3 caps a single ramp run at a 30 in (0.762 m) rise, CBC 1012.2 caps the slope at 1:12, so the maximum single-run porch is 0.762 m up a 9.144 m ramp — and 0.762 m is exactly 5 risers of 6 in, inside CBC 1011.5.2's 4–7 in band, paired with a 12 in going that satisfies the 11 in minimum tread and the 2R+T = 24 in rule. An earlier draft carried a 0.25 m riser, which no code in California permits, and drew the ramp on the west edge while declaring it on the south — where it ran 1.49 m outside this section's own envelope and left a 0.09 m lip standing proud of the deck.

figures._: EVERY number the module builds from has a row here: its tier, the arithmetic that produced it, and — when it is [estimated] — the sourced thing it extends. This is the Keeling bar: keeling.roofs.pv names a real 1.65 × 0.99 m module and a real 0.5 × 0.06 × 0.38 m ballast tray, and every figure beside them is derivable. A round number nobody derived is a defect, and the test walks the blocks named in FIGURE_BLOCKS and fails on any numeric leaf with no row. Paths use [] for an array level, so one row covers a whole array.

grid.sourcedBay.derivation: 13 fins span 955 px of an 1113 px SE face in phf17's top storey band; 955/1113 × 53.08 m surveyed = 45.55 m over 12 fin gaps... taken as 15 whole bays across the surveyed 53.08 m, 53.08/15 = 3.5387 m

grid.bayBand[].derivation: the actual spread of the six counted tower and Mid faces, 3.306–3.738 m, rounded outward to 3.2–3.8; hard-coded in the test and asserted equal to this

grid.baseBrickBand[].derivation: the actual spread of the eight counted brick/colonnade plinth faces, 3.301–4.250 m; the plinth is a retail podium and is not on the residential module — see grid.bandSource

grid.baseGlazedBand[].derivation: half the sourced bay, 1.7695 m, ±0.08; the three glazed plinth faces produce 1.763–1.796 m

grid.floorToFloorSourced.derivation: Largo Concrete, Aug 2022: 10'-6" typical = 3.2004 m. Recorded, never extruded

grid.floorToFloorSelect[].derivation: Largo Concrete: select levels at 11'-0" = 3.3528 m and 11'-6" = 3.5052 m. Recorded, never extruded

grid.panelModule.derivation: phf22 resolves 4–6 reveals across a panel field; the sourced 3.539 m bay divided by three reveals is 1.1797 m, taken as 1.18

facadeSystem.standoff.derivation: the drained back-ventilated cavity behind a large-format rainscreen panel. 50 mm is the smallest cavity such a system is built with and the smallest gap that still reads as a shadow line at phf22's 25 m. It is this section's zero datum: every proud dimension is measured from it, so it is declared here rather than inferred anywhere else

facadeSystem.pleat.foldDepth.derivation: the plan fold is directly visible in SWA Learning-9 and as a sawtooth silhouette in phf22; its depth reads between a fifth and a quarter of a bay, and 0.212 × 3.539 = 0.75 m sits in the middle of the declared 0.6–0.9 range

facadeSystem.pleat.everyBays.derivation: the fold period counted in the SWA Learning-9 close crop: the wall breaks plane at every second bay boundary

facadeSystem.pleat.range[].derivation: the band the crop supports, carried so the single figure is never mistaken for a measurement

facadeSystem.panel.thickness.derivation: a 60 mm composite/ACM rainscreen cassette including its return leg; no crop resolves the panel edge, so this is the system's own smallest honest thickness

facadeSystem.panel.gap.derivation: the open joint between adjacent cassettes, 50 mm, which is what makes the bay boundary read as a line rather than a seam in phf22

facadeSystem.panel.revealWidth.derivation: the fine vertical reveal joint inside a panel field; the COUNT (4–6 per bay) is sourced from phf22, the 30 mm width is not resolved and is the narrowest joint that survives the renderer

facadeSystem.panel.revealDepth.derivation: 0.3 of the panel thickness, the depth a reveal is routed to in a cassette of that thickness

facadeSystem.fin.projection.derivation: 0.113 of the sourced 3.539 m bay in the phf22 crop, i.e. 0.40 m, inside the declared 0.3–0.5 range

facadeSystem.fin.thickness.derivation: 0.35 of the projection — the fin is a folded plate, not a blade, and reads about a third as thick as it is deep in phf22

facadeSystem.fin.returnThickness.derivation: the warm return is the fin's folded side leg, 50 mm, the same plate as the panel gap

facadeSystem.fin.capHeight.derivation: the sloped closure at the top of each one-storey fin, 80 mm, the return plate plus its fold

facadeSystem.fin.range[].derivation: the band the phf22 crop supports for the fin's depth, 0.085–0.141 of the sourced bay; carried so the single 0.4 m figure is never mistaken for a measurement

facadeSystem.window.width.derivation: the slot reads a quarter of a bay in the SWA Learning-9 3.2× crop: 0.25 × 3.539 = 0.885 m

facadeSystem.window.height.derivation: the slot reads 0.66 of a storey in the same crop: 0.66 × 3.0476 = 2.012 m

facadeSystem.window.sill.derivation: the RESIDUAL of the drawn storey once the sourced slot, its head vent and the slab band are taken out: 3.0476 − 2.012 − 0.28 − 0.15 = 0.606 m

facadeSystem.window.surroundWidth.derivation: the recessed charcoal surround reads 0.41 of a bay in the SWA Learning-9 crop: 0.41 × 3.539 = 1.451 m, i.e. 1.64 times the slot it frames

facadeSystem.window.surroundProud.derivation: the surround plate stands 20 mm off the recess back; a third of a panel thickness

facadeSystem.window.recess.derivation: the surround is set 80 mm BACK from the panel face, which is the standoff plus the reveal depth; it is what makes the charcoal read as a shadow in phf22

facadeSystem.window.ventHeight.derivation: the awning/hopper head band reads 0.14 of the slot height in the SWA Learning-9 crop: 0.14 × 2.012 = 0.28 m

facadeSystem.window.ventEveryBays.derivation: the head band appears on every third bay in the SWA Learning-9 crop

parapet.height.derivation: two independent reads agreeing to 0.2 mm: the parapet band is one third of a storey in the phf17 4× crop and 3.2004/3 = 1.0668 m, and 2022 CBC 1015.2's 42 in guard minimum is 1.0668 m

parapet.copingHeight.derivation: a 100 mm metal coping fascia — the thinnest cap that resolves as a line in the phf15 aerial; it sits ON TOP of the 1.067 m upstand, so the assembly clears the code minimum

parapet.copingProud.derivation: the coping oversails the upstand by 60 mm each side, which is the drip a 100 mm cap is formed with

parapet.neStepDown.derivation: 35 px in the phf17 4× crop against 31.25 px/m, calibrated on the adjacent 100 px = 3.2004 m top storey band: 35/31.25 = 1.12 m. It EXCEEDS the 1.067 m upstand, which is the finding rather than an error — over the loggia stack the solid parapet is absent and the coping and pipe guardrail carry the edge

parapet.rail.height.derivation: 2022 CBC 1015.2: 42 in = 1.0668 m guard minimum, the same figure the parapet upstand lands on

parapet.rail.postSpacing.derivation: 6 ft = 1.829 m, the standard post pitch for a galvanised pipe guard in NPS 1½ Schedule 40; phf17 resolves the rail as a line and not its posts

parapet.rail.bar.derivation: NPS 1½ Schedule 40 pipe, 1.900 in = 48.3 mm OD (ASTM A53 / ASME B36.10M) — the product every galvanised pipe guard is made from, taken as 0.048 m

loggia.count.derivation: eighth.ucsd.edu sankofa-layout-info.pdf: 21 floors, L1 lobby, L2–L21 residential = 20 residential floors, one loggia each; ~19 downlights counted in phf17 before the crop runs out

loggia.loggiaBays.derivation: the loggia opening spans 2 of the 5 counted bays of the surveyed 16.34 m north-east end: 2 × 3.2680 = 6.536 m, which brackets the two independent pixel reads of Apple close-08 (≈6.4 m and ≈6.7 m)

loggia.curtainBays.derivation: the dark glazed study/lounge bay takes the remaining 3 counted bays: 3 × 3.2680 = 9.804 m, which is the run close-08 shows reaching the north-west corner unbroken

loggia.pierBays.derivation: zero. Apple close-08 and orbit-08, both 8° off a true elevation of this face, show no pale solid panel wider than about a metre at the north-west corner; the inventory's 'solid pier' is not built and is declared absent

loggia.slabProjection.derivation: 0.466 of the sourced 3.539 m bay on the phf15 4.5× crop, i.e. 1.65 m, inside the 1.5–1.8 m the crop supports

loggia.slabThickness.derivation: the white slab band reads 0.115 of a storey in the phf15 5× crop: 0.115 × 3.0476 = 0.35 m. That is the slab EDGE plus its upstand, not the structure — Walter P Moore's post-tensioned flat plate would be nearer 0.22 m — which is why it is [estimated] and why the structural figure is not claimed

loggia.soffitDrop.derivation: 0.34 of the slab thickness: the soffit of the slab above drops 120 mm below the structural line as a shadow gap, which is what makes each loggia read as a separate opening in phf17. Read by the module — the glazed lounge and the dark recess are both shortened by it

loggia.balustrade.height.derivation: 2022 CBC 1015.2, 42 in = 1.0668 m, consistent with the thin line phf17 resolves at the open edge

loggia.balustrade.postSpacing.derivation: 1.2 m, the pitch a 48.3 mm pipe post carries a guard at over a 6.5 m opening in five equal bays; phf17 resolves the rail line and not its posts

loggia.balustrade.bar.derivation: NPS 1½ Schedule 40, 48.3 mm OD — the same guard product as the crown rail, which is what the two lines look like in phf17

loggia.downlight.diameter.derivation: a 220 mm recessed downlight aperture — the size class of exterior soffit downlight that reads as a distinct point at phf17's range and not as a wash

loggia.downlight.depth.derivation: 0.36 of the aperture: the lens plate's own thickness where it sits in the soffit

loggia.downlight.inset.derivation: a quarter of the slab projection, 1.65/4 = 0.4125 m from the open corner, which is where the vertical run of points sits relative to the slab edge in phf17

loggia.downlight.emissive.derivation: a LOW emissive so the fixture reads as a luminaire rather than as an invented night source; dimensionless, and the same register Keeling's 16 lamps use

loggia.glassInset.derivation: the glazed lounge sits behind the recess face by the same 4½ in (0.114 m) system depth the plinth's storefront uses, so the building has ONE glazing depth rather than two invented ones

roof.frame.originFace.derivation: ring edge index 1, P1→P2, the surveyed south-east long face; the roof frame is built from the ring and not stored

roof.walkway.width.derivation: 0.09 of the roof width on the phf15 5× crop: 0.09 × 19.67 = 1.77 m, inside the 1.5–2.0 m the crop supports

roof.walkway.inset.derivation: the pad sits 0.8–1.2 m inside the parapet in the same crop; 1.0 m is the middle of that band and is 0.56 of the pad's own width

roof.walkway.strip.derivation: not a claim about the building: the 1 m sub-segment the pad is laid in so it can be clipped against the drawn ring and the notch. A build resolution, and the finer it is the more honest the clip

roof.penthouses[].uFrac.derivation: position along the roof read as a fraction of its own length in the phf15 5× crop: 0.28 and 0.779

roof.penthouses[].vFrac.derivation: position across the roof as a fraction of its 19.67 m width: the lift overrun is centred (0.5) and the stair head sits at 0.686

roof.penthouses[].size[].derivation: the south-west box is 0.14 of the 54.16 m roof length × 0.56 of the 19.67 m width = 7.582 × 11.015 m, and its 4.38 m height is measured at 137 px against 31.25 px/m in phf17; the north-east box is 0.70 of that footprint and 0.68 of that height

roof.penthouses[].louvre.size[].derivation: 0.475 of the penthouse width and 0.50 of its measured height: 3.601 × 2.19 m

roof.penthouses[].hatch[].derivation: a roof-access hatch on the lift overrun's lid; 2.2 × 1.8 m in plan at 0.12 m upstand is the standard double-leaf hatch size class, and phf15 resolves that there is one, not how big

roof.equipment[].uFrac.derivation: each island's position along the roof read as a fraction of its own length in the phf15 5–6× crops, counted south-west to north-east

roof.equipment[].vFrac.derivation: each island's position across the roof as a fraction of the 19.67 m width, always between the two pale walkway runs and never on one

roof.equipment[].size[].derivation: plan dimensions as fractions of the 19.67 m surveyed roof width and heights as fractions of the one measured absolute this roof has, then multiplied up — which is why none of them is a round metre

roof.equipment[].diameter.derivation: 0.155 of the 19.67 m roof width = 3.049 m for the cylindrical unit

roof.equipment[].height.derivation: 0.57 of the measured penthouse height = 2.497 m for the cylindrical unit

roof.equipment[].pipes.derivation: nine vertical risers counted in the phf15 6× crop and corroborated in SWA Learning-1's silhouette

roof.curbs.candidates.derivation: phf15 resolves that small curbs, vents and drain pairs are scattered across this roof but not where; 26 candidates are seeded and every one whose footprint leaves the drawn ring is dropped, which is what empties the notch

roof.curbs.size[].derivation: a 0.6 × 0.6 m curb 0.3 m tall — the size class of a roof drain sump or a small vent curb, and the smallest object phf15 still resolves as an object

roof.clips[].u0.derivation: the surveyed notch's u-extent in the roof frame, from the ring: P2 at u 53.08

roof.clips[].u1.derivation: past P4's u 56.87, out to 60.0, so the clip covers the whole open quadrant and not just the ring's own corner

roof.clips[].v0.derivation: −1.0, i.e. just outside the south-east face line, so a strip cannot straddle the boundary into the void

roof.clips[].v1.derivation: the surveyed notch's inward depth from the ring: P4 at v 3.30

midRoof.box.xFrac.derivation: 0.22 of the Mid's drawn bounding box in x — which is what 'positioned toward the west third' means once it is written as a number instead of a sentence

midRoof.box.zFrac.derivation: 0.506 of the Mid's drawn bounding box in z: centred on the depth, as phf15 shows it

midRoof.box.size[].derivation: a 5 × 4 m stair/plant box 3 m tall — the smallest volume that houses a stair head, and 0.68 of the tower's own measured 4.38 m overrun

midRoof.units.count.derivation: phf15 resolves two or three small units; three is the upper read

midRoof.units.candidates.derivation: 12 seeded candidates, of which the first three that land inside the drawn Mid ring are kept — a scatter, because the frame gives a count and not a position

midRoof.units.size[].derivation: the same small condenser/vent size class as the tower's smallest island, at 0.6 of it

midRoof.pv.panels.derivation: zero, and it is the same finding as the tower's: phf15 and SWA Learning-1 show membrane and small plant on this roof and no array, against the 2021 design deck that draws one. A negative is a number and it carries a derivation like every other

plinth.roof.strip.derivation: not a claim about the building: the 1.5 m sub-segment the plinth roof is laid in so it can be subtracted against the tower and Mid rings. A build resolution

plinth.roof.edgeBand.derivation: 0.03 of the surveyed 21.5 m west wall in the phf15 crop = 0.645 m, taken as 0.65

plinth.roof.edgeInset.derivation: the band sits 0.3 m in from the plinth's own edge — 0.46 of its width, which is the gap the crop shows between the band and the parapet line

plinth.roof.units.count.derivation: two to four units counted in phf15 and Apple close-00-south; three is the middle read

plinth.roof.units.candidates.derivation: 26 seeded candidates over the plinth's drawn BOUNDING BOX, of which the first three that land on roof surviving the tower/Mid subtraction are kept — the box is a good deal larger than the ~840 m² of exposed roof, so the candidate pool has to be several times the count

plinth.roof.units.size[].derivation: the same curb-scale plant box class as the tower's islands; nothing is claimed about what they are — see absent

plinth.storefront.height.derivation: the head and the spandrel PARTITION the surveyed 4.3 m plinth: 3.6 + 0.7 = 4.3 exactly, and phf19 shows the head aligning with the canopy soffit

plinth.storefront.spandrel.derivation: the remainder of the surveyed 4.3 m above the 3.6 m head: 0.7 m of spandrel louvre, which is the band phf19 resolves between the glass and the canopy

plinth.storefront.mullion.derivation: the 2 in (50.8 mm) face of the 2 × 4½ in centre-set storefront system — the standard North American shopfront profile, not a rounded 0.09

plinth.storefront.mullionDepth.derivation: the 4½ in (114.3 mm) depth of the same system

plinth.storefront.glassInset.derivation: half the 114.3 mm system depth: the glass line sits 57 mm behind the mullion face, which is where centre-set glazing sits by definition

plinth.amazon.frontageFrac.derivation: the 2025 Open House plan puts the Amazon block on the northern HALF of this edge; stored as 0.5 and multiplied by the surveyed 26.93 m to 13.465 m

plinth.brick.courseHeight.derivation: nominal 4 in course of a 4 × 4 × 12 in utility brick = 101.6 mm. The FFT gives the RATIO and the visual read gives the family; the absolute follows from the standard unit, because no in-plane reference exists — see absent

plinth.brick.unitLength.derivation: nominal 12 in length of the same unit = 304.8 mm, a 1 : 3 course-to-length ratio that matches the long thin brick the crops read

plinth.canopy.projection.derivation: 1.20 of the sourced 3.539 m bay in the SWA Learning-9 and phf19 crops = 4.25 m; sanity-checked against the plinth's own surveyed 5.865 m projection past the tower's south-east face, which the canopy must not exceed

plinth.canopy.fascia.derivation: 0.14 of a storey in the same crops = 0.448 m

plinth.canopy.fasciaEdge.derivation: the knife-edge chamfer's own plate, 100 mm — 0.22 of the fascia depth, which is the taper SWA Learning-9 shows at the outer edge

plinth.canopy.underside.derivation: the canopy soffit aligns with the storefront head in phf19, so it is the same 3.6 m, and the 4.3 − 3.6 = 0.7 m above it is the spandrel band

plinth.canopy.topPlate.derivation: the canopy's flat top plate, 80 mm — a rainscreen cassette plus its return, the same plate family as the wall

plinth.canopy.downlight.diameter.derivation: 0.91 of the loggia downlight's aperture: the same soffit downlight family one size smaller, at 200 mm

plinth.canopy.downlight.spacing.derivation: the sourced 3.539 m bay: the canopy downlights sit one per structural bay in phf19, which is the one canopy figure that is not scaled

plinth.canopy.gussetLength.derivation: 0.56 of the projection in the SWA Learning-9 crop = 2.38 m along each canopy edge from the corner. BUILT — one plate at base ring vertex 9

plinth.colonnade.columnSize.derivation: the column face reads 0.21 of the sourced bay in phf22: 0.21 × 3.539 = 0.743 m

plinth.colonnade.recess.derivation: the MEAN of the two surveyed perpendiculars from the ends of base ring edge 10→11 to the tower's north-west face line P5→P0: (1.391 + 1.830)/2 = 1.6105 m. Not an estimate — the undercroft's depth is what the two rings themselves say it is

plinth.colonnade.glassInset.derivation: the glazed line behind the columns sits at the building's one glazing depth, 114.3 mm, the same as the storefront and the loggia

plinth.bikeRacks.hoops.derivation: 8 hoops at the 0.762 m standard pitch fill 5.3 m of the photographed undercroft. phf22 shows a run and does not resolve its end, so this is a FILL and not a count — see absent

plinth.bikeRacks.spacing.derivation: 30 in = 0.762 m, the minimum on-centre spacing every inverted-U rack layout guide specifies

plinth.bikeRacks.width.derivation: 24 in = 0.610 m between the legs of a standard inverted-U (staple) rack

plinth.bikeRacks.height.derivation: 36 in = 0.914 m above grade, the standard inverted-U height; the hoop is built as two legs of 0.914 − 0.305 = 0.609 m and a semicircular top of radius 0.305 m so it actually stands that tall

plinth.bikeRacks.bar.derivation: NPS 2 Schedule 40 pipe, 2.375 in = 60.3 mm OD (ASTM A53) — the heavier of the two sizes inverted-U racks are made from, which is what the frame's chunky read supports

signage.capHeight.derivation: recorded, never rendered. 0.20 m is the starting figure a future text pass should use; the absolute is unresolved because no in-plane reference exists

signage.wordLength.derivation: 205 px on the SWA Learning-9 2× crop, at the cap-height : word-length ratio of 1 : 6.2; carried as a RATIO, since the block is recorded and not rendered

signage.ruleLength.derivation: 270 px on the same crop, 1.32 times the word

signage.ruleOverrun.derivation: the underline overruns the word by 16% of its own length at each end, (270 − 205)/2/205

frontPorch.rect.x0.extends: the Mid's surveyed 14.80 m west end
frontPorch.rect.x0.derivation: the Open House plan's orange hatch scaled against that surveyed end; the plan is a tour map, not a drawing, so this is a proportion

frontPorch.rect.x1.derivation: pulled back to −129.8 so the deck clears the surveyed wall at x −129.3 by 0.5 m

frontPorch.rect.z0.extends: the Mid's surveyed 14.80 m west end
frontPorch.rect.z0.derivation: the Open House hatch's north edge, scaled against the Mid's surveyed west end; it runs a little north of the Mid's own 604.0 north-west corner

frontPorch.rect.z1.extends: the Mid's surveyed 14.80 m west end
frontPorch.rect.z1.derivation: the Open House hatch's south edge on the same scaling, giving a 19 m deep platform against the Mid's 14.80 m end — the hatch is drawn deeper than the wing it serves

frontPorch.lift.derivation: 2022 CBC 1012.3: 30 in = 0.762 m is the maximum rise a single ramp run may take. The plan draws ONE ramp and no intermediate landing, so the porch is at most 0.762 m up — and 0.762 m is also exactly 5 × 6 in, which is why the flight comes out whole

frontPorch.kerb.derivation: 0.21 of the lift: the deck's edge upstand, carried DOWN to the lowest drawn surface under the rect so no ground passes beneath the platform

frontPorch.steps.count.derivation: 0.762 m lift / 0.1524 m riser = 5 risers exactly

frontPorch.steps.rise.derivation: 6 in = 0.1524 m, inside 2022 CBC 1011.5.2's 4–7 in band and the riser that divides the code-limited 0.762 m lift into whole steps. The earlier 0.25 m riser exceeds the 7 in maximum and is not buildable in California

frontPorch.steps.going.derivation: 12 in = 0.3048 m: clears CBC 1011.5.2's 11 in minimum tread and satisfies 2R + T = 24 in with the 6 in riser

frontPorch.steps.width.derivation: the flight reads about a quarter of the deck's 19 m depth on the Open House hatch; a proportion off a tour map, not a measurement

frontPorch.ramp.run.derivation: 2022 CBC 1012.2 caps the slope at 1:12, so the code-limited 0.762 m rise needs 12 × 0.762 = 9.144 m of run

frontPorch.ramp.width.derivation: 60 in = 1.524 m, the CBC 1012.6.1 landing dimension and the next standard increment above the 44 in clear-width minimum for this occupancy; the plan draws the ramp wider than a doorway and no frame resolves it

frontPorch.ramp.thickness.derivation: a 6 in (0.152 m) cast slab, the standard exterior ramp slab and the same 6 in module as the riser

panelSunlit.source: EYRC phf22 — median of a 36×36 px patch on a directly sunlit rainscreen panel field at ~25 m

panelBright.source: SWA Learning-9 — median over the brightest frontal-lit panel return, midday

absent: ROOFTOP PHOTOVOLTAICS, on every Sankofa roof — 0 panels, 0 racks, 0 ballast trays. The 2021 Revelle town-hall deck (slides 4 and 16) draws large dark PV fields across the Eighth roofs; the built aerials EYRC phf15 (2024-25) and SWA Learning-1 (2024-25) show white/grey membrane, parapets, penthouses, ducts and RTUs and no array, with Keeling Apartments' own roof PV plainly visible in the same frames as the positive control that proves the camera could record PV if PV were there, and Apple close-08-north-east (2026-08-06) looks straight down this roof and shows the same. The design-epoch rendering is superseded and nothing is built.

The SANKOFA wordmark's lettering. Ratios are measured (cap height : word length = 1 : 6.2, underline overrunning 16% at each end) and recorded in `signage`, but the absolute size is unresolved — no in-plane reference exists in any frame and UCSD's campus signage standard was not located. Not rendered, on the same standard the shipped argo and blake sections hold: lettering needs a text mechanism this repo does not have.

The base brick's FORMAT. Course pitch (12.1–12.5 px) and head-joint repeat (~14.5 px) were measured by FFT on the SWA Learning-9 2× crop, but no in-plane absolute reference exists — the guardrail and the lamp post are at different depths and the tower storey behind is at a different distance. The wall ships at the nominal 4 × 4 × 12 in utility unit, which is the nearest standard long-format modular brick to the visual read, but NO PRODUCT IS CONFIRMED and the coursing stays [estimated].

The roof membrane's HEX. Every aerial that resolves this roof is golden-hour, so a sampled hex would encode the sun rather than the material. The membrane ships as the described light grey single-ply derived from this building's own sourced neutrals, and the sample is deliberately not taken.

The building's REAL height. Largo Concrete's 21 levels at 10'-6" typical with select 11'-0"/11'-6" totals 67.21–67.67 m against the drawn ArcGIS 64.0 m formula prism — a one-storey conflict. Anchored to the drawn box per the Keeling rule; the sourced figure is recorded in conflicts[0] and nothing is built on it.

Sankofa Mid at 9 storeys. ArcGIS levels = 10 and the 2021 site plan label '(10 STORIES)' against the 2021 aerial rendering's '9' and a syndicated project text. Unresolved; the survey's 10 is built and the 9 stays on the record.

EVERY ENTRANCE DOOR ON THE BUILDING, and this is a hole rather than an omission. Four separate entrance classes are documented and none is built: the MAIN RESIDENTIAL ENTRY off the Front Porch (the 2025 Open House plan locates the lobby but the porch side is the least photographed side of the building); the RESTAURANT / RETAIL shopfront entries along the 50.30 m south-east storefront and round onto Market Hall Plaza (the plan gives the tenancy block, never a door position); the AMAZON locker-room entry on the north-east end (the layout PDF puts the lockers on the first floor and nothing resolves the opening); and the COLONNADE's glazed line on the Ramble side, which phf22 shows as a continuous glazed wall with no leaf resolved. A door in a storefront is one bay with a different mullion pattern and a threshold — WHICH bay is the whole claim, and no source in this set gives it. Nothing is guessed; 46 storefront bays, the Amazon frontage and the colonnade glazing all ship without a leaf.

The SOLID PIER at the north-east end's north-west corner. The research inventory describes one; Apple close-08-north-east and orbit-08-north-east, both 8° off a true elevation of that face, show the dark glazed bay running unbroken to the corner with no pale solid panel wider than about a metre. The pier is not built, `loggia.pierBays` is 0, and the inventory's read stays on the record in conflicts[3].

The NORTH-EAST END's three sub-widths AS MEASUREMENTS. Apple's photogrammetric mesh melts the loggia stack into taffy at this range, and two independent pixel reads of close-08 disagree by 0.3 m on the loggia and by more than 3 m on where the curtain bay ends. The composition is therefore built as a COUNT over the surveyed 16.34 m face — 2 + 3 + 0 of the face's 5 bays — which is the same rule every other face here uses, and the metres are consequences rather than claims. Google Street View or a frontal EYRC frame would settle it.

The MARKET HALL PLAZA TERRACE GUARDRAIL. phf19 shows a galvanised picket guard along the terrace edge in front of the south-east storefront, and it is real. It is not built here because what carries it is the PLAZA's level change, not the building: no frame resolves how far that step lies from the plinth wall, and the round-one draft carried it at an invented 1.20 m standoff with no source of any kind. The plaza and its rails belong to the Eighth landscape sections; better absent than at a guessed offset.

The colonnade's ~5-column RETURN round the plinth's north-east end. Sourced present in phf17 and phf15, but it shares the surveyed 26.93 m edge with the sourced canopy and no frame resolves how the two meet. The canopy is built and the return is not.

The LOGGIA BALUSTRADE'S INFILL TYPE. phf17 resolves a thin line at the open edge but not whether it is glass or picket. Built as the picket family photographed at the plinth in phf19, on NPS 1½ Schedule 40 pipe, labelled [estimated]; replaced the day a close frame appears.

The IDENTITY of every unit on the TOWER roof. phf15 resolves six islands and their silhouettes — a cylindrical unit, two boxy AHU/condensers, two packaged RTUs and a pipe rack — but not one manufacturer, model or capacity. They ship as generic plant at ratios to the one measured absolute this roof has, and nothing is claimed about what they are.

The POSITIONS of the small units on the PLINTH roof and the MID roof. Two to four are counted in phf15 and Apple close-00-south on the plinth, two or three on the Mid; NO frame resolves where any of them stands. The round-one draft typed six positions at round metres. They now ship as a seeded scatter clipped to roof that actually exists, which claims a count and not a location, and their identity is not claimed either.

The BIKE RACK RUN's true extent under the colonnade. phf22 shows a run of inverted-U hoops and the crop cuts before its end. The product step is the standard staple rack (NPS 2 Schedule 40, 36 in tall, 24 in wide, 30 in on centre) and that much is a real product; the COUNT of 8 is a fill of the photographed undercroft, not a count of resolved hoops.

Every INTERIOR. Community kitchens on every even floor, laundries on even floors from L10, study rooms on every floor, trash chutes, the Residential Life Office and the Amazon locker bank itself are all sourced from the university's own layout PDF — as programme, with no geometry. STATION8 is still unopened as of Feb 2026, so the plinth reads as a finished but unoccupied shell.

The SUBTERRANEAN four-level parking structure beneath the site (Walter P Moore: ~1,165–1,200 cars connected to only three of the towers). Sourced and entirely invisible; nothing is built and nothing is implied at grade.

OPENINGS on the plinth's south and west walls. No frame in the reference set resolves those planes frontally; they ship as the plinth's own sourced cream brick with a glazed run only on the 21.16 m Market Hall Plaza edge, where the Open House plan carries the Restaurant/Retail tenancy, and every one of those faces is labelled [estimated].

The AWNING/HOPPER VENT LEAVES at the window heads. gbdmagazine documents the natural-ventilation openings and the SWA Learning-9 crop shows the head band, but no frame shows an open leaf. The vents ship as a fixed head band, never as an operable sash.

The FRONT PORCH's plan outline and its handrails. The platform is named and located on the 2025 Open House plan but is absent from campus-arcgis.json entirely, so its rectangle, its step width and its ramp width are proportions off a tour map and are labelled [estimated]. The LIFT, the riser, the going and the ramp run are NOT estimates — they are the 2022 CBC maxima for a single-run ramp and the flight that divides that rise into whole steps — but no handrail is built, because CBC 1012.8 would require one on a ramp of this rise and the plan draws neither its position nor its return.

The CEQA/EIR record ceqanet 2016111019 — unmined in this pass and still the likeliest public source for a real height in feet, a parapet elevation and per-building floor areas. It would close the height conflict outright and would probably replace a dozen of the [estimated] rows in `figures`.

The HKS project page, which returns 403 to WebFetch and to curl and needs a real browser or web.archive.org. It is the design architect's own page and may carry facade drawings that would replace several [estimated] figures here.

Google Street View of Theatre District Drive, which would give a near-frontal ground-level south-east elevation and settle the bay module to better than the ±0.1 m achieved here. Not reachable from this tool set; the bay module is the one facade number a later pass could still improve.

Everything OUTSIDE Sankofa: Survivance, the Market Hall, Podemos and its academic wing, Azad, Pulse, the Meditation Pavilion, the Ramble and the basketball court all belong to other sections and are deliberately untouched here.

TREES, planting and ground surfacing around Sankofa. The measured LiDAR canopies already stand on this site and the Eighth landscape section owns the ground; nothing is added, per the standing finding that the correct tree work on this site is subtractive.

conflicts: HEIGHT, declared SOURCE CONFLICT, resolved in favour of the DRAWN prism. UC San Diego's own CEQA Addendum No. 5 (2020-09-01, Table 2.5-1) publishes 120 ft = 36.58 m to roof top for Building 3, and phf26 corroborates it (grade to the top of the brow fascia is 10.77 storey-equivalents). campus-arcgis.json massing[464].h is 33.5 m, which is exactly 11 x 3.048 (levels x 10 ft) - a formula, not a survey. The drawn prism is nonetheless what campus-massing.js extrudes on screen, and York's 2026-08-17 audit failure was a skin solved on a taller claim than the drawn box: the membrane floated 6 m over the drawn parapet. So EVERY datum here solves on 33.5 m / 11 storeys = 3.045 m floor-to-floor, and the published 36.58 m / 3.325 m is recorded but not built. When the massing is re-surveyed, grid.publishedHeight is the number to move to.

MARKET HALL WING HEIGHT. massing[462].h = 6.1 is 2 x 3.048, the same discredited formula, and the aerials show the south-east pavilion end is clearly taller. No source resolves it. The drawn 6.1 m prism is what ships; the pavilion's extra height is in `absent`.

LEVEL 11 PLAN REGISTRATION. The published L11 plan agrees with the surveyed ring on total length (81 vs 82.1 m), on depth (18.5 m) and on the kink angle (16.6-16.9 deg vs the surveyed 16.7 deg) - the two documents describe the same building - but it places the south kink about 12 m further east. The ring is therefore a simplified survey outline, not a traced floor plate. The plan is used here for what EXISTS and for proportions, and never to place anything in world coordinates. Everything it alone would have located is in `absent`.

THE MARIGOLD RIBBON'S LEAN, declared SOURCE CONFLICT, resolved in favour of building it as a WHOLE-STOREY GRID SHEAR. The overcast north-elevation frame reads the marigold stripes leaning 6.8 deg off vertical ((175,120)->(290,1090) = 115 px lateral over 970 px vertical). Two readings fit that measurement. (a) The facade grid itself is sheared: every storey's bay grid is offset sideways from the one below, so the openings migrate with the stripes. (b) The stripes are plumb and the 6.8 deg is lens convergence: the frame is a near-frontal but upward-looking shot and no vertical of known plumb was measured in it to cancel keystone. Nothing in the record separates them. Reading (a) SHIPS, because it is the only one that keeps the sourced measurement, and it ships as a shear of the WHOLE storey grid - openings, panel field, jambs and boxes together - because a return jamb that leans while its own opening stays put is a jamb with no wall behind it. Round one built exactly that and left 278 unglazed holes. Reading (b) is recorded in `absent`.

measured.rule: Verbatim from docs/data/campus-arcgis.json, ring coordinates divided by 10 (the survey is in decimetres). Both rings carry the same survey name 'TDLLN - Survivance' and must never be merged: 464 is the 11-storey tower, 462 is the Dining Hall / Market Hall wing. The tower ring lies ENTIRELY inside the wing ring, so the tower's own ground storey is buried inside the wing prism and the podium band, storefront and canopy belong to the WING perimeter - which is the zigzag phf19 photographs the canopy following.

wall.note: Flat metal / composite rainscreen, one panel course per storey with a continuous horizontal reveal at every floor line. THE RAINSCREEN DATUM RULE, which round one broke: the drawn prism is the GIS footprint extruded and campus-massing.js draws it SOLID, so every layer of this section is measured OUTWARD from the prism face and nothing may be placed at or behind it. `standoff` is the innermost plane any layer may occupy; the panel face is standoff + panelDepth = 0.26 m proud; punched glass is recessed window.reveal BEHIND the panel face and is still 0.16 m proud of the prism. Round one placed glass at -0.06 m, terraces at -6.15 m and storefront at -0.10 m, i.e. inside a solid mass, and the test could not see it. Note also that the tower's own L1 and L2 are inside the WING prism, so no tower facade is emitted below the wing lid - see `absent`.
wall.source: Conference Center flyer p.2 (2025-03); EYRC phf19 and phf26 (2024-25); sdarchitecture.org 2025 'serrated facades for natural ventilation'; the standoff and panel depth extend Keeling's own measured rainscreen (docs/data/campus-photo-detail.json keeling.systemB), the nearest same-class wall on this campus.

window.note: 1.70 m x 2.40 m punched opening = 72% of the storey height, measured as 35 x 52 px against the 67.3 px / 3.325 m storey in the same region of the overcast frame. The WIDTH is a plan dimension and ships as measured; the HEIGHT and the SILL ship as their measured FRACTION of the storey, because the drawn prism's storey is 3.045 m rather than the published 3.325 m (conflicts[0]) and a 2.40 m opening with a 0.70 m sill does not fit inside it. The reveal depth and the frame face are NOT measurable in any frame and extend Keeling's measured window (reveal 0.10, frame 0.07); the slot window's width is derived as one third of the punched opening, because no frame resolves it.
window.source: Conference Center flyer p.2 exterior photograph (2025-03, photo 2024-25)

marigold.note: THE SIGNATURE MOVE. Each feature bay is a punched window in a box popped out of the panel plane and rotated six degrees - gbd magazine publishes the mechanism and the +30% airflow figure - so the exposed return jamb reads marigold. The POP-OUT DEPTH is derived from the rotation itself: a 2.19 m box turned 6 deg displaces its leading corner by boxW/2 x sin 6 deg = 0.115 m, so the box must stand at least that proud of the panel plane or the rotation cuts into the wall; it ships at 2 x 0.1225 = 0.245 m so the return is a full jamb and not a sliver, and the JAMB WIDTH is that same pop-out, because the jamb IS the box's own side. The LEAN measured in the overcast frame (115 px lateral over 970 px vertical = 6.8 deg) ships as an ANGLE re-solved on the drawn 3.045 m storey (0.363 m per floor, not the 0.40 m derived on the published 3.325 m storey), and it is applied to the WHOLE STOREY GRID - see conflicts[3]. At both ends of every face the grid is CLIPPED to the surveyed face: a bay that would walk past a corner is dropped and the strip it leaves is closed with blank panel, because nothing may hover past the ring and nothing may leave an unglazed hole.
marigold.distribution: Continuous one-per-bay on the east wing's north face and across the whole south elevation; every other bay on the west bar's north face (122 px vs the 92.5 px bay); ABSENT entirely from both end walls.
marigold.source: Conference Center flyer p.2 (colour-threshold pass R>200, G 150-215, B<160, R-B>70 over rows y500-900 isolated all 14 stripes); gbdmagazine.com 2025; EYRC phf26 (south, dusk) and phf19 (east end, none)

ribbon.note: [estimated] mullion pitch. The Level 11 Theatre District Conference Center is a continuous teal-tinted glazed band one storey tall wrapping every face and stepping at both plan kinks - the single most identifying feature of Survivance from any distance, sourced beyond doubt. Its MULLION PITCH was never counted against a calibrated span, so it extends the sourced 4.30 m bay module at a half-bay, 2.15 m. Since round one the band runs on ALL SIX faces, because the three L11 terraces it used to be interrupted by cannot be built inside a solid prism - see `absent`.
ribbon.source: EYRC phf19 (2024-25); Conference Center flyer p.2 (2025-03); EYRC phf26 and phf17 at dusk, where the same band reads warm-gold from within

terraces.source: Conference Center flyer p.1 LEVEL 11 PLAN (WEST PATIO, chamfered SW corner, lounge chairs and low tables drawn) + EYRC phf26, which photographs the deep cantilever and its two round columns.

terraces.patternRef: the plan's 3.35 m x 43.7 m SOUTH PATIO
terraces.source: Conference Center flyer p.1 LEVEL 11 PLAN (SOUTH PATIO, a long roofed terrace with planters and cafe tables). Its EXISTENCE and depth are the plan's; [estimated] is only which surveyed segments it runs along, because the plan's south kink sits about 12 m east of the ring's - see conflicts[2].
EYRC phf19 (2024-25): the east end opens to a small roofed terrace with a frameless glass guardrail under the brow.

l11.guardSource: 1.07 m is the CBC R-2 guard minimum (42 in) and is what phf26 reads against the balcony slab pitch; the same figure carries every guard and the parapet here.
l11.rooms: The plan publishes 1 large conference room (SV126, podium, two drop-down screens, 210 theatre / 450 standing), 3 meeting rooms (SV122, SV120, plus Pre-Function), 1 board room (SV105, 12 executive chairs), a staff office, a three-car lift bank, a scissor stair, an AV rack room, a catering/prep kitchen, an IT control room, an all-gender restroom and an arrow to hotel rooms. NONE of it is built - see conflicts[2] and `absent`.
l11.builtNote: NOT BUILT, and that is a change from round one. All three terraces are voids cut into the top storey, and campus-massing.js extrudes the surveyed ring as a SOLID prism with no notch: a deck at -6.15 m, a glass guard at -0.08 m and an enclosure glazing at -3.2 m are all inside solid geometry and cannot be seen from anywhere. Round one shipped exactly that - four decks, four guards, four caps and four enclosure lites, entombed - and called the top storey of four elevations complete. The terraces stay here as sourced FACTS (the plan names WEST PATIO and SOUTH PATIO and phf19 shows the east one) and are declared in `absent`. What ships on those faces is the L11 ribbon band, which is the same glazing line and is genuinely visible.

balconies.patternRef: bay.module - one 4.30 m bay less a 0.4 m return
balconies.note: A column of projecting trapezoidal slabs at the WEST end of the south face, immediately east of the west end wall. Metal picket guard on the outer edge only; every soffit is lit (a bright point source under each slab in phf26); a full-height glazed sliding door behind each. Nine slabs counted directly at displayed y 130, 320, 505, 700, 890, 1085, 1290, 1490, 1690 in the 3x crop - 195 displayed px, one storey. L2-L10 is inferred: nine balconies on an 11-storey building whose L11 is an open terrace and whose L1 is the lobby. Projection 2.4 m from 190 displayed px against the 195 px storey pitch, reduced for the oblique (band 2.0-3.2 m). The WIDTH along the facade is [estimated] from the bay module - the photograph is too oblique to measure it. ONLY THE SLABS CLEAR OF THE WING PRISM ARE BUILT: on level ground the L2 slab lands at 3.05 m and the L3 slab at 6.09 m, both at or under the wing's drawn 6.10 m lid and both inside the wing ring, so they would be solid-buried geometry. Which of them is buried depends on the two prisms' rim medians, so the module decides it against the drawn lids rather than by a hard-coded level, and the count is declared in `absent`. That is the conflicts[0]/[1] height shortfall showing locally and is not a reason to move a sourced level.
balconies.source: EYRC phf26 (2024-25), crops p26_westend.png and p26_balc.png

brow.note: THE DEFINING OBJECT: one thin planar roof oversailing the whole building at L11 head height, folding at both plan kinks, charcoal fascia, ribbed soffit, a continuous concealed LED cove that outlines the entire building in one warm line at night. It is built as a MITRED ANNULUS offset outward from the surveyed ring, so the folds are the ring's own folds and no corner opens a gap. Typical projection 1.64 m, measured at the north-east arris in phf19 as 40 displayed px against an 81 displayed px storey (band 1.6-2.0 m). THE WEST CANTILEVER AND ALL THREE COLUMNS ARE NOT BUILT - see `absent`. Round one stood them on the L11 terrace slab; that slab cannot be built inside a solid prism, so the columns were left standing on nothing 30 m in the air, 3.07 m outboard of the ring. A column with nothing under it is worse than an absent column.
brow.source: EYRC phf26 (the west cantilever, the columns, the fold, the cove), phf19 (the projection at the NE arris), phf17 (the continuous night cove), phf15 (the brow as a plane outboard of and below the parapet)

parapet.patternRef: l11.guard.height - the same 1.07 m CBC guard this building uses at every balcony and terrace
parapet.note: [estimated] HEIGHT. No frame resolves the parapet: phf15 is near-nadir so it foreshortens to a line, and phf19 and phf26 hide it behind the brow. It EXISTS beyond doubt (phf15 shows a continuous parapet line with a thin dark coping) - only the height is extended, from this building's own sourced 1.07 m guard. Replaced the day an elevation turns up.

membrane.note: Bright white single-ply (TPO) over the whole deck, clipped to the surveyed ring as a filled polygon rather than a bounding box, so it cannot oversail the kink.
membrane.source: EYRC phf15 near-nadir drone frame (2024-25), crop surv_roof.png at 6x

roof.anchorSource: A line of small evenly spaced vertical studs along the roof edge in phf19 - fall-arrest anchors or window-washing tie-offs. The PITCH is the sourced 4.30 m bay module; the SETBACK is the 6 ft (1.829 m) unprotected-edge distance of OSHA 1910.28(b)(1)(i), which is what such a line is for; the post is an 18 in (0.457 m) stud in 2 in (0.0508 m) square section. Existence is sourced, every dimension is derived from that standard and none is counted in frame.

penthouses.source: The taller elevator-overrun / machine-room box that breaks the skyline in the Conference Center flyer p.2 north elevation and in phf19; placed at the plan kink, where both penthouses sit in phf15. Clad in the same pale panel as the walls (colour sampled separately at p2-000 (1280,115)).
The lower, longer LOUVRED mechanical enclosure immediately south-west of the overrun, with legible horizontal louvre blades on its flank (phf15, phf19).

roof.penthouseNote: Both penthouses are placed at the plan kink where phf15 shows them. EXISTENCE, kind and relative footprint are sourced; every dimension is [estimated] against the 4.30 m bay module - the overrun reads about two bays by one and a half (8.60 x 6.45 m) and the plant enclosure about three by one and a half (12.90 x 6.45 m). The overrun's 12 ft height is a machine-room-less lift overrun and the enclosure's 8 ft is a standard plant screen. THE GATE: the test re-derives every corner of both boxes inside the surveyed ring at not less than parapet.thickness + 0.5 = 0.963 m of edge clearance; measured, the tighter of the two clears 3.98 m. Round one's note claimed the test enforced 4.2 m, which it never did - the prose oversold its own gate and has been corrected.
roof.mechNote: Roughly 8-10 discrete items are legible in phf15 - boxy RTUs, small cylindrical exhaust fans, duct and pipe runs, a linear tray - but individual footprints fall below the frame's resolution, so the COUNT (10) is sourced and each item's exact position and size is [estimated]. Every one is placed inside the surveyed ring with at least parapet.thickness + 0.5 = 0.963 m of edge clearance, which the test re-derives corner by corner; measured, the tightest clears 3.6 m. No skylights are visible and none is built.
roof.mechPatternRef: the 8-10 units counted in EYRC phf15 (2024-25)

pv.note: ABSENT, and it ships as a declared absence rather than as silence. The Keeling PV trap running backwards: the 2021 design renderings (Revelle town-hall deck slides 4 and 16) draw large dark-blue PV fields on the Eighth roofs; the built record does not. Three independent built frames agree that this roof carries white membrane, a parapet, two penthouses, ducts and RTUs and nothing else - EYRC phf15 (near-nadir, bright daylight, the entire deck legible), SWA Learning-1 (aerial from the east) and EYRC phf17 (dusk aerial). The control that makes the negative credible is that Keeling Apartments' own rooftop PV is plainly visible in the very same phf15 frame.

canopy.patternRef: the canopy photographed following the plan's zigzag in EYRC phf19

podium.note: The base band, the storefront and the broad flat canopy belong to the WING ring, not the tower's: the tower ring lies entirely inside the wing ring, so the tower's own ground storey is buried. That is also what the photographs show - phf19 has the canopy following the plan's zigzag, which is this 16-vertex ring. THE WHOLE BASE IS SET OUT ON ONE PRODUCT MODULE, standard modular brick: three courses to 8 in, so one course is 67.7 mm. The band is one storey, 3.0455 m = 45 courses (45 x 67.7 = 3.047 m, 1.5 mm absorbed in the joints); the plinth is 6 courses (0.406 m); the storefront is 36 courses = exactly 8 ft (2.437 m), the standard head height; and the brick header over it is the remaining 3 courses (0.203 m). 6 + 36 + 3 = 45. The pier is 5 nominal 8 in units (1.016 m) at two bays (8.60 m) and projects two brick widths (0.184 m); the band stands one 3-5/8 in wythe plus a 50 mm ventilated cavity (0.142 m) proud of the drawn prism, and the storefront glass is recessed one wythe (0.092 m) behind the brick face and is still proud of the prism. The brick band skirts to the lowest drawn ground along each segment, so the exposed height varies with the falling site and nothing hovers. The L2 band above the canopy - pale panel with a clerestory strip - is [estimated], extending the tower's sourced panel field and the sourced storefront pattern across a zone no frame resolves head-on. The canopy is on the eight segments phf19 photographs it following, NOT on all sixteen: round one wrapped it round the whole ring, which drove it straight through the 9145 garage portal on the west face.
podium.patternRef: wall (the tower's sourced panel field) + podium.storefront
podium.source: Conference Center flyer p.2 (2025-03, the fullest record of the base); EYRC phf19 (the canopy following the zigzag, the storefront bays); EYRC phf26 (the base at the west end)

forecourt.note: The stepped seat-wall terrace and the raised planters flanking the entry, both standing on the DRAWN terrain rather than on the podium. The riser is a 17 in (0.432 m) seat height, which is what a seat wall is; three tiers is what the frame shows. THE PLANTERS ARE PLACED CLEAR OF THE STEPS along the face: their inner edge starts one `gap` past the outer end of the terrace, because round one overlapped them by 0.30 x 0.30 x 0.58 m and 0.31 x 0.30 x 0.50 m. The ramped walk and its stainless tube guardrails are NOT built - see `absent`.

entries.source: Conference Center flyer p.2 (2025-03): a glazed entrance under the canopy reached by a ramped walk with stainless tube guardrails and a stepped seat-wall terrace in warm tan concrete, raised planters of low chaparral planting flanking it, the SURVIVANCE wordmark applied to the dark brick east of the doors in individual metal letters with two small round wall lights above. The segment is the wing's north frontage the tower's north-east face addresses. Cap height reads 0.25-0.35 m against the 3.325 m storey and ships at a standard 12 in (0.305 m); the opening is four 5 ft storefront modules (6.096 m) and its head is the storefront head (0.406 + 2.437 = 2.843 m), which is the continuous head line the frame shows across the whole base.
entries.patternRef: 0.25-0.35 m read against the storey in the same frame; 12 in standard cap height

entries.source: EYRC phf26 (2024-25): the garage-and-loading portal numbered 9145 in the blank base under the balcony stack, with a flush metal service door beside it. Four levels of subterranean parking sit under this building (Walter P Moore) and none of it surfaces except this portal and the 5,000 GSF loading dock. The opening is two 10 ft lanes (6.096 m) and its head is the storefront head (2.843 m), so the whole base carries one head line; the 14 ft loading clearance is inside at the dock, not at this portal, and no frame resolves the portal's own head against a calibrated span.
EYRC phf26 (2024-25): the flush metal service door beside the 9145 portal. One 3 ft 0 in leaf plus a 2 in frame (0.965 m) in a 7 ft (2.134 m) opening - the standard commercial single door.

address.source: Conference Center flyer p.2 footer (2025-03); EYRC phf26 (2024-25)

roof.note: One large roof plane over the whole 16-vertex ring with a thin pale edge trim running the entire perimeter; the surface reads mid grey. It is built as a filled polygon with the TOWER RING PUNCHED OUT as a hole, because the tower rises through it - a roof plate laid over the bounding box would pass straight through the tower. The roof is FOLDED in both aerials; no source gives the ridge line or the pitch, so it ships flat at the drawn lid and the fold is in `absent`.
roof.source: SWA Learning-1 (2025-04 upload); EYRC phf17 and phf19 (2024-25)

festoon.patternRef: the festoon run photographed at the plaza edge in phf26
festoon.note: Festoon lighting strung under the canopy at the plaza edge. EXISTENCE is sourced; WHICH surveyed segments it runs along is [estimated] to the wing's south-east plaza frontage, because no frame resolves both ends of the run against the ring. IT HANGS FROM THE CANOPY SOFFIT, not from a free-standing height: round one hung it at a flat 3.60 m above the podium base, which put 12 lamps above the canopy plate with nothing holding them, 8 inside the slab, and sagged one run 0.06 x 34.9 m = 2.09 m so the lowest lamp hung at chest height. The run is now broken into 20 ft (6.096 m) spans - the standard commercial festoon span - and sags sagFraction of ONE SPAN, and the cord is a polyline through the lamps rather than one straight bar per segment.

wallPanel.source: Median of three separated 6x6 px samples on the overcast-daylight north elevation (Conference Center flyer p.2, 2559x1405 @300 ppi): #e9e9eb, #eae9ea, #e7e8ec. The 4-unit spread across separated points is what makes this albedo rather than a lighting artefact; overcast is the most colour-honest frame this building has.

marigold.source: Same overcast north-elevation frame, on a rotated-bay return at p2-000 (1506, 480). Corroborated as a distinct family by the colour-threshold pass (R>200, G 150-215, B<160, R-B>70) that isolated all 14 stripes.

ribbonGlass.source: Same overcast frame at p2-000 (1728, 275), glass body colour clear of reflection. Corroborated as a deep teal / sea-green in phf19 (sunlit, from the north-east) and as warm-gold from within at dusk in phf26 and phf17.

browFascia.source: Same overcast frame at p2-000 (768, 262). The lit flank of the same element reads #696c73 at (1856, 243), which brackets the material as a near-black charcoal metal.

browSoffit.source: The lit flank of the brow in the same overcast frame at p2-000 (1856, 243) - the same charcoal metal read in direct rather than shadowed light, which is what the uplit soffit shows.

penthousePanel.source: Same overcast frame at p2-000 (1280, 115). Same panel family as the wall field read in ambient rather than direct light, so the penthouses are clad in the same system as the tower.

podiumBrick.source: Region medians on the overcast frame at (1600-2000, 1080-1180) -> #706d6c, with point samples at (1745,1124) -> #807e7e and (1849,1113) -> #726e77. ALL SAMPLED IN SHADE under the canopy: the true albedo is lighter and warmer than this. Flagged rather than silently corrected.

canopySoffit.source: Overcast frame at p2-000 (1544, 954), the underside of the flat entry canopy.

windowGlass.source: SWA Learning-16, k-means cluster n=2464 (eighthPulse's sample) - the same tinted IGU family as Pulse. ARBITRATION: the earlier #abc4cb was an overcast SKY REFLECTION at p2-000 (1532,555), i.e. the specular appearance, not the albedo. This section's own note already recorded that under direct sun the same glass reads a deep petrol blue in phf19, which is this value. The pale reflection is produced by the material's specular path in campus-materials.js and must not also be baked into the base colour.

siteConcrete.source: Overcast frame at p2-000 (1975, 1193), the stepped seat-wall terrace flanking the entry ramp.

roofMembrane.source: [estimated] hex. phf15 resolves the deck as bright white single-ply beyond doubt, but it is a near-nadir daylight frame with no neutral reference in it, so no honest sample can be taken. The value extends this building's own pale panel family read in ambient light (penthousePanel #e2e3e3), lifted slightly for a white membrane.

coping.source: The parapet coping reads as the same continuous charcoal line as the brow fascia in phf15 and phf19, so it carries the fascia's own sample at p2-000 (768, 262). One material, two roles.

mullion.source: [estimated] hex. The slender mullions of the L11 ribbon and the storefront are plainly dark in every frame but are one to two pixels wide, so any sample is a blend with the glass behind. The value extends this building's sourced charcoal metal (browFascia #32313a), lifted a little because the mullion is anodised rather than painted.

storefrontGlass.source: [estimated] hex. The ground-storey storefront is in deep canopy shadow in every frame that shows it, so a sample would carry the canopy, not the glass. The value extends the sourced residential IGU (windowGlass #abc4cb), darkened for the taller, less reflective storefront lite.

railMetal.source: [estimated] hex. Balcony pickets, stainless tube entry guardrails and terrace guard caps read as bare pale metal in every frame but are all thinner than a reliable sample window. The value is the sourced pale panel family (wallPanel #e9e9eb) taken down to a bare-metal value.

coveLight.patternRef: the warm cove and lit balcony soffits photographed at dusk
coveLight.source: [estimated] hex. phf26 and phf17 both show the brow's concealed cove and the balcony soffit downlights as a warm white line, but both are dusk exposures with the whole frame graded warm, so the pixel value is the camera's, not the lamp's. A warm-white 2700K value is used and labelled.

roofEquipment.patternRef: the RTUs, fans and duct runs counted in phf15
roofEquipment.source: [estimated] hex. The units are below the frame's resolution, so a sample is aliased sky and membrane. A neutral galvanised grey is used.

wordmarkMetal.source: [estimated] hex. The SURVIVANCE letters are individual applied metal characters on dark brick; at 0.30 m cap height in that frame each stroke is under two pixels. The value extends the sourced pale panel family.

addressBlue.patternRef: the blue applied street numbers photographed across TDLLN (9185, 9165, 9145)
addressBlue.source: [estimated] hex. The 9145 numerals are small and in shade in phf26. A mid campus blue is used and labelled.

wingRoof.patternRef: the mid-grey roof surface read in both aerials
wingRoof.source: [estimated] hex. Both aerials that show the wing roof are oblique and at a distance; the surface reads mid grey but no sample survives the atmosphere between camera and roof. A neutral mid grey is used.

wingTrim.source: [estimated] hex. The thin pale edge trim running the wing roof's whole perimeter is one to two pixels deep in every frame. The value extends the sourced pale panel family.

absent: THE PARAPET'S TRUE HEIGHT. It is built at 1.07 m, [estimated] from this building's own sourced guard height. No frame resolves it: phf15 is near-nadir so the parapet foreshortens to a line, phf19 and phf26 hide it behind the brow. Replaced the day a dimensioned elevation turns up.

THE NORTH-WEST CORE-BLOCK STEP. The L11 plan shows the north boundary bevelling out and running about 1.7 m further north for roughly 12 m where the core - catering kitchen, scissor stair, three-car lift bank, lobby - projects past the residential bar. It is NOT built: the plan's south kink sits about 12 m east of the surveyed ring's, so the plan cannot place a 1.7 m step in world coordinates, and a step guessed onto the wrong metre would push geometry outside the surveyed footprint. The slot-window column that marks the core zone IS built, because it lies in the wall plane. See conflicts[2].

EVERY LEVEL 11 INTERIOR WALL AND ROOM. The flyer publishes the whole plan - SV126 the Large Conference Room, SV122, SV120, SV105 the Board Room, Pre-Function, the AV rack room, the catering/prep kitchen, the IT control room, the three-car lift bank, the scissor stair, the all-gender restroom, the staff office and an arrow to hotel rooms - and none of it is placed, for the same 12 m registration reason. Only what is legible on the OUTSIDE (the ribbon, the three terraces, the guards) is built.

THE MARKET HALL WING'S FOLD AND PITCH. Both aerials show a single large FOLDED / sloping roof plane whose zigzag edge follows the ring. No source gives a ridge line or a pitch, so the plane ships flat at the drawn lid.

THE MARKET HALL WING'S TRUE HEIGHT. massing[462].h = 6.1 m is 2 x 3.048, the same discredited formula that made the tower's 33.5 m wrong by 3.1 m, and the aerials show the pavilion end is clearly taller. Nothing resolves it, so the drawn prism ships and the pavilion's extra height is not invented.

THE MARKET HALL WING'S COURTYARD VOID. A rectangular courtyard void / light well with its own raised parapet and planting inside it is cut through the roof in the wing's western third (SWA Learning-1, phf17). Its outline and size are not measurable from either frame, so no hole is cut - better absent than a hole in the wrong place.

THE SOUTH-EAST GLAZED PAVILION as a distinct taller volume. It exists (SWA Learning-1, phf17, phf26) but its height and its footprint within the 16-vertex ring are both unresolved, so it ships as part of the wing's own prism rather than as an invented mass.

THE PLAZA IN FRONT OF THE MARKET HALL - the rectangular water feature / reflecting basin and the lawn panel visible in phf19 and phf26. They are landscape outside both surveyed rings and belong to the Eighth landscape section, not to this building.

ROOFTOP PHOTOVOLTAICS: zero modules, zero racks, zero canopy, against 2021 renderings that drew large PV fields. Three built frames agree the deck carries membrane, parapet, two penthouses, ducts and RTUs and nothing else - EYRC phf15, SWA Learning-1, EYRC phf17 - with Keeling's own rooftop PV visible in the very same phf15 frame as the control. See roof.pv.

PER-FACE MARIGOLD COUNTS beyond the two the photographs cover. 6 stripes were counted on the west bar's north face and 8 on the east wing's, but that frame does not cover either face end to end and the whole south elevation was only ever shot at dusk. What ships is the sourced 4.30 m module, the sourced distribution rule (continuous / alternate / none), and per-face bay counts of which only TWO are counted in frame - north-west 11 and east-end 4. The other four are DERIVED as round(faceLength / 4.30) and are labelled `derived` in faces[].bayCountTier; round one's prose called all six 'the photographed count', which was not true of four of them.
THE BROW'S WEST CANTILEVER REACH past the terrace edge - superseded by the entry below, which withholds the whole cantilever and its columns.

FLOOR-TO-FLOOR VARIATION. Only the total is sourced. The photograph says the module is near-uniform (10 storeys occupy 659 px and the fascia sits at 10.77 storey-equivalents) but the individual L1 and L2 heights are not separately resolved, so one uniform storey is drawn.
THE L11 RIBBON'S MULLION PITCH, never counted against a calibrated span; it ships at a half-bay and is labelled [estimated].

THE BALCONY WIDTH along the facade, and independent confirmation of which levels are served. Nine slabs are counted directly; L2-L10 is inferred from nine balconies on an 11-storey building whose L11 is an open terrace and whose L1 is the lobby.

THE FOUR SUBTERRANEAN PARKING LEVELS under this building. They exist (Walter P Moore) and nothing of them surfaces on this footprint except the 9145 portal and the loading dock, so nothing below grade is drawn.

INTERIORS of every kind - the eucalyptus-leaf lobby mural, the Community Demonstration Kitchen, the Game Room, the study rooms, the conference centre fit-out. Photographed (phf07/09/11/32/35) but this section models the exterior envelope only.
SKYLIGHTS. None is visible in phf15 and none is built.
PLANT SPECIES anywhere on this building. The entry planters carry low chaparral planting in the flyer photograph; no frame resolves a species, so the planters ship as planters and nothing is named.

THE THREE LEVEL 11 TERRACES - the WEST PATIO, the SOUTH PATIO and the east terrace - and the frameless glass guards that edge them. They are sourced beyond doubt (the flyer p.1 plan names two of them and phf19 photographs the third) and they are NOT BUILT, because a terrace is a void cut into the top storey and campus-massing.js extrudes the surveyed ring as a SOLID prism with no notch. Round one drew the decks 1.6-6.15 m inside that solid mass, the guards 0.08 m inside it and the enclosure glazing 3.2-6.15 m inside it: four decks, four guards, four caps and four lites of invisible geometry, on the top storey of four of the six elevations. Nothing may be drawn inside a solid mass. The L11 ribbon band ships on all six faces instead, because it is the same glazing line and is genuinely on the outside. The terraces return the day the massing carries a notch.

THE BROW'S WEST CANTILEVER AND ALL THREE OF ITS COLUMNS. phf26 photographs a deep cantilever over the West Patio on two round columns, and a third column stands at the north-east arris. Its clear height (4.4 m) and the column diameter (0.83 m) are measured against the 1.7 m human figures standing in the same plane; its REACH past the terrace edge never was. All of it is withheld, because the columns land on the L11 terrace slab and that slab cannot be built (see the entry above): round one shipped them standing on nothing 30 m in the air and 3.07 m outboard of the surveyed ring, while the section's own note said they landed on the slab. The uniform 1.64 m mitred brow annulus, which IS measured, still ships on every face including this one.

THE TOWER'S OWN LEVEL 1 AND LEVEL 2 FACADE. The tower ring lies entirely inside the wing ring and the wing prism is 6.10 m tall, so the tower's lowest two storeys are inside another solid mass. No panel, window, reveal, marigold box or skirt is emitted below the wing lid - round one built about 390 panel pieces, 96 glazings, 68 marigold boxes with their jambs, 112 mullions and 18 reveals down there, none of which can be seen from anywhere. What the eye actually reads at that height is the WING's podium, which is built in full.

THE L2 AND L3 BALCONY SLABS of the nine-slab stack - whichever of them the drawn prisms bury. On level ground the L2 slab lands at 3.05 m and the L3 slab at 6.09 m against the wing's drawn 6.10 m lid, and both sit inside the wing ring, so both would be buried in the wing prism together with their guards, pickets, doors and soffit lights. On the falling site the two prisms seat on different rim medians and the count can be one rather than two, so the module re-derives it from the drawn lids at build time and the test re-derives the same number independently. The rest of the nine sourced slabs are built. This is the conflicts[0]/[1] height shortfall showing locally.

THE NORTH ENTRY'S RAMPED WALK and its stainless tube guardrails. The flyer photograph shows both. The walk's rise is the fall from the drawn terrain to the entry threshold, which this repo's terrain does not resolve at that precision under this segment, and a ramp guessed at the wrong gradient is a trip hazard drawn as architecture. The rails go with it: round one built the rails and not the walk, so they served nothing.

ANY MECHANICAL EQUIPMENT ON THE MARKET HALL WING'S 4,157 m2 ROOF. A dining hall of 22,750 GSF has kitchen exhaust, make-up air and refrigeration plant on it, and both aerials are too oblique and too distant to resolve a single unit. A bare plate ships and nothing is invented on it. This is a declared gap, not a claim that the roof is empty - unlike the TOWER roof, where phf15 IS near-nadir and the absence of PV is a measured negative.

THE READING THAT THE MARIGOLD RIBBON DOES NOT LEAN AT ALL. The 6.8 deg is measured off a single near-frontal but upward-looking frame with no vertical of known plumb in it, so it cannot be separated from lens convergence. What ships is the whole-storey grid shear of conflicts[3]; if the stripes turn out to be plumb, every leaning row in this section is one edit away - set marigold.leanDeg to 0 and the grid stops shearing.

THE CANOPY'S TRUE EXTENT around the 16-vertex wing ring. It is built on the eight segments phf19 photographs it following and is [estimated] there; whether it continues round the west and south frontages is not resolved by any frame, and it demonstrably does NOT continue across the 9145 garage portal.

windowGlass was re-pointed to the Pulse curtain-wall value (#2c4c5c) in arbitration: the two buildings share one glass family and the earlier 4x luminance gap between this section's #abc4cb and eighthPulse's #2c4c5c was an illuminant/geometry error, not a material difference. What stays absent is a SUNLIT, square-on median of this building's own glass — every frame of Survivance's curtain wall in the set is either overcast or oblique, so the albedo shipped here is Pulse's measurement adopted for the same product rather than a read of this facade.

bay.module.basis: FFT of the horizontal luminance profile over three blank wall patches of the Conference Center flyer p.2 overcast north elevation (2025-03 PDF, photograph 2024-25): dominant period 83.3 px (x1250-1500) and 100.0 px (x400-900) against the 67.3 px / 3.325 m storey in the same region = 4.11 m and 4.94 m. Cross-checks: 208.41 m ring perimeter / 4.30 = 48.5 bays; 390 beds / 8 residential floors = 48.75 beds per floor.

bay.total.basis: Sum of the six per-face counts (11+4+9+10+4+10), two counted in frame and four derived as round(faceLength/4.30) - see faces[].bayCountBasis. Independently 208.41 / 4.30 = 48.5.

faces[].bays.basis: Per face: `photographed` where the bays are counted in a named frame (north-west 11, east-end 4) and `derived` as round(faceLength / bay.module) for the other four. Every face carries its own tier in bayCountTier and its own arithmetic in bayCountBasis; the WIDTH is always faceLength/count, never the module, so no bay runs past a surveyed corner.

wall.standoff.basis: [estimated]. No frame resolves the rainscreen cavity. campus-massing.js draws the surveyed prism SOLID, so this is also the hard floor for every layer in the section: nothing may sit at or behind the prism face. The value is Keeling's own measured rainscreen standoff on this campus, 0.12 m, and the same class of wall.

wall.panelDepth.basis: [estimated]. The panel cassette's own depth, not resolvable at this range in any frame. Keeling's measured panel thickness is 0.14 m; the same figure is used, giving a panel face 0.26 m proud of the drawn prism.

wall.reveal.height.basis: [estimated]. The horizontal shadow gap at each floor line is legible in the Conference Center flyer p.2 overcast north elevation (2025-03 PDF, photograph 2024-25) but is one to two pixels deep, below any calibrated read.
