It extends Keeling's measured frame band (0.28 x 0.20 m) reduced to a shadow gap at 0.09 x 0.09 m.

wall.reveal.depth.basis: [estimated]. Same reveal, same reason; the depth is set equal to the height so the groove reads square, and it is shallower than the 0.14 m panel so the groove cannot cut back to the prism.

window.width.basis: 35 px against the 67.3 px / 3.325 m storey in the same region of the Conference Center flyer p.2 overcast north elevation (2025-03 PDF, photograph 2024-25) = 1.73 m; ships at 1.70 m. A plan dimension, so it ships as measured rather than as a fraction of the storey.

window.measuredHeight.basis: 52 px against the same 67.3 px storey = 2.57 m; ships at 2.40 m after the oblique correction. RECORDED, NOT BUILT - see heightFraction and conflicts[0].

window.measuredSill.basis: The sill line in the same column of the same frame, 0.70 m at the published storey. RECORDED, NOT BUILT - see sillFraction.

window.measuredStorey.basis: The published 36.58 m / 11 storeys = 3.325 m, the datum the two figures above were measured against. RECORDED, NOT BUILT - conflicts[0].

window.heightFraction.basis: 2.40 / 3.325 = 0.7218. The opening ships as its measured PROPORTION of the storey, because the drawn prism's storey is 3.0455 m and a 2.40 m opening with a 0.70 m sill does not fit inside it.

window.sillFraction.basis: 0.70 / 3.325 = 0.2105. The sill ships as its measured PROPORTION of the storey for the same reason as heightFraction: the drawn prism's storey is 3.0455 m, not the published 3.325 m the sill was read against, and a 0.70 m sill under a 2.40 m opening does not fit inside it.

window.slotWidth.basis: No frame resolves the core slot window's width - the flyer locates the column at x 1320-1382 px but that is the column zone, not the glass. It ships as one third of the sourced 1.70 m punched opening, 0.567 m, and it is one figure for the whole building rather than a per-face guess.

window.reveal.basis: [estimated]. The depth the glass is set back behind the panel face; the frames are all too oblique or too distant to read it. Keeling's measured window reveal on this campus is 0.10 m and is used. It is shallower than the 0.26 m panel face, so the glass is still 0.16 m proud of the drawn prism.

window.frame.basis: [estimated]. The dark surround around each punched lite is one to two pixels wide in every frame. Keeling's measured 0.07 m frame face is used.

marigold.rotationDeg.basis: PUBLISHED, not inferred: gbdmagazine.com (2025) states the windows on the lower towers are 'popped out and rotated six degrees' for a +30% airflow gain. This is the one figure in the section that comes from the designers rather than from a photograph.

marigold.rotation.basis: 6 deg in radians = 0.10472, the value the module actually turns the box by.

marigold.popOut.basis: Derived from the rotation itself. A boxW = 1.70 + 2 x 0.245 = 2.19 m box turned 6 deg displaces its leading corner by boxW/2 x sin 6 deg = 1.095 x 0.10453 = 0.1145 m, so the box must stand at least that proud of the panel plane or the rotation cuts back into the wall. It ships at 2 x 0.1225 = 0.245 m so the exposed return is a full jamb and not a sliver. Solved self-consistently with jambWidth.

marigold.jambWidth.basis: The marigold IS the pop-out box's own side face, so the jamb's plan width is the pop-out depth: 0.245 m. One mechanism, one figure - round one carried 0.32 m here and 0.25 m there with nothing joining them.

marigold.leanDeg.basis: (175,120) -> (290,1090) along one marigold stripe in the Conference Center flyer p.2 overcast north elevation (2025-03 PDF, photograph 2024-25) = 115 px lateral over 970 px vertical, atan = 6.76 deg; ships at 6.8 deg. See conflicts[3] for the competing reading of that same measurement.

marigold.measuredStepPerFloor.basis: 3.325 x tan 6.8 deg = 0.397 m, the lateral step at the PUBLISHED storey. RECORDED, NOT BUILT: the module re-solves the ANGLE on the drawn 3.0455 m storey, giving 0.363 m. conflicts[0].

ribbon.mullionPitch.basis: [estimated]. Never counted against a calibrated span in any frame. Extends the sourced 4.30 m bay module at a half-bay, 2.15 m. Replaced the day the pitch is counted.

ribbon.mullionWidth.basis: [estimated]. The ribbon's mullions are one to two pixels wide in every frame that shows them. A standard 2 1/2 in (0.0635 m) curtain-wall mullion face is used.
ribbon.mullionWidth.patternRef: a standard 2 1/2 in curtain-wall mullion face

ribbon.recess.basis: [estimated]. The set-back of the ribbon glass behind the panel face; not resolvable. Set equal to this building's own window reveal so the two glazing lines share one detail.

ribbon.spandrel.basis: The opaque band at the ribbon's foot has to cover the L11 slab edge plus an upstand: 0.229 m post-tensioned slab + 6 in (0.152 m) upstand = 0.381 m.

l11.terraces[].depth.basis: Scaled off the Conference Center flyer p.1 LEVEL 11 PLAN (1635x787 @222 ppi) against that plan's own 18.5 m building depth, which agrees with the surveyed ring: WEST PATIO 6.15 m, SOUTH PATIO 3.35 m; the east terrace 3.2 m from EYRC phf19. NOT BUILT - see l11.builtNote and `absent`.

l11.guard.height.basis: 1.0668 m = 42 in, the CBC/IBC guard minimum for R-2 occupancies, which is what phf26 reads against the balcony slab pitch; ships at 1.07 m and carries every guard and the parapet in this section. NOT BUILT at L11 - see l11.builtNote.
l11.guard.height.patternRef: CBC/IBC 1015.3 - 42 in guard minimum for R-2

balconies.count.basis: Nine slabs counted directly in EYRC phf26 crop p26_balc.png at displayed y 130, 320, 505, 700, 890, 1085, 1290, 1490, 1690 - a 195 px pitch, one storey. Only seven are BUILT; the L2 and L3 slabs are inside the wing prism and are in `absent`.

balconies.projection.basis: 190 displayed px against the 195 px storey pitch in the same crop = 2.97 m, reduced for the oblique to a 2.0-3.2 m band; ships at 2.40 m, the band's midpoint.

balconies.width.basis: [estimated]. The photograph is too oblique to measure the width along the facade. One 4.30 m bay less a 0.40 m return = 3.90 m.

balconies.slabThickness.basis: [estimated]. Walter P Moore publish post-tensioned slabs for this building; a 9 in (0.229 m) PT flat plate is the standard depth at the 8.60 m structural bay this facade's pier pitch implies. No frame resolves the slab edge.
balconies.slabThickness.patternRef: a 9 in post-tensioned flat plate (Walter P Moore, post-2024)

balconies.guardHeight.basis: The same guard minimum as every other guard on this building: 42 in x 0.0254 = 1.0668 m (CBC/IBC 1015.3, R-2), which phf26 corroborates against the 195 px storey pitch; ships at 1.07 m.

balconies.picketWidth.basis: A 5/8 in square bar, the standard picket section: 0.625 x 0.0254 = 0.0159 m. Not measurable in any frame - at this range a picket is under one pixel - so it is the product, not a reading.

balconies.picketPitch.basis: CBC/IBC 1015.4: no opening in a guard may pass a 4 in sphere, so the clear gap is at most 0.1016 m. Pitch = 0.1016 + 0.0159 picket = 0.1175 m, the code maximum. Round one's 0.11 m was a round number nobody derived.

balconies.doorWidth.basis: A standard 6 ft sliding patio door: 6 x 0.3048 = 1.829 m, which is what phf26 shows behind each slab. Round one carried 2.2 m, which matches no product in the catalogue.
balconies.doorWidth.patternRef: a standard 6 ft sliding patio door

balconies.cap.height.basis: The guard's top rail, 2 in square tube: 2 x 0.0254 = 0.0508 m - the standard section for a picket guard's cap.

balconies.cap.depth.basis: The same 2 in square top rail as balconies.cap.height: 2 x 0.0254 = 0.0508 m. One tube, so one section in both directions.

brow.projection.basis: 40 displayed px against an 81 displayed px storey at the north-east arris in EYRC phf19 = 1.50 m at the drawn storey; band 1.6-2.0 m allowing for the arris foreshortening; ships at 1.64 m.

brow.fasciaHeight.basis: [estimated], and it is load-bearing because it sets the soffit line. It is NOT measured: at the arris where phf19 reads the brow, the fascia depth and the projection foreshorten into the same 40 px and cannot be separated. It ships at one third of the measured projection, 0.55 m.

brow.ribPitch.basis: [estimated]. The soffit ribbing is visible in phf26 but was never counted against a calibrated span. Eight ribs to a bay: 4.30 / 8 = 0.5375 m.

brow.ribDepth.basis: A 2 in linear soffit rib: 2 x 0.0254 = 0.0508 m, the standard section for a linear metal soffit. The ribbing is visible in phf26 but no blade is resolvable.

brow.coveSection.basis: The concealed cove channel, 2 in square: 2 x 0.0254 = 0.0508 m - the standard recessed LED channel, and the same section as the soffit rib beside it.

brow.coveDrop.basis: [estimated]. How far the cove sits below the soffit plane so its light washes the fascia; not resolvable in a dusk exposure. 0.09 m, the same shadow-gap dimension the wall's floor-line reveal uses.

roof.parapet.height.basis: [estimated]. No frame resolves it: phf15 is near-nadir so the parapet foreshortens to a line and phf19/phf26 hide it behind the brow. It EXISTS beyond doubt (phf15 shows a continuous parapet line with a thin dark coping); the height extends this building's own 42 in guard.

roof.parapet.thickness.basis: The parapet is the wall assembly turned up: an 8 in (0.2032 m) concrete upstand plus this building's own 0.12 m rainscreen standoff and 0.14 m panel = 0.4632 m; ships at 0.463 m. It also sets the roof-furniture gate at thickness + 0.5 = 0.963 m.

roof.parapet.copingHeight.basis: A formed metal coping with the standard 3 in face: 3 x 0.0254 = 0.0762 m. phf15 and phf19 both read a thin dark line along the parapet but neither resolves its depth.

roof.parapet.copingOverhang.basis: The coping's standard 1 1/2 in (0.038 m) drip past the parapet face, each side.

roof.membrane.inset.basis: The membrane stops at the parapet's INNER face, so the inset is the parapet thickness itself: 0.2032 + 0.12 + 0.14 = 0.463 m. Round one carried an unrelated 0.4 m, which left a 63 mm strip of bare deck under the parapet.

roof.anchors.pitch.basis: [estimated]. The studs are evenly spaced along the roof edge in phf19 but are not countable against a calibrated span; the pitch is set to the sourced bay module.

roof.anchors.inset.basis: OSHA 1910.28(b)(1)(i): the unprotected-edge distance a tie-off line exists to serve is 6 ft (1.829 m).

roof.anchors.height.basis: An 18 in fall-arrest stud: 18 x 0.0254 = 0.457 m, the standard post height. The studs are a line of small verticals in phf19 and none is measurable against a calibrated span.
roof.anchors.height.patternRef: a standard 18 in fall-arrest anchor post

roof.anchors.width.basis: The anchor post's section, 2 in square: 2 x 0.0254 = 0.0508 m - the standard stud for a roof tie-off line.

roof.penthouses[].x.basis: [estimated]. phf15 places both boxes at the plan kink and gives their order and relative size; it gives no coordinate. Positions are set at the kink and every corner is re-derived inside the surveyed ring by the test.
roof.penthouses[].x.patternRef: the plan kink both boxes sit at in EYRC phf15

roof.penthouses[].z.basis: [estimated], for the same reason as x: phf15 places both boxes at the plan kink and gives their order and relative size, and gives no coordinate at all. Every corner is re-derived inside the surveyed ring by the test.
roof.penthouses[].z.patternRef: the plan kink both boxes sit at in EYRC phf15

roof.penthouses[].size.basis: [estimated]. The overrun reads about two bays by one and a half (2 x 4.30 = 8.60 by 1.5 x 4.30 = 6.45 m) and the plant enclosure about three by one and a half (12.90 x 6.45 m). Heights: a machine-room-less lift overrun at 12 ft (3.658 m) and a plant screen at 8 ft (2.4384 m).

roof.penthouses[].louvrePitch.basis: A 6 in (0.1524 m) blade pitch, the standard for an architectural stationary louvre. The blades are legible in phf15/phf19 but not countable.
roof.penthouses[].louvrePitch.patternRef: a standard 6 in louvre blade pitch

roof.mech[].x.basis: [estimated]. The COUNT (10) is what phf15 resolves; individual positions fall below the frame's resolution. Each is placed clear of the parapet and the test re-derives every corner.
roof.mech[].x.patternRef: the 8-10 units counted in EYRC phf15 (2024-25)

roof.mech[].z.basis: [estimated], for the same reason as x: the COUNT is what phf15 resolves and individual positions fall below the frame's resolution. Each unit is placed clear of the parapet and the test re-derives every corner.
roof.mech[].z.patternRef: the 8-10 units counted in EYRC phf15 (2024-25)

roof.mech[].size.basis: [estimated]. Boxy RTUs and duct runs at plausible plant sizes; no footprint is measurable in phf15.
roof.mech[].size.patternRef: the 8-10 units counted in EYRC phf15 (2024-25)

roof.mech[].radius.basis: [estimated]. Small cylindrical exhaust fans; diameter not measurable.
roof.mech[].radius.patternRef: the 8-10 units counted in EYRC phf15 (2024-25)

roof.mech[].height.basis: [estimated]. The cylindrical exhaust fans' height above the deck; at phf15's near-nadir angle a fan is a disc and its height is not readable at all. Plant-plausible values, labelled.
roof.mech[].height.patternRef: the 8-10 units counted in EYRC phf15 (2024-25)

roof.pv.modules.basis: ZERO, and it is a measured negative rather than an omission. Three independent built frames - EYRC phf15 (near-nadir, whole deck legible), SWA Learning-1, EYRC phf17 - agree the deck carries membrane, parapet, two penthouses, ducts and RTUs and nothing else, against 2021 renderings that drew large PV fields. The control that makes the negative credible is Keeling's own rooftop PV, plainly visible in the same phf15 frame.

podium.brickCourse.basis: Standard modular brick: three courses to 8 in, so one course is 2 2/3 in = 0.0677 m. This is the product module the whole base is set out on.

podium.brickHeight.basis: One drawn storey, 3.0455 m = 45 modular courses (45 x 0.0677 = 3.047 m, 1.5 mm absorbed in the joints). The canopy sits on this line, which is what phf19 shows.

podium.plinthHeight.basis: 6 modular brick courses: 6 x 0.0677 = 0.406 m. It is the first term of the 6 + 36 + 3 = 45 course fit that sets the whole base out on one product module.

podium.storefront.height.basis: 36 modular courses = 2.4372 m = exactly 8 ft, the standard storefront head height; ships at 2.437 m.

podium.headerHeight.basis: The remainder of the 45-course band above the storefront head: 45 - 6 - 36 = 3 courses = 0.203 m. Round one's storefront head landed ABOVE the brick top, so zero headers were ever built and the module shipped an InstancedMesh with count 0.

podium.storefront.sill.basis: Zero: the storefront sits directly on its plinth, which is what the 6+36+3 = 45 course fit requires and what the frame shows.

podium.bandDepth.basis: One 3 5/8 in (0.092 m) modular brick wythe plus a 50 mm ventilated cavity = 0.142 m, measured OUTWARD from the drawn prism. Round one placed the band at -0.175 m, entirely inside the solid mass.

podium.storefront.reveal.basis: The glass is recessed exactly one modular brick wythe behind the brick face: 3.625 x 0.0254 = 0.092 m. It therefore sits 0.12 + 0.142 - 0.092 = 0.17 m proud of the drawn prism rather than 0.10 m inside it, which is where round one put it.

podium.pierWidth.basis: 5 nominal 8 in brick units: 5 x 8 x 0.0254 = 1.016 m. A pier is a whole number of units wide or its coursing does not close; 1.1 m, which round one carried, is 5.41 units.

podium.pierPitch.basis: Two structural bays: 2 x 4.30 = 8.60 m. The piers land on the bay module the whole facade is set out on, so no pier ever falls mid-bay.

podium.pierProud.basis: Two brick widths, 2 x 3 5/8 in = 0.184 m, past the band face.

podium.storefront.mullionPitch.basis: [estimated]. The storefront bays are legible in phf19 but are in canopy shadow and not countable against a calibrated span. The standard 5 ft (1.524 m) US storefront framing module is used.
podium.storefront.mullionPitch.patternRef: a standard 5 ft storefront framing module

podium.storefront.mullionWidth.basis: A standard 2 in storefront mullion face: 2 x 0.0254 = 0.0508 m. In every frame that shows the base the mullions are in canopy shadow and under two pixels wide, so this is the product rather than a reading.

podium.canopy.projection.basis: [estimated]. No frame resolves the canopy's depth against a calibrated span; it ships at half the sourced bay module, 2.15 m. At a right-angle vertex the overlapping plates reach 2.15 x sqrt(2) = 3.04 m, which is the widest reach anywhere in this section and is inside the declared 3.6 m envelope pad; measured over the real ring the worst corner is 3.04 m.

podium.canopy.thickness.basis: A 6 in flat-plate canopy assembly: 6 x 0.0254 = 0.152 m, which is what a steel entry canopy of this span is. Round one's 0.28 m matched nothing.

podium.canopy.fascia.basis: The edge fascia hanging below the canopy plate, 4 in: 4 x 0.0254 = 0.102 m. It is two thirds of the 6 in plate above it, which is the standard proportion for a flat-plate canopy edge.

podium.canopy.soffitDepth.basis: [estimated]. The applied soffit lining under the plate, 0.04 m - a lining, not a structure.

podium.clerestory.height.basis: [estimated]. No frame resolves the L2 band head-on. A 4 ft (1.219 m) clerestory strip.

podium.clerestory.sill.basis: [estimated], same band and same reason. A 2 ft (0.610 m) sill above the canopy line.

podium.bury.basis: [estimated]. Nothing is claimed about the foundation. The band already reaches down to the LOWEST drawn ground sampled along each segment; this is the extra 0.30 m it buries below that, so no drawn terrain triangle can pass under the wall.
podium.bury.patternRef: a nominal 300 mm bury below the lowest drawn ground

entries[].u.basis: [estimated]. Where along a surveyed segment each opening sits. The frames show which frontage each is on and roughly where, but the 12 m plan-registration failure (conflicts[2]) means no document places them in world coordinates. Fractions of the segment length, not metres.
entries[].u.patternRef: the frontage each opening is photographed on

entries[].width.basis: north-main: four 5 ft storefront modules = 6.096 m. west-garage: two 10 ft lanes = 6.096 m. west-service: one 3 ft 0 in leaf plus a 2 in frame = 0.965 m. Round one carried 6.2 / 6 / 1.6, none of which matched a product.

entries[].height.basis: north-main and west-garage take the storefront head, plinth + storefront = 0.406 + 2.437 = 2.843 m, so the whole base carries one continuous head line - which is what the frame shows. west-service is a standard 7 ft (2.134 m) door opening. Round one's 4.2 m garage portal punched straight through the canopy plate at 3.05 m.

entries[].wordmark.capHeight.basis: [estimated] on size, not on existence. The letters read 0.25-0.35 m against the 3.325 m storey in the Conference Center flyer p.2 overcast north elevation (2025-03 PDF, photograph 2024-25); a standard 12 in (0.305 m) cap height sits inside that band.
entries[].wordmark.capHeight.patternRef: 0.25-0.35 m read against the storey in the same frame

entries[].wordmark.letterPitch.basis: Cap height x 1.4, the standard set width for applied capitals: 0.305 x 1.4 = 0.427 m.

entries[].wordmark.offset.basis: [estimated]. The wordmark sits on the brick east of the doors; the frame does not measure how far. One entry width, 6.096 m.

entries[].numberHeight.basis: The same applied character height as the wordmark - one signage family on one building: 12 x 0.0254 = 0.305 m.

entries[].wallLights.basis: Two small round wall lights counted directly above the wordmark in the Conference Center flyer p.2 overcast north elevation (2025-03 PDF, photograph 2024-25).

entries[].forecourt.seatTerrace.tiers.basis: Three tiers counted in the Conference Center flyer p.2 overcast north elevation (2025-03 PDF, photograph 2024-25).

entries[].forecourt.seatTerrace.rise.basis: A 17 in seat height: 17 x 0.0254 = 0.432 m, which is what a seat wall is for and is the anthropometric standard. Round one stepped 0.30 / 0.60 / 0.90 m, none of them a seat.

entries[].forecourt.seatTerrace.tread.basis: [estimated]. The terrace's depth per tier is not measurable in the frame; 0.70 m, a seat plus a step.

entries[].forecourt.seatTerrace.setback.basis: [estimated]. How far the first tier stands off the building line; 1.00 m. Chosen so the outermost tier reaches 1.00 + 3 x 0.70 = 3.10 m, inside the declared 3.6 m envelope pad.

entries[].forecourt.seatTerrace.overrun.basis: [estimated]. How far the terrace runs past the doors each side; 3.00 m.

entries[].forecourt.planter.length.basis: [estimated]. A raised planter flanking the entry; 2.40 m long.

entries[].forecourt.planter.depth.basis: [estimated]. The planter's depth across the walk is not measurable in the frame - it is seen end-on. 1.20 m, half its 2.40 m length, which keeps its outer edge at 2.20 m, inboard of the seat terrace's 3.10 m.

entries[].forecourt.planter.height.basis: 0.60 m: a raised planter wall is not a seat, so it stands one 17 in seat height plus a 6 in (0.152 m) rim = 0.584 m; ships at 0.60 m.

entries[].forecourt.planter.setback.basis: [estimated]; 1.60 m off the building line, so the planter's outer edge sits at 2.20 m, inboard of the terrace's 3.10 m.

entries[].forecourt.planter.gap.basis: 0.30 m of clear ground between the terrace's outer end and the planter's inner end. It exists because round one overlapped them by 0.30 x 0.30 x 0.58 m and 0.31 x 0.30 x 0.50 m; the test now re-derives the separation from these figures.

wing.roof.trimWidth.basis: [estimated]. The pale edge trim running the wing roof's whole perimeter is one to two pixels deep in every frame. An 18 in (0.4572 m) edge band.

wing.roof.trimThickness.basis: A 4 in upstand: 4 x 0.0254 = 0.1016 m, the standard depth of a roof edge trim. The trim is one to two pixels deep in both aerials.

wing.festoon.span.basis: The standard commercial festoon span between suspension points: 20 x 0.3048 = 6.096 m. It is what breaks the run so no lamp can hang lower than one span's sag - round one sagged a whole 34.9 m ring segment as one span.

wing.festoon.lampPitch.basis: The standard commercial festoon lamp spacing: 5 x 0.3048 = 1.524 m, which is four lamps to a 20 ft span.
wing.festoon.lampPitch.patternRef: a standard 5 ft festoon lamp spacing

wing.festoon.sagFraction.basis: [estimated]. The sag reads shallow in phf26 but is not measurable against a calibrated span. 1.2% of ONE 6.096 m span = 0.073 m - NOT 6% of a 34.9 m ring segment, which is what round one did and which sagged that run 2.09 m and left its lowest lamp at 1.32 m. The figure is bounded by the 2.032 m clear headroom, which is the only hard constraint on it.

wing.festoon.drop.basis: [estimated]. How far the suspension points hang below the canopy soffit: 0.05 m, i.e. the run is strung taut against it. The soffit itself only clears 3.0455 - 0.152 - 0.04 = 2.853 m over the podium datum, the drawn ground rises above that datum along this frontage, and drop + sag together have to leave the 2.032 m code headroom the test enforces lamp by lamp. There is no room for a swag, so there is no swag.

wing.festoon.lampRadius.basis: An S14 festoon lamp is 14/8 in = 1.75 in across, so 0.0635 m radius - the product this run is.

wing.festoon.cordThickness.basis: A standard 1/2 in festoon cord: 0.5 x 0.0254 = 0.0127 m. At the range phf26 shoots the run from, the cord is a single pixel, so this is the product.

brow.fasciaThickness.basis: The fascia plate's own thickness, a 4 in formed metal edge: 4 x 0.0254 = 0.1016 m. Round one carried a bare 0.12 literal inside the module, beyond every provenance gate.

podium.canopy.fasciaThickness.basis: The canopy's edge plate at 2 in: 2 x 0.0254 = 0.0508 m - half the brow's 4 in, because it is roughly half the span.

balconies.soffitLight.diameter.basis: A 6 in recessed soffit downlight: 6 x 0.0254 = 0.152 m, one under each slab - the bright point source phf26 shows. Round one carried a bare 0.18 literal inside the module.

balconies.soffitLight.depth.basis: The trim depth of the same 6 in recessed fitting, 2 in: 2 x 0.0254 = 0.0508 m. phf26 reads the lamp as a bright point and resolves no fitting.

signage.letterWidthRatio.basis: 0.72: the standard cap-width to cap-height ratio for a grotesque capital, which is what the applied letters are. Letter width = 0.305 x 0.72 = 0.220 m.

signage.relief.basis: 3/4 in (0.019 m), the standard return depth of a flat-cut applied metal letter.
signage.relief.patternRef: a standard 3/4 in flat-cut letter return

signage.wallLightDiameter.basis: A 6 in round surface-mounted wall light: 6 x 0.0254 = 0.152 m, which is the size the two fittings read above the wordmark.
signage.wallLightDiameter.patternRef: a standard 6 in round wall light

signage.wallLightDepth.basis: The same fitting's projection off the brick, 3 in: 3 x 0.0254 = 0.0762 m.

wing.festoon.minClear.basis: The minimum clear headroom any part of the run may leave above the DRAWN ground under it: 80 x 0.0254 = 2.032 m, the protruding-object headroom of ADA 307.4 / CBC 11B-307.2, which is the code that governs a lamp hanging over a walking route. It is not a shape figure - it is the gate the test enforces lamp by lamp - and it exists because round one hung the lowest lamp of a 34.9 m run at 1.32 m, which is chest height. The canopy soffit itself only clears 2.853 m over the podium datum, so the drop and the sag are both solved backwards from this figure.
wing.festoon.minClear.patternRef: ADA 307.4 / CBC 11B-307.2 - 80 in clear headroom below a protruding object

survivance.dimensionRule: THE KEELING BAR. Every load-bearing number this section builds from carries an entry here, keyed by its own path, with a tier and the arithmetic. `measured` means read against a calibrated span in a named, dated frame. `derived` means arithmetic from a sourced module, a published product module or a code minimum, shown in full. `estimated` is the third invented tier of the ultra standard: labelled [estimated], carrying the patternRef it extends, and replaced the day a source turns up. A number with no entry is a defect and the test fails on it; the test walks the built subtrees and demands coverage rather than trusting a list, so a new figure cannot be added without a provenance entry.

signage.note: One signage family for the whole building: the SURVIVANCE wordmark, the 9145 street numbers and the two round wall lights above the wordmark. These figures were literals inside the module in round one - 0.62, 0.03, 0.14, 0.06 - which put them beyond every provenance gate. Colours are DATA and so are these.
signage.source: Conference Center flyer p.2 (2025-03); EYRC phf26 (2024-25)

pulsefitness.label: Pulse outdoor fitness zone — the open-air calisthenics / functional-training rig with two heavy bags, on the Pulse (Eighth College) north colonnade terrace
pulsefitness.epoch: 2024-25 published photography. SWA Group image -16 (Learning-16) is the ONLY frame in the EYRC (phf01-49) or SWA (-1..-23) sets that resolves this object; UCSD's own 2024-25 programme text names it; the 2020 TDLLN planning update is the oldest rung and describes intent, not the built thing. The 2014 LiDAR is BLIND here — campus-lidar.json massHeights has no entry for any Eighth mass — and the Apple 3D-mesh orthos in .cache/eighth-furniture reconstruct the court and the Pulse slab but resolve no part of a thin steel frame, so NO height and NO position in this section comes from LiDAR, from campus-3d OSM h, or from imagery.
pulsefitness.note: ONE OBJECT, ONE OWNER, AND IT IS BIGGER AND FURTHER EAST THAN EITHER PREDECESSOR THOUGHT. This rig shipped twice — eighthcourtyards.calisthenics (5.0 x 2.0 m plan, top bar 2.4, at -169.5, 534.5) and eighthsiteworks rig-1 (4.0 x 2.0, top bar 2.4, at -174.0, 537.0) — two sizes 4.9 m apart, both [estimated], neither with a calibration object on it and nothing arbitrating the pair. Both are superseded here by a camera resection of swa-16 that is validated against three independent facade measurements and against research-pulse's own 71.5 px/m at the far hoop. The rig is 7.72 m long overall, its frame stands 2.89 m, it carries TWO black heavy bags on cantilever arms, and it stands against Pulse's surveyed north face, not out on the lawn. The photogrammetry lands its whole footprint inside surveyed walkway-3238 — the only paved polygon in that 17.6 m strip — in the only part of that polygon which is NOT under Pulse's massing ring. That was not an input to the solve; it is a check that passed.
pulsefitness.confidence: Geometry: high for length, bay pitch and every height (all from one validated camera model, cross-checked three ways). Medium for the rig's plan DEPTH (1.40 m — the two-row post fit prefers it but 0.6-1.6 m all fit within 2.4 px rms). Medium for world POSITION: x and z are photogrammetric, not surveyed, and carry the uncertainty stated in `positionCaveat`. Low-to-absent for product identity, footing detail, safety surfacing and the hanger webbing colour — all four are in `absent`.
pulsefitness.positionCaveat: [estimated] POSITION, WITH ITS DERIVATION AND ITS ERROR BAR — not a guess and not a rule-of-thumb. No photograph in the 2024-25 set is registered to the ArcGIS survey, so this object has no surveyed world coordinate. What it has instead is a full camera resection of swa-16 (see `camera`), which converts image pixels into world metres on a declared plane. The rig is placed on the plane of Pulse's surveyed north face because the single-view SCALE says so: the rig images at 38.5-43.7 px/m and the facade directly above it at 40 +/- 2 px/m, i.e. the same distance. Putting the rig 10 m nearer the court instead (z = 540) would make it image at 61 px/m, which would make the heavy bags 0.18 m across and the pull-up bar 1.49 m off its own paving — both impossible. So the rig IS in the wall plane. Residual uncertainty: +/- 1.6 m in z (4% scale error over a 39 m camera distance) and, because dx/dz along the sight line is cot(39.18 deg) = 1.225, +/- 2.0 m in x from the same source, plus +/- 1.5 m in x from the resection itself. Quote it as x = -154.4 +/- 2.5 m, z = 549.5 +/- 1.6 m. What would close it: a frame with a surveyed feature and the rig both in it, or the .cache/eighth-furniture ref2 ground-plane registration extended to an oblique that reaches the colonnade terrace.
sources: https://swacdn.s3.amazonaws.com/UCSD_UC-San-Diego_Theater-District_Living-Learning-16.webp — SWA Group / Lawrence Anderson, 2024-25. THE frame, and the only one. A sunlit eye-level photograph from just off the court's north-west corner looking east-south-east at Pulse's north elevation. It resolves: the whole rig in elevation, both top chords, the perforated upper chord, the pull-up bar with a person hanging from it, the lower orange rails, both cantilever bag arms, BOTH HEAVY BAGS with their hangers, the two basketball standards that calibrate the camera, and the ground-storey masonry and window rhythm that validate it.

https://eighth.ucsd.edu/residential-life/living-at-eighth.html — UC San Diego Eighth College, retrieved 2026-08-19. Programme text: the Pulse fitness centre is on L1 with 'peletons, lifting weight section, punching bags and other exercise equipment'; the college separately advertises an 'open-air calisthenics area' and 'a relaxing grassy space'. This NAMES the outdoor thing and confirms it is a calisthenics facility. It does NOT say the bags are outdoor — swa-16 does.

https://plandesignbuild.ucsd.edu/_files/planning/TDLLNAugust2020Update.pdf and the CEQA addendum text at scratchpad/docs/add5.txt lines 2173-2182 / 11393-11395 — UCSD Capital Planning, August 2020. 'The Wellness Corridor ... would include space for informal and programmed activities such as basketball, volleyball, and badminton, and fitness equipment integrated along the periphery of the great lawn. Situated just north of the fitness center located in Building 1'. Planning INTENT, 2020, and the oldest epoch here. It is the reason the two predecessors put the rig out on the lawn. The 2024-25 photography overrules it: the built rig is at the building, and the lawn periphery in phf22 carries bike racks and a bike repair stand, not fitness stations.

https://eyrc.com/hubfs/UCSD_TDLLN-phf22_LA-ppt.jpg — EYRC / Lawrence Anderson, 2024-25. A NEGATIVE, and a correction: round one recorded the rig as 'legible in phf22'. It is not. phf22 shows the Sun Lawn's paved periphery with staple bike hoops and a vertical-post BIKE REPAIR STAND (a T-clamp arm on a post, tool arms below) — not fitness equipment. The rig does not appear in phf22 at all.

scratchpad/docs/addendum5.pdf — UC Regents / UC San Diego, TDLLN CEQA Addendum, 2021 (3,299 pp; cached 2026-08-18) — and scratchpad/pulse/Pulse-Layouts.pdf, UC San Diego Eighth College, 2024. Both searched and EXHAUSTED for a product-level schedule. Zero hits for calisthenic/monkey/pull-up/heavy bag/punching/boxing/plyo/dip bar/site furnishing/CSI 11 66 00/11 68 00; the only 'fitness equipment' hit is the Wellness Corridor prose above. Neither document is a construction specification and neither carries a landscape-equipment or site-furnishing schedule.

camera.note: A FULL CAMERA RESECTION OF swa-16, derived in-session from surveyed control, then validated. Every metre in this section comes out of it. Frame is the 1920 x 1080 SWA publication crop.
camera.axisConvention: axisBearingDeg is the optical axis measured from the +x world axis toward +z. For an image point (u, v) assumed to lie on the plane z = Z: beta = atan((u - u0) / f); theta = axis + beta; t = (Z - 520.0) / sin(theta); x = -190.9 + t*cos(theta); s = f / t px per metre; Y = 2.24 - (v - v0)/s, where Y is height above the COURT surface (the surveyed court plane, taken as Y = 0).

derivation.step1: The two basketball backboards are the same object at two known separations. Their VERTICAL extents (unaffected by the boards' yaw) read 251 px near and 70 px far, so the distance ratio is 251/70 = 3.586. Board centres sit 1.2 m inside each surveyed baseline, i.e. at x = -184.7 and x = -164.4 on z = 525.2, 20.3 m apart.
derivation.step2: Image u of the two board centres: 1273.5 and 285. With f = s_near * d_near and the triangle 20.3^2 = d^2 + (3.347d)^2 - 2*3.347*d^2*cos(gamma), gamma = atan(313.5/f) + atan(675/f), the only consistent solution is d_near = 8.07 m, f = 1929 px.
derivation.step3: Intersecting the two distance circles gives the camera at (-190.9, 520.0) — just off the court's north-west corner, 5.0 m west of the west baseline and 5.2 m north of the centre line. The axis bearing follows from either ray: 40.0 deg - atan(313.5/1929) = 30.77 deg from +x.
derivation.step4: Height and principal v: the far rim is 3.048 m above the court (regulation, and research-pulse's own calibration) and images at v = 547; the surveyed court south-east corner (-163.2, 532.9) is at Y = 0 and images at v = 746. Two equations give eye height 2.24 m and v0 = 604.7 (the frame is a crop, so v0 is not 540).
derivation.validation1: The model predicts 73.9 px/m at the far hoop. research-pulse derived 71.5 px/m there independently, from the rim height alone. 3% apart.
derivation.validation2: Pulse's storey pitch is the sourced 3.048 m. Measured off window heads on three separate window columns: 130 px at u=1410 (42.7 px/m), 137 px at u=1620 (45.0), 155 px at u=1840 (50.9). The model, given only the surveyed face z = 550.5, predicts 43.9, 48.2 and 52.0. Errors 3%, 7%, 2% — over a range where the scale changes by 19%, so the model is reproducing the perspective, not a constant.
derivation.validation3: Run backwards, the model puts the rig's whole footprint inside surveyed walkway-3238 (arcgis.ground#3238, x -163.5..-148.1, z 548.1..554.8), which is the only paved surveyed polygon anywhere in the 17.6 m strip between the court's south edge and Pulse's north face, and specifically in the northern sliver of it that is NOT inside Pulse's massing ring. Nothing about walkway-3238 was an input.

measured.note: Rings copied VERBATIM. The court and walkway come out of docs/data/campus-eighth.json ground (each registered to a docs/data/campus-arcgis.json ground[] polygon); the Pulse north face is the closing segment of docs/data/campus-arcgis.json massing[463] at /10 (ArcGIS rings are DECIMETRES). tests/campus-photo-pulsefitness.test.mjs re-reads both files and fails on one changed number. The survey beats the photograph on ground extents, always.

basketball-court.role: camera control — its four corners and the two standards on its long axis are what the resection solves against

walkway-3238.role: the paving the rig stands on, and the reason its ground datum is the `pad` rung

pulse-north-face.role: the plane the rig stands against, and the z the resection is solved on

planting-bed-1760.role: clearance check only — the lead named it; the rig clears it by 19.4 m in x and 9.9 m in z, so it never bit

reads.note: The raw image readings, in swa-16 pixels, that every derived metre below is computed from. They are recorded so the arithmetic can be re-run. `Yc` is height above the COURT plane straight out of the camera model; the rig's own datum is 0.90 m above that (see derivations.terraceRise), so rig heights are Yc - 0.90.

derivations.overallLength: [measured] The rig's two extreme points image at u = 1143 and u = 1347. On the rig plane z = 549.5 the camera model puts them at x = -150.44 and x = -158.16. Overall length 7.72 m.
derivations.bagArmProjection: [measured] The left bag's hanger drops at u = 1148 and the end upright of that row images at u = 1176, a 28 px gap at 38.6 px/m = 0.73 m. Both ends carry the same arm, so the frame proper is 7.72 - 2 x 0.73 = 6.26 m.
derivations.bayPitch: [measured] Seven dark vertical minima survive in the band v = 555..605 (see reads.uprightMinimaU). Fitting a two-row post grid through the camera model — free parameters the first post's x, the bay pitch, the row spacing and the plane z — the bay pitch converges on 1.04-1.05 m for EVERY row spacing tried (rms 1.98-2.83 px, against +/- 2 px reading error), and degrades to 5-12 px rms outside 0.9-1.35 m. A one-row model cannot get below 5.2 px rms at any pitch. Taken as 6.26 / 6 = 1.0433 m, which closes the frame length exactly on 6 bays and 7 uprights per row.
derivations.planDepth: [estimated] The same fit prefers a row spacing of 1.40 m (rms 1.98 px) over 1.20 (2.81), 1.60 (2.22), 0.60 (2.31) and 1.80 (3.08). The preference is real but shallow, so 1.40 m ships labelled [estimated] with its competitors recorded. What is MEASURED and not estimated is that the rig has TWO rows at all: two parallel orange top chords are resolved 9 px apart in v at u = 1245, and a single-row post model cannot fit the upright minima.
derivations.terraceRise: [sourced] The rig's paving is Pulse's L1 colonnade terrace. research-pulse section 5 photographs the stair up to it in this same frame as 'a broad flight of ~6 risers'; at the 0.15 m riser that section assumes, the terrace is 0.90 m above the court plane. Every rig height below is the camera model's height above the court MINUS 0.90. Cross-check that this is the right datum and not 1.64 m: at 1.64 the pull-up bar would stand 1.53 m off its own paving, and the woman photographed hanging from it with her feet clear would not fit.
derivations.frameHeight: [measured] Top chord top edge v = 541 at u = 1245, s = 41.2 px/m: Yc = 2.24 - (541 - 604.7)/41.2 = 3.79 m above the court; 3.79 - 0.90 = 2.89 m.
derivations.secondChord: [measured] Underside v = 556: Yc = 3.42, so 2.52 m above the paving. With the chord at 0.076 m the axis is 2.52 + 0.038 = 2.558 m.
derivations.pullUpBar: [measured] v = 567 at u = 1215, s = 40.4: Yc = 3.17, so 2.27 m above the paving. Spans u 1190-1240 = x -152.6..-154.5, one and a bit bays.
derivations.lowerRail: [measured] Two orange horizontals at v = 601 (u 1228-1274) and v = 600 (u 1310-1355) give Yc = 2.33 and 2.35, so 1.43 and 1.45 m above the paving. Taken as one rail height, 1.44 m.
derivations.bagArmTip: [measured] The left arm's hanger point images at v = 551, u = 1148, s = 38.5: Yc = 3.635, so 2.74 m above the paving — 0.15 m below the frame top, which is the arm's drop.
derivations.bag: [measured] Bag L: top v = 583, bottom v = 620 at s = 38.7 -> 0.96 m long; width 11 px -> 0.474 m. Bag R: top v = 576, bottom v = 618 at s = 42.3 -> 0.99 m long; width 14 px -> 0.495 m. Shipped at the means, 0.98 m long and 0.48 m diameter, with +/- 0.07 m on the diameter because 11-14 px is 3-4 px from the 25 mm/px resolution floor. Bag tops sit at Yc 2.80 and 2.92 -> 1.90 and 2.02 above the paving; shipped at 1.94, so the bottoms hang 0.96 m clear.
derivations.hangerLength: [measured] Arm tip 2.74 minus bag top 1.94 = 0.80 m of webbing, which is the 30 px run visible between them at 38.5 px/m.
derivations.uprightSection: [measured] The dark verticals read 4 px wide at s = 40.7 px/m = 0.098 m. Shipped at 0.10 m square, which is 2.5x the frame's 25 mm/px resolution floor and therefore a real measurement rather than a rounding.
derivations.chordSection: [measured, at the resolution floor] The orange chords read 3 px at the same scale = 0.074 m. Shipped at 0.076 m with +/- 0.025 m declared — this is ONE pixel from the floor and must not be quoted as precise.
derivations.gripBarSection: [estimated] A pull-up or monkey bar is 0.03-0.05 m and swa-16 cannot resolve it: one pixel is 25 mm. Rather than invent a number, this extends the SAME SITE's documented pipe: eighthsiteworks MEASURED Eighth's handrail and guard pickets at 0.042 m and 0.048 m round tube (1.5 in nominal pipe) by autocorrelation off swa-5, and 0.042 m is the gripping-surface member of that family. Replace it the day a frame resolves the bar.
derivations.monkeyBridge: [measured extent, estimated rungs] The upper chord carries a repeating dark pattern from u = 1164 to u = 1248 — on the rig plane, x = -151.0 to -154.0, i.e. 3.0 m, which is three bays. The pattern's own pitch reads 4.4 px = 0.11 m, which is 4 px from the resolution floor and is a hole pattern or an aliasing artefact, NOT a rung pitch (monkey rungs are 0.30-0.38 m and would read 12-15 px, and no 12-15 px spacing exists in the run). So the BRIDGE EXTENT is measured at 3 bays and the RUNG PITCH is [estimated] at 3.13 / 9 = 0.348 m, inside the 0.30-0.38 m band the object type sets. The hole pattern itself is in `absent`.
derivations.position: [estimated] See positionCaveat. x centre = (-150.44 + -158.16)/2 = -154.30 on the trial plane z = 549.6, and -154.42 once the plane settles (below) — a 0.12 m shift, five per cent of the smallest error bar. The DEPTH is set by the one rule that cannot make the rig intersect the building, applied at the WORST point rather than at the centre. Two things make the centre the wrong place to apply it. First, the rig's rearmost geometry is the FOOTING PLATE, 0.22 m deep against a 0.10 m post, so setting the post's own face on the wall pushes 0.06 m of plate through it. Second, the surveyed north face is NOT parallel to the rig: it runs from z 550.3 at x = -149 to z 550.7 at x = -197.7, a 0.47 degree splay, so the face is 0.05 m NEARER at the rig's east end than at its centre. The binding point is therefore the easternmost plate edge, x = -151.06, where z_face = 550.3 + 0.4 x (151.06 - 149)/48.7 = 550.317. Far row axis = 550.317 - 0.22/2 = 550.20, near row = 550.20 - 1.40 = 548.80, plan centre = 549.50. Re-running the x solve on 549.50 returns -154.42, which is the value shipped. The rig then stands 0.007 m clear of the face at its closest point and 0.04 m clear at its far end — touching, and through nothing.

colorSources.safetyOrange: [measured] swa-16, 2024-25. Three separate SUNLIT members, masked on hue (R > 140, R > 1.7B, G < 0.75R) and averaged over the 30-85th luminance percentile: the top chord at (1160-1265, 543-556) reads #d17541 over 274 px, the right-hand rails at (1265-1350, 548-566) read #dd844d over 196 px, the lower bar at (1225-1300, 594-606) reads #d98b46 over 43 px. Shipped at their mean. DECLARED ILLUMINANT: swa-16 is a low warm late-day sun, so this hex is warmer than the powder coat would read at D65 — research-pulse section 7 asks that this be said rather than silently corrected, and no correction is applied here. NOTE FOR THE MERGE: eighthcourtyards derived a safetyOrange of #d4622a for this same rig and eighthsiteworks adopted it; that read is 0.03 apart in hue from this one and was taken without a camera. Neither is wrong enough to overturn the other, and this section does not edit theirs.
colorSources.frameCharcoal: [measured, SHADED — declared conflict] swa-16. The uprights are dark and every one of them presents a shaded face to this camera; there is no sunlit read of an upright anywhere in the set. Two posts sampled below L=110: (1174-1184, 556-606) reads #674f3a over 193 px and (1256-1266, 556-606) reads #4f443a over 244 px. Shipped at their mean. This violates the discipline eighthsiteworks set in its CONFLICT C1 ('no colour ships raw out of shadow') and it is recorded rather than worked around: the true finish is very likely a more neutral, darker charcoal, and a sunlit read is in `absent`.
colorSources.bagBlack: [measured, SHADED] swa-16. Bag L at (1144-1160, 586-616) reads #444030 over 339 px below L=110; bag R at (1282-1300, 580-616) reads #424135 over 445 px below L=120. Shipped at their mean. Same shadow caveat as the frame; a black vinyl bag in warm bounce light is expected to read exactly like this.
colorSources.hangerWebbing: [estimated] NOT MEASURED, and the reason is recorded. The hanger is a 1-2 px strap in front of a pale sunlit wall; a bright-percentile sample of it returns #fdf4d9, which is the wall, not the webbing. What swa-16 does establish is that the hanger reads LIGHTER than its background is dark and lighter than every steel member on the rig, i.e. it is pale webbing and not a black chain. The hex shipped is a neutral off-white consistent with that and labelled [estimated]; a clean read is in `absent`.
colorSources.footingPlate: [estimated] The base plates are not visible in any frame (planting occludes the rig below 1.9 m above the court). They take the same finish as the frame they belong to — the standard extension inside this section's own sourced pattern — and the footing detail itself is in `absent`.

groundDatum.derivation: [derived] The rig's whole footprint (x -158.28..-150.56, z 548.80..550.20) lies inside surveyed walkway-3238, which is a campus-eighth.json `ground` feature, and campus-eighth.js draws ALL of its ground features as a lifted decal on campus-overlay.js's `pad` rung (its surfaceMeshes() opens `const rung = "pad"`), which is +0.09 m above the terrain triangle. Anything this module seated on the raw surfaceAt would stand 0.09 m BELOW the paving a viewer can see. Same argument, same rung and same number as eighthsiteworks.groundDatum, because it is the same paving. The lift is read from campus-overlay.js at build time, never from this number — the number is here so the test can check the two agree.

chords.note: axis height; the chord's top edge is the measured 2.89 m frame height
axis height; the measured underside is 2.52 m

bags.note: THE ANSWER TO 'IS THERE AN OUTDOOR PUNCHING BAG' IS YES, AND IT IS TWO. Round one concluded the bags were indoor-only on the strength of UCSD's programme text ('fitness centre on L1 ... punching bags'), which is true and is about the L1 gym. swa-16 shows two black cylindrical heavy bags hanging on webbing from cantilever arms at the rig's two ends, in the open air, roughly 8 m from that gym's storefront. They are visible at 6x in the published frame and both survive the camera model as bags of a real, ordinary size.

clips.why: Pulse Tower's surveyed massing ring (arcgis.massing[463]). The rig stands against its north face and NOTHING this module builds may cross it — the far row is set so the rig's rearmost geometry lands on the face and the test re-checks every built vertex against the surveyed line rather than against this rectangle.

The surveyed basketball court. swa-16 is a clean sunlit photograph of the whole playing surface with nothing standing on it. FORWARD GUARD, not a live cut: the rig is 16 m away in z and nothing this module builds falls inside, so it removes nothing today. It is here so that a future correction to the rig's [estimated] position cannot silently walk it onto the court.

supersedes: eighthcourtyards.calisthenics — 'plan 5.0 x 2.0 m, topBar 2.4, tube 0.09, rungs 7, centre (-169.5, 534.5)', [estimated]. Superseded in full. swa-16 with a validated camera puts the object at 7.72 x 1.40 m plan, frame top 2.89 m, centred (-154.4, 549.5). The predecessor had no calibration object on the rig and no camera; its 2.4 m top bar is within 0.13 m of the pull-up bar this section measures at 2.27 m, which is probably what it was looking at, but its overall size and its position are both wrong. eighthsiteworks rig-1 — 'plan 4.0 x 2.0, topBar 2.4, uprights 6, barDiameter 0.045, postDiameter 0.09, at (-174.0, 537.0)', [estimated], with its own note 'no calibration object on it'. The claim (round one, scratchpad/eighth-recon.md and research-eighthCourtyards.md) that the rig is 'legible in phf22'. It is not in phf22 at all. The object at the Sun Lawn's paved edge in that frame is a public BIKE REPAIR STAND with staple hoops beside it, which belongs to eighthsiteworks' bike kit.

The claim (research-eighthCourtyards section 5.2) that the rig is 'set on a rubber/paver pad'. Nothing visible in swa-16 supports it — planting occludes the rig below about 1.9 m above the court plane — so it is withdrawn rather than carried forward, and the question moves to `absent`.
absent: AN OUTDOOR BOXING BAG IS *NOT* ABSENT — see `bags`. This entry exists so the next agent does not re-open the question: two heavy bags are resolved in swa-16 and are built. What IS absent about them is the make, the fill weight and the swivel/mount hardware at the arm tip, none of which any source gives.

PRODUCT IDENTITY for the rig. Exhausted: the 3,299-page CEQA addendum (scratchpad/docs/addendum5.pdf) and Pulse-Layouts.pdf, both searched for calisthenic / monkey / pull-up / heavy bag / punching / boxing / plyo / dip bar / site furnishing and the CSI 11 66 00 and 11 68 00 sections — zero hits and neither is a construction specification; the HKS, EYRC, SWA, Safdie Rabines, Walter P Moore and Kitchell project pages, none of which carries an equipment schedule; UCSD Recreation and eighth.ucsd.edu, which name the 'open-air calisthenics area' but describe no product. Orange-and-charcoal two-row rigs with monkey-bar bridges and hung bags are made by several manufacturers and the geometry here is complete enough to model without one. No brand is invented.

A SUNLIT READ OF THE FRAME'S DARK MEMBERS. Every upright presents a shaded face to swa-16's camera and there is no second frame. The charcoal shipped is therefore a shadow read, flagged as such in colorSources, against a project rule that normally forbids it. Closeable by any frame of this elevation taken with the sun on the north face at a different hour.
THE HANGER WEBBING'S COLOUR. A 1-2 px strap against a pale sunlit wall; every sample returns the wall. Shipped [estimated] as pale webbing, which is what the frame does establish.

THE FOOTING DETAIL AND THE SAFETY SURFACING. Planting occludes the rig below about 1.9 m above the court plane in the only frame there is, so the base plates, anchors, any concrete pad and any rubber/poured safety surface under the rig are all unresolved. A base plate is built because nothing may hover and the posts must land on the paving; its size is [estimated] and it is the only part of the rig that is. Whether a rubber pad exists at all is unknown and none is built — see the fourth `supersedes` entry, which withdraws round one's assertion that there is one.

THE UPPER CHORD'S PERFORATION. The chord carries a repeating dark pattern at a 4.4 px pitch, four pixels from swa-16's 25 mm/px resolution floor. It is very likely an adjustment-hole pattern (0.11 m by the model) but it cannot be separated from JPEG aliasing at this scale, so no holes are modelled and the chord ships plain.

THE MONKEY-BAR RUNG PITCH. The bridge's EXTENT is measured at three bays; the rungs themselves are below resolution. Nine rungs at 0.348 m ship [estimated], inside the 0.30-0.38 m band the object type sets.

THE RIG'S PLAN DEPTH, to better than the shallow preference recorded in derivations.planDepth. That the rig has two rows is measured; that they are 1.40 m apart rather than 1.2 or 1.6 is a best fit, not a measurement.

A WORLD-COORDINATE SURVEY OF THE RIG. See positionCaveat: x and z are photogrammetric with +/- 2.5 m and +/- 1.6 m. Closeable by extending .cache/eighth-furniture's proven ref2 ground-plane registration to an oblique frame that reaches the colonnade terrace, or by any frame containing both the rig and a surveyed feature.

THE 2020 PLAN'S LAWN-PERIPHERY FITNESS EQUIPMENT. The CEQA addendum promises 'fitness equipment integrated along the periphery of the great lawn'. The 2024-25 photography of exactly that periphery (phf22) shows staple bike hoops and a bike repair stand and NO fitness station. Either it was value-engineered out or it postdates the photography. Nothing is built from the 2020 promise: better absent than wrong.

ROOFTOP-DECK FITNESS EQUIPMENT. Pulse's rooftop deck is built (campus-photo-pulse.js owns it) and was still closed in the UCSD Guardian's 2024-09-30 report. No source shows any equipment on it and none is built here.

THE STAIR AND THE PLANTING between the court and this terrace. Both are visible in swa-16 and neither is this section's — the stair is a flight eighthsiteworks explicitly does not rail, and the planting belongs to eighthcourtyards. Named so the next agent does not read their absence here as a claim that they do not exist.
